PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Experience managing large-scale gas turbine facilities (100 MW+), preferably with high-availability critical power applications (data centers, industrial, or similar)

• Proven track record of achieving and sustaining high plant availability, reliability, and low forced outage rates

• Hands-on experience with plant construction, commissioning, start-up, and concurrent operations/expansion of gas turbine facilities

• Deep knowledge of gas turbine technology (aeroderivative and/or heavy-duty frames), performance optimization, emissions controls (SCR, etc.), and balance of plant systems

• Experience with high-voltage electrical systems, generators, switchgear, protection, and data center or industrial interconnection

• Strong understanding of environmental permitting, air quality compliance, and regulatory reporting for combustion turbines

• Experience in fast-paced, high-growth environments requiring simultaneous operations and major construction

• Demonstrated ability to manage budgets, fuel costs, contractors, and complex stakeholder relationships

• Excellent oral and written communication, leadership, and interpersonal skills

• Unfazed by major, abrupt changes in strategic direction or aggressive timelines

• Ability to work in a demanding, autonomously driven, start-up atmosphere

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Ability to support and supervise plant operations and construction outside of normal business hours, including nights, weekends, and on-call response

• Must be based at the Memphis/Southaven site

• Willingness to work extended hours as needed to support plant reliability and construction milestones

• General physical fitness required; ability to walk the plant site, access equipment, and work in industrial/outdoor environments (heat, noise, etc.)

• Order processing: Execute end-to-end processing of customer orders utilising AI-supported entry tools and enterprise ERP systems. Validate automated extractions, correct pricing or item discrepancies, resolve EDI transaction holds, and manage allocations for bottlenecked materials.
• Dual Logistics & Vendor Coordination: Align closely with internal warehouse teams and external providers regarding dispatch cut-offs, picking schedules, and delivery tracking. Track outbound and return shipments, manage carrier updates, and safeguard cold-chain integrity across all transit legs.
• Variance Resolution & Returns Management: Investigate shipment variances against carrier Proof of Delivery (POD) logs and warehouse records. Oversee the complete customer returns cycle. Log complaints in CRM, document operational notes in SAP ERP, and maintain audit-ready records.
• Deliver exceptional customer support: Drive high customer satisfaction by maintaining prompt call-queue response times and clear email resolution.

Key Collaborators

You will collaborate across a diverse global network:

• Internal: Customer Success, Access & Innovation, Strategy & Solutions, Service & Support, Finance & Operations, IT, Quality & Regulatory, and Legal.
• External: Pathology Laboratories, Hospitals, Wholesalers, Regional APAC/Global teams, and Supply Chain Providers.

Who You Are

• Experienced: 3+ years of customer service, returns, or order management experience preferably within medical distribution, pharmaceuticals, or healthcare logistics.
• Logistics Tech-Savvy: Proven experience with SAP Or similar ERP software , and EDI exception resolution (desired). Knowledge of Google Suite tools or similar (essential)
• Compliance Minded: Strong understanding of Good Distribution Practice (GDP) requirements and temperature-controlled cold-chain logistics.
• Agile Problem Solver: Meticulous attention to detail, and a proactive, customer-first approach under dynamic timelines.
• Effective interpersonal skills- excellent communication skills in both written and spoken, maturity and confidence in handling customer queries and complaints.

This role is only open to candidates that have full eligibility to live and work in Australia.

We do not accept any unsolicited resumes or enquiries from recruitment agencies. Roche has a dedicated in-house Talent Acquisition team.

What we offer

Roche offers rewarding growth opportunities, a competitive remuneration package and a collaborative culture where people are united in purpose and will stretch you to be brave, speak up and think differently. Feel empowered to deliver meaningful outcomes, supported by accessible and inspiring leaders.

Roche encourages a high-performance culture where you are empowered and trusted to make decisions. We strive for excellence and extraordinary results and take a genuine interest in our people and their well-being, and our patients.

Take pride in knowing you can make a difference to millions of patients worldwide in developing diagnostics and treatments for oncology, neuroscience, inflammation, immunology, ophthalmology, rare diseases, respiratory disease and diabetes.

We are committed to providing an inclusive, safe, secure and healthy workplace, and to minimise any such impacts to our employees, customers and the community. We welcome applications from all people and encourage you to advise of any individual circumstances that may require consideration.

Who we are

A healthier future drives us to innovate. Together, more than 100’000 employees across the globe are dedicated to advance science, ensuring everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Our efforts result in more than 26 million people treated with our medicines and over 30 billion tests conducted using our Diagnostics products. We empower each other to explore new possibilities, foster creativity, and keep our ambitions high, so we can deliver life-changing healthcare solutions that make a global impact.

Let’s build a healthier future, together.

Roche is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

jobs.title: Manager, Mid Market (Central)
jobs.description:
Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

Samsara is seeking Sales Managers to join our passionate, high energy, and fast moving sales team. You’ll lead and support our Account Executives II focusing on mid-sized Private Sector organizations. You will have a consistent track record of ability to hire, develop, and lead an inclusive, engaged, and high performing team.

This is a remote position open to candidates living in the US Central Time Zone. Relocation assistance will not be provided for this position.

You should apply if:

• You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.

• You have innate curiosity in how businesses work: One day you’ll meet with someone in waste management and the next you may be learning about the inner workings of a food distribution center. Our top sales team members seek to learn the ins and outs of the businesses they support in order to make a larger impact.

• You build genuine relationships with your customers: The industries we serve have relied on pen-and-paper solutions for years and haven’t been met with the type of technology we offer. Our customers value earned trust and human relationships built over time.

• You want to be with the best: Samsara’s high-performance culture means you’ll be surrounded by the best and challenged to go farther than you have before.

• You are a team player: At Samsara, sales is a team sport. We help each other out by sharing best practices and focus on winning as a team.

Click here to learn about what we value at Samsara.

In this role, you will:

• Coach a team of ~8 account executives on sales strategy, pipeline reviews and achieve quarterly targets

• Hire new account executives and provide both onboarding and ongoing coaching to ensure their growth and success

• Work cross-functionally to strategically solve problems and project manage

• Create content for ongoing training and development

• Support account executives through professional development plans

• Provide clear and tactical feedback to account executives

• Further culture within the team and commercial organization with high emotional intelligence

• Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices

• Hire, develop and lead an inclusive, engaged, and high performing team

Minimum requirements for the role:

• At least two years of proven leadership performance

• Strong track record of overachievement with experience in coaching a team on outbounding

• Understanding of complex sales cycles involving multiple decision makers, multiple products, and extended time-frames

• Excellent communication skills and comfortable with public speaking

• Strong interpersonal and team management skills

• Self-starter and adaptable to change

• Continued growth mindset to learn a unique industry

• Proven proficiency in data driven decision making in current role

• Demonstrated ability to provide upwards feedback to upper management

• Showcased ability to analyze and accurately forecast existing pipeline

• Comfort working with cross functional teams

• Proficient in utilizing tools such as SFDC, SalesLoft, Gong

The compensation range shown spans approved pay zones for this role. Your primary work location determines the range applicable to you, which may be narrower than the full range displayed.

The range of annual on-target earnings (OTE) range for full-time employees for this position is below. Please note that OTE pay may vary depending on factors including your city of residence, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Learn more about our total rewards and benefits below.

Annual OTE Salary

$176,460—$259,500 USD

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

Accommodations

Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email accessibleinterviewing@samsara.com or click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.

Our Commitment to Authenticity

We use Tofu, a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara’s Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.

Fraudulent Employment Offers

Samsara is aware of scams involving fake job interviews and offers. Please know we do not charge fees to applicants at any stage of the hiring process. Official communication about your application will only come from emails ending in @samsara.com, @us-greenhouse-mail.io or @mail3.guide.co. For more information regarding fraudulent employment offers, please visit our blog post here.

jobs.title: Executive Assistant
jobs.description:
Coder is looking for an Executive Assistant to support our Chief Revenue Officer (CRO) and Chief Marketing Officer (CMO). You'll help both leaders stay focused on the decisions, relationships, and priorities that move our business forward. Your work will keep two fast-moving organizations organized, connected, and prepared.

In this role, you'll manage complex schedules, coordinate executive communications, and bring structure to competing priorities. You'll work closely with leaders across Sales, Marketing, and the broader company to keep important work on track. We need someone who anticipates what's next, handles sensitive information with care, and makes the day-to-day easier for everyone involved.




WHAT YOU'LL DO HERE

 - Serve as a trusted partner to our CRO and CMO, anticipating their needs, managing competing priorities, and helping them stay focused on what matters most.

 - Manage complex calendars across multiple time zones, making thoughtful decisions about scheduling, prioritization, and executive availability.

 - Coordinate executive meetings, including agendas, preparation materials, logistics, action items, and follow-ups to keep decisions and commitments moving forward.

 - Own domestic and international travel arrangements, itineraries, expenses, and related logistics, adapting quickly when plans change.

 - Facilitate clear, timely communication with internal and external stakeholders, including drafting correspondence and coordinating executive requests.

 - Partner across Sales, Marketing, and other teams to coordinate leadership meetings, team offsites, customer engagements, and company events.

 - Identify opportunities to improve workflows, streamline administrative processes, and bring greater efficiency to how our executives and teams operate.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 5+ years of experience supporting senior executives, ideally at the VP or C-suite level in a fast-paced technology company.

 - Proven ability to support multiple executives simultaneously, balancing competing priorities and adapting to different working styles.

 - Exceptional organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to manage complex schedules, logistics, and deadlines.

 - A proactive, resourceful approach to problem-solving, with the ability to anticipate needs, exercise sound judgment, and operate independently.

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the confidence to collaborate with stakeholders at all levels of the organization.

 - Discretion, professionalism, and good judgment when handling sensitive information and confidential business matters.

 - Comfort navigating ambiguity and shifting priorities, along with proficiency with AI, Google Workspace, Slack, Zoom, and other collaboration tools.




BONUS TACOS IF YOU HAVE

 - Experience supporting Sales, Revenue, or Marketing executives at a scaling startup.

 - Familiarity with go-to-market operations, including quarterly planning, sales kickoffs, leadership reviews, and customer events.

 - Experience coordinating board meetings, investor engagements, or other high-visibility executive activities.

 - Experience planning leadership gatherings, or other company events.




ABOUT CODER

Coder is the leading platform for AI development Infrastructure, enabling enterprises to securely run human and AI-driven development workflows in consistent, governed environments. Coder provides self-hosted, agent-ready workspaces that unify developer productivity and platform governance. With Coder, enterprises can confidently evolve from human-only development to AI-assisted and autonomous workflows, without sacrificing security, compliance, or performance. Learn more at coder.com http://coder.com.




INTERVIEW PROCESS 

We believe that the interview process should be transparent, consistent, and enjoyable. We value your time and hope to complete the interview process in two to four weeks, if schedules allow.  Through your interviews, you will meet a mix of individual contributors, managers, and senior leaders. 




AI USE DURING THE INTERVIEW PROCESS

As an AI company, Coder embraces the use of AI tools, and we want to be transparent about our expectations as you navigate our interview process.  

Not permitted: Using AI assistance during conversational interviews.

Permitted: Using AI tooling for take-home assessments. Please flag where and to what extent it was used in your take-home. Your submission will not be penalized for using AI as long as it is done honestly.




OUR USE OF AI IN HIRING

We use AI tools to help manage our recruitment process efficiently and fairly. Specifically:

 - Ashby and Brainerr help us review inbound applications by surfacing candidates who best match the role requirements we've defined. This tool does not make hiring decisions; it helps our team prioritize which applications to review first.

 - Granola takes notes during our interview calls so our team can focus on the conversation with you.

All hiring decisions are made by humans. Our team reviews applications, conducts interviews, and makes final selections. AI tools assist us but never replace human judgment, and these practices are conducted in compliance with applicable data protection, AI governance, and labor laws. Your data is not used to train AI models.

In accordance with New York City Local Law 144, an independent bias audit has been conducted on "Automated Employment Decision Tools"; results are available for Ashby https://www.ashbyhq.com/downloadables/ashby-bias-audit-08-2024.pdf.

If you're applying for a role at Coder and have questions about how we use AI in our process, or if you'd like to request information about the data we collect, please contact careers@coder.com.

 


CODER IS A PROUD EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

We are committed to providing equal employment opportunities to qualified applicants and do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, pregnancy, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, national origin, age, marital status, genetic information, disability, protected veteran status or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.

jobs.title: Senior/Staff Data Scientist (ACF)
jobs.description:
About Skylight

Skylight is a digital consultancy using design and technology to help government agencies deliver better public services.

We’re at the forefront of a civic movement to reinvent how all levels of government serve families, patients, and many others in today’s digital world.

If you want to play a part in driving this critical movement forward, we’d love for you to join our growing team of public interest technologists.

The work we do matters.

About the job

At Skylight, data scientists organize, synthesize, visualize, and analyze data to help government stakeholders and product teams make informed decisions. They apply a variety of analytical models to find meaningful insights in both structured and unstructured data, and they communicate these insights in an easily digestible format.

The Administration for Children and Families (ACF) is expanding surge support and capacity for its new Data Capacity and Digital Services organization within the Office of Administration, through the option year of our Task Order 1 contract. The team works with enterprise-serving organizations like ACF Tech and the Office of Grants Management to help programs deliver on ACF’s mission, including priorities focused on reducing grantee burden; reducing waste, fraud, and abuse; and modernizing legacy systems.

You’ll help answer hard questions with data. This role also flexes into lightweight engineering: when a problem calls for a small tool or automation built with AI, DataBricks, or Power Apps rather than a model, you build it.

What to know going in

This work calls for a consultant’s skill set: you’ll interface directly with senior leaders, and much of the work isn’t scoped in advance. This isn’t a team where you take tickets off the top of a backlog. Alongside delivery, we do a lot of technical consulting and capacity building, so people who take initiative and are comfortable with uncertainty and ambiguity tend to do best here.

While the scope of this role is likely to evolve over time, the majority of this work may not focus directly on predictive analytics or statistical analysis. Rather, the majority of your work would be focused on data ingestion, data storage and processing, and data visualization.

What you’ll do

• Engage executive and program stakeholders to frame the right questions, then take the initiative to go find the answers, even when the ask is ambiguous or the audience is tough

• Organize data and build data pipelines, using tools like Palantir Foundry and PowerBI

• Build AI agents, integrating them into workflows, validating outputs

• Visualize grant and program data using Tableau and PowerBI

• Analyze large amounts of structured and unstructured information, including grants and program data, to discover trends and patterns

• Build lightweight tools, prototypes, and automations with platforms like Credal and Power Apps when a quick solution beats a long one

• Propose solutions and strategies for business challenges, and select the right tools, frameworks, and languages for the job, with a preference for open-source, and low/no-code solutions

• Communicate findings through data visualization that leadership can act on

• Build predictive models and machine-learning algorithms, at times, and

• Collaborate with others as part of a cross-functional team that includes user experience researchers and designers, product managers, engineers, and other functional specialists

What we’re looking for

Basic qualifications

• Can think about and use data strategically to identify the right questions to ask, communicate ideas, surface opportunities to create business value and drive decisions

• Familiar with modern data engineering, including techniques for cleaning and preprocessing data from a variety of sources

• Ability to analyze a data set using the appropriate analytical method and can design, prototype, and build statistical models that are credible, effective, and accessible

• Ability to preserve privacy and security when performing data analysis

• Can articulately communicate your data, models, and findings to technical and non-technical audiences

• Ability to use the appropriate visualization tools to highlight actionable insights, trends, and recommendations from data

• Champion leading practices within data science to your team and others

• Ability to flex into lightweight engineering, building small tools and automations with low-code and AI platforms such as Credal, DataBricks and Microsoft Power Apps

• Experience working on cross-functional teams (product, design, engineering, ops) in iterative delivery

• A mindset and work approach that aligns with our core values

Nice-to-haves

• Experience and interest in policy, public health, or human services

• Experience with grants management data and large, unstructured data sets

• Familiarity with Palantir Foundry and/or Databricks

• Experience delivering AI-forward technology in government, regulated industries, or other public-benefit settings

• A track record of staying aligned and accountable on remote teams

Don’t meet every qualification but think you can do the job? We’d still love to hear from you. If you’re excited about the role, apply. We consider candidates with a range of backgrounds and experiences.

Other requirements

• Some of our available roles are on federal contracts that require a degree or additional years of experience as a substitute.

• All work must be conducted within the U.S., excluding U.S. territories.

• You must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. now and in the future without sponsorship.

• An existing clearance isn’t required to apply, but as a government contractor, anyone hired into this role must be able to obtain a Tier 2 public trust background investigation.

• You must complete a company background check successfully.

Logistics

Position type

This is a full-time, exempt position.

Location

This is a fully remote position.

Travel

This role may require travel one to two times a year based on client or contract needs.

Care package

Salary

We want to give you the most competitive salary possible. After all, you deserve it! To that end, we use the results of our interview process to determine what salary is most appropriate given your current level of seniority. For a Data Scientist at Skylight, the current salary ranges are as follows:

• Associate Data Scientist: $90,000–$125,000

• Data Scientist I: $120,000–$140,000

• Data Scientist II: $135,000–$160,000

• Senior Data Scientist: $150,000–$185,000

• Staff Data Scientist: $170,000–$203,000

• Principal Data Scientist: $180,000–$230,000

Benefits

Your well-being is important to us, so we focus on supporting you in a variety of ways:

• Medical insurance, dental insurance, vision insurance

• Short-term and long-term disability insurance

• Life and AD&D insurance

• Dependent care FSA, healthcare FSA, health savings account

• Dollar-for-dollar 401(k) match up to 10% of your salary with no vesting period

• Flexible paid-time-off policy (generally around 25 days per year), plus 11 paid federal holidays

• Up to 12 weeks paid-time-off for all eligible new birth, adoption, or foster parents

• Performance rewards, including annual salary increase, annual performance bonus, spot bonuses, and stock options

• Business development / sales bonuses

• Referral bonuses

• Annual $2000 allowance for professional development

• Annual $750 allowance for tech-related purchases

• Annual swag budget of $100 to display your Skylight pride with some merchandise (hoodies, hats, and more)

• Flexible, remote-friendly work environment

• An environment that empowers you to unleash your superpowers for public good

Interview tips

Our process includes a preliminary screen, a skills interview, a behavioral interview, and a reverse interview where you meet your potential team — usually four conversations across two to three weeks. Here are some tips to help you prepare for a successful interview:

• Visit our join page to learn more about how our interview process works.

• Check out our Career Pathways framework to learn more about the different roles within Skylight and the skills needed to do them.

• Browse our case studies to learn more about our work.

If you’d like to request reasonable accommodations during the application or interviewing process, please contact our recruiting team at recruiting@skylight.digital.

We participate in E-Verify and upon hire, will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you’re authorized to work in the U.S.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, national origin, sex, religion, age, disability, veteran status, or any other category protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Product Lead, Internal Tools
jobs.description:
CHAOS Industries is redefining modern defense with a multi-product portfolio that gives the ultimate advantage—domain dominance. The company's products are powered by Coherent Distributed Networks (CDN™), empowering warfighters, commercial air operators, and border protection teams to act faster, adapt rapidly, and stay ahead of evolving threats.

CHAOS Industries was founded in 2022 and has raised a total of $1 billion in funding from leading investors, including 8VC, Accel, and Valor Equity Partners. The company is headquartered in Los Angeles, with offices in Washington, D.C., San Francisco, San Diego, Seattle, and London. For more information, please visit www.chaosinc.com.

Role Overview

Agents of CHAOS is a new internal software and AI team focused on making CHAOS faster and more effective. As Product Lead, you’ll work across business functions to identify high-value problems, decide when to build, buy, integrate, automate, or change a process, and turn the best opportunities into working software.  You’ll also balance your team building software versus creating capabilities (software and enablement) for other internal teams to develop their own.

Especially early on, this is a builder role as much as a product role. You’ll prototype, write code, create automations and integrations, and use AI-assisted development tools alongside engineers—not simply scope work for others. Over time, you’ll help establish reusable foundations that enable teams across CHAOS to build and automate more effectively themselves.

Responsibilities

• Work directly with teams across Finance, HR, Recruiting, Growth, Operations, Engineering, Manufacturing, IT, and Security to understand workflows, bottlenecks, and opportunities for internal software or AI.

• Turn ambiguous requests into clear problem statements, user workflows, success measures, and appropriately scoped projects; distinguish software opportunities from process, policy, training, or vendor problems.

• Develop priorities in concert with a steerco to address quick wins, reusable platform capabilities, and longer-term internal systems while balancing impact, urgency, cost, risk, dependencies, and maintenance burden.

• Personally build working prototypes, automations, lightweight applications, and integrations using code, APIs, AI-assisted development tools, and low-code platforms; particularly early on, expect to implement meaningful portions of solutions.

• Partner closely with engineers to move solutions from prototype to production, making pragmatic decisions about architecture, data flows, permissions, maintainability, sequencing, and build-versus-buy tradeoffs.

• Create reusable capabilities for data access, permissions, integrations, agent workflows, and other common needs so each new internal tool is easier to build, deploy, and operate than the last.

• Work full-time onsite in our Los Angeles office.

• Occasional travel may be required for cross-functional collaboration with other CHAOS offices and operating locations.

Minimum Requirements

• 4+ years in product management delivering software products or internal tools in high-ambiguity environments.

• A software engineering background with meaningful hands-on coding experience and strong working knowledge of modern web applications, APIs, data models, integrations, authentication, permissions, and software architecture.

• You are equally comfortable interviewing a business team about a broken workflow and opening an IDE to test a solution.

• You have strong product judgment and focus on the underlying problem rather than the requested feature.

• You thrive in high-autonomy, ambiguous environments and can move from discovery to a working solution without waiting for perfect requirements.

• You know when to prototype quickly, when to invest in durable infrastructure, and when not to build software at all.

• You earn credibility with engineers through technical depth and with business teams through pragmatism, communication, and follow-through.

• Demonstrated ability to take ambiguous business problems from discovery through implementation and adoption, ideally across multiple functions, clients, or domains.

• Fluency with modern AI development workflows and tools such as Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Codex, or similar, including using them to materially accelerate prototyping and software development.

Preferred Requirements

• Experience in a design-build software consultancy, internal-tools or enterprise-platform team, forward-deployed engineering organization

• Familiarity with systems such as ERP, CRM, QMS, manufacturing, or data platforms

Why CHAOS?

• Health Benefits: Medical, dental, and vision benefits 100% paid for by the company

• Additional benefits: 401k (+ 50% company match up to 6% of pay), FSA, HSA, life insurance, and more

• Our Perks: Free daily lunch, ‘No meeting Fridays’, unlimited PTO, casual dress code

• Compensation Components: Competitive base salaries, generous pre-IPO stock option grants, relocation assistance, and (coming soon!) annual bonuses

• Team Growth: 350 employees and counting across 5 global offices

Salary Range: $211,000 - $290,000

The stated compensation range reflects only the targeted base compensation range and excludes additional earnings such as bonus, equity, and benefits. jobs.title: Staff Product Engineer
jobs.description:
Founded in 2017, Trust & Will is the leading digital estate planning platform, trusted by over one million users. We provide modern, accessible solutions to help families protect their legacies with attorney-approved, legally valid documents tailored to individual state requirements. Our seamless online platform simplifies the estate planning and settlement process, empowering individuals to create wills and trusts while also partnering with financial advisors, attorneys, and institutions to make legacy planning more inclusive and affordable.

As a Staff Product Engineer, you take product work from a customer or business need through production, across both product and engineering. You combine product judgment, full-stack engineering and agent-driven development, partner closely with product management, design and engineering, and carry a project independently when the work calls for it. This is a staff-level individual contributor role with company-wide scope.

About the Role:

• Own product and engineering work from intake through launch, and stay with it after it ships.

• Partner with product managers on the problem, the customer and the business case, and bring a view on scope, sequencing and what not to build.

• Partner with engineering leaders and senior engineers on architecture, design reviews and technical direction.

• Talk directly with members, advisors, attorneys and internal teams to understand use cases.

• Design and ship across the platform (UI, services, data and integrations).

• Carry a project end to end, partnering with others when the work calls for it.

• Build testing, safe release, and production visibility into the work, and make tradeoffs explicit.

• Move across product areas as priorities change, pairing with others, and leaving behind systems the team can reuse.

Qualifications:

• 8+ years building and shipping customer-facing software, or equivalent depth, including work at a staff, principal or lead level.

• Staff-level product judgment: framing an ambiguous problem, defining success, setting scope and deciding what not to build.

• Staff-level engineering depth: system design across user interfaces, APIs and relational data, with sound tradeoffs between speed, reliability and long-term maintainability.

• A record of shipping from idea to production, with or without a detailed spec, and owning the result after launch.

• Experience partnering as a peer with product managers, designers and engineering leaders, and bringing decisions through design and architecture review.

• Comfort working directly with customers and non-technical partners, and turning what they say into a scope.

• Care for quality, security, and reliability in production, especially in products that handle sensitive personal and financial information.

• Influence without formal authority, through clear writing, clear tradeoffs, pairing and example.

• This position is available to candidates residing in the following states only: California (CA), Colorado (CO), Florida (FL), Georgia (GA), Idaho (ID), Illinois (IL), Maryland (MD), New Jersey (NJ), New York (NY), North Carolina (NC), Pennsylvania (PA), Tennessee (TN), Texas (TX), Vermont (VT), Nevada (NV), Utah (UT)

How We Work: AI-First

• Works mainly by specifying outcomes: a clear goal, constraints and acceptance criteria that agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or similar) pursue without continuous supervision.

• Builds validation into the system, through tests, evaluations, automated checks and production signals, so agents confirm their own work before a person reviews the result.

• Sets and governs the boundaries agents work within, including what they may change, release or access, with extra care around customer data, security and production.

• Handles the exceptions agents escalate, and keeps step-by-step supervision for work where the risk calls for it.

• Helps other engineers move from using AI as an assistant toward delegating whole outcomes, safely.

• Candidates must walk through a real outcome they delegated to agents during the interview, including how it was validated and where a person stepped in.

Bonus Points for:

• Experience in regulated or high-trust products, such as financial services, legal, insurance or health.

• Founder, founding engineer or early product engineer experience building a product from scratch.

• Experience writing product specs, running customer research or working in product management.

• Experience leading cross-team work that left a team with a better way to build.

• Experience working on high-autonomy, remote-first teams where problems arrive loosely defined.

What Success Looks Like:

• Important product work ships, and the members, advisors or teams who needed it use it.

• Product managers and engineering leaders see this role as a partner who makes their plans easier to deliver.

• Architecture and design decisions are reviewed, written down and fit the platform.

• What ships can be tested, watched and reversed.

• Engineers and product partners who work with this person ship faster at the same, or higher, quality bar.

• Agents deliver and validate defined outcomes within clear boundaries, and people handle the exceptions.

Full-time Employee Benefits & Perks:

• Our salary range for this position is $225,000 - $250,000, in addition to compensation we also include an employee equity package as a component of our offer along with other benefits and perks outlined below.

• PTO

• Flexible time off that you are encouraged to use

• Generous paid company holidays and breaks throughout the year

• Monthly friends & family day

• Paid time off to volunteer in your community

• Exceptional health benefits including medical, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance - we cover 100% of premiums for employees and dependents on medical coverage

• Mental health support through Spring Health, plus access to One Medical for primary care.

• Financial wellness benefits (unlimited 1:1 sessions with a UBS financial coach and employer-sponsored 401k with up to 4% company match)

• Extra

• Flexible work schedule + hours

• Family-friendly work environment. We support the complexity of a remote world with the needs of families

• Up to $1,000 annually in learning & development reimbursement

• Optional company-sponsored events and travel throughout the year

Our hiring process is also conducted virtually unless otherwise noted. We are a company that was founded in San Diego, CA, and offer a collaborative co-working space that is available for you to use if you'd like but not required. #LI-Remote

jobs.title: CX Knowledge Specialist
jobs.description:
WHY HARVEY

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

 


ROLE OVERVIEW

Harvey ships product every week, and every release changes what our customers, our support specialists, and our AI Support agent need to know. Today that knowledge lives across fragmented surfaces, and the gap between what's shipped and what's documented shows up directly in ticket volume, resolution time, and the quality of answers customers get.

The CX Knowledge Specialist owns the source of truth: the articles, troubleshooting guides, and product knowledge that specialists and our AI Support agent answer from. You'll consolidate that knowledge into one well-structured foundation built for both people and AI, keep it accurate as the product moves, and use ticket, search, and agent data to decide what to fix next.

You'll work alongside our Enablement Specialists, who turn that knowledge into training and get the team ready for each launch. This is a hands-on role for a strong writer and systems thinker who wants to build the knowledge layer an AI-first support organization runs on.

 


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Audit today's fragmented content surfaces: inventory and tag what exists, flag what's duplicate or stale, and migrate it into one knowledge foundation.

 - Own the knowledge base: product support articles, troubleshooting guides, how-tos, and product best practices that specialists and the AI Support agent rely on.

 - Structure knowledge for both humans and AI. Apply taxonomy, metadata, and templates consistently, and write articles that retrieve and chunk cleanly for the AI Support agent as well as for specialists.

 - Keep knowledge current through every release. Track what Product ships, and update or create the affected articles before launch so they're ready for the Enablement Specialists' training and for the AI Support agent.

 - Close knowledge gaps at the source by owning the feedback loop. Triage reports of inaccurate, missing, or buried content from downstream teams, then update the source material.

 - Mine ticket signals, search logs, and agent escalations to find missing content, stale articles, and areas with high deflection potential, then prioritize fixes.

 - Build AI-assisted workflows for drafting, refreshing, and detecting stale content (prompts, automations, review queues) so knowledge scales without adding headcount.

 - Run review cycles, ownership assignments, versioning, and archiving so content stays accurate as the product changes weekly.

 - Serve as the day-to-day contact for SMEs in Product, Engineering, AI Support, and GTM Enablement to get content reviewed, validated, and adopted.

 


WHAT YOU HAVE

 - 5+ years of experience in knowledge management, support operations, technical writing, or content operations.

 - Hands-on experience with knowledge base platforms (Zendesk, Notion, or similar), including structuring, migrating, and maintaining content at scale.

 - Comfortable using LLMs in your daily workflow, and able to speak concretely to how you've used them to write, maintain, or improve content.

 - A systems thinker who likes structure, and a strong writer who can turn complex technical or legal-product details into clear, retrievable content.

 - Comfortable operating at Harvey's pace, where the product changes weekly and content needs to keep up without waiting for a perfect process.

 - Uses data (ticket trends, search behavior, QA findings) to decide what to write or fix next, rather than working from a static backlog.

 - Builds strong working relationships with cross-functional SMEs quickly, and can get content reviewed and adopted without direct authority.

 


COMPENSATION

$88,000 - $132,000 USD

jobs.title: Manager, Data Management & Operations
jobs.description:
CHAOS Industries is redefining modern defense with a multi-product portfolio that gives the ultimate advantage—domain dominance. The company's products are powered by Coherent Distributed Networks (CDN™), empowering warfighters, commercial air operators, and border protection teams to act faster, adapt rapidly, and stay ahead of evolving threats.

CHAOS Industries was founded in 2022 and has raised a total of $1 billion in funding from leading investors, including 8VC, Accel, and Valor Equity Partners. The company is headquartered in Los Angeles, with offices in Washington, D.C., San Francisco, San Diego, Seattle, and London. For more information, please visit www.chaosinc.com.

Role Overview

Data is foundational to how CHAOS develops, tests, and improves complex sensing systems. As the company scales, we need a data operating model that makes information consistent, trusted, secure, and usable across Engineering, AI, Test, and business teams.

As Manager of Data Management and Operations, you'll own the end-to-end data lifecycle: how data is defined, collected, transported, governed, transformed, secured, and delivered for analysis. You'll lead our data management and field data operations functions, partnering closely with the Foundry engineering team to ensure the platform meets company needs.

This isn't an analytics-only role. It's a technical and operational leadership role spanning data governance, data-platform coordination, and test operations. You'll build durable systems and teams while remaining close enough to field execution to understand where data quality and collection break down.

Success means teams use the same definitions, analysts can trust the datasets they receive, test data is captured and available quickly, and access to sensitive data is controlled and auditable without becoming a barrier to execution.

Responsibilities

• Establish company-wide governance for data definitions, ownership, quality, lineage, retention, and calculation change management.

• Create authoritative, documented analytical datasets and shared definitions so teams can work from consistent data and metrics.

• Work with the Foundry engineering team to ensure that data ingestion, ETL, modeling, transformation, validation, and monitoring align with stakeholder needs.

• Own permissions management and partner with Security and Compliance to implement least-privilege access, auditability, retention, and handling controls for sensitive data.

• Build a repeatable process for planning data capture at test events, including required sensor data, metadata, truth data, labels, logging, storage, and validation.

• Coordinate across teams to translate test objectives into clear data requirements and ensure collection systems are ready before testing begins.

• Establish pre-test readiness and post-test reconciliation processes so required data is captured, validated, transferred, cataloged, and available for analysis.

• Use test outcomes and data gaps to continuously improve collection methods, retention strategy, data quality controls, and the underlying data architecture.

• Build and manage teams responsible for data governance and field data operations, while establishing an effective partnership with the Foundry engineering team.

• Sustain data operations at CHAOS test sites, including contributing to test schedule strategy, extraction technology and logistics, , and data labeling.

• Create clear operating procedures, ownership, service levels, and metrics for pipeline reliability, test data capture, and data availability.

• Partner with Foundry engineering to balance immediate test and program needs with long-term investments in scalable architecture, automation, , and team capability.

• Work full-time on-site at our El Segundo, CA headquarters

• Travel to CHAOS test sites and other company locations on a regular basis.

• Support critical test events and field operations outside standard business hours when needed.

Minimum Requirements

• 8+ years of experience across data engineering, data platforms, data governance, analytics infrastructure, test data, or similarly complex technical environments, including significant team leadership.

• 1+ years of management experience, ideally with prior experience managing teams incorporating non-exempt or contract employees.

• You see data as both a technical platform and an operating discipline, not simply a reporting or analytics function.

• You can move comfortably between data engineers, radar and test teams, security stakeholders, analysts, and senior leadership.

• You build governance creating clarity and trust without unnecessary bureaucracy.

• You are willing to get close to field operations and understand the practical realities of collecting, moving, and validating data.

• You thrive in high-execution environments where requirements evolve quickly and ownership is expected.

• You combine strong technical judgment with practical prioritization and can make sound tradeoffs across platform, operations, and compliance.

• You enjoy building teams, systems, and operating rhythms from the ground up.

• Demonstrated ownership of production data pipelines from source ingestion through transformation, quality assurance, publication, and consumption.

• Strong knowledge of ETL, data modeling, metadata, lineage, data quality, observability, and modern data engineering practices.

• Strong cross-functional leadership and communication skills, with the ability to turn ambiguous needs into clear standards, systems, and operating processes.

• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, Information Systems, or a related technical field.

Preferred Requirements

• Experience with Palantir Foundry or a comparable enterprise data platform; deep Foundry experience is strongly preferred.

• Radar or defense systems experience

• Experience planning or supporting test events and coordinating the operational logistics required to reliably collect and transport data.

• Experience designing permissions and access-control processes in environments with significant security, compliance, audit, or data-handling requirements.

• Experience supporting data collection from physical systems, sensors, laboratories, manufacturing, or field testing.

Why CHAOS?

• Health Benefits: Medical, dental, and vision benefits 100% paid for by the company

• Additional benefits: 401k (+ 50% company match up to 6% of pay), FSA, HSA, life insurance, and more

• Our Perks: Free daily lunch, ‘No meeting Fridays’, unlimited PTO, casual dress code

• Compensation Components: Competitive base salaries, generous pre-IPO stock option grants, relocation assistance, and (coming soon!) annual bonuses

• Team Growth: 350 employees and counting across 5 global offices

Salary Range: $246,000 - $339,000

jobs.description:
About Glean:

Glean is the Work AI platform that helps everyone work smarter with AI. What began as the industry’s most advanced enterprise search has evolved into a full-scale Work AI ecosystem, powering intelligent Search, an AI Assistant, and scalable AI agents on one secure, open platform. With over 100 enterprise SaaS connectors, flexible LLM choice, and robust APIs, Glean gives organizations the infrastructure to govern, scale, and customize AI across their entire business - without vendor lock-in or costly implementation cycles.

At its core, Glean is redefining how enterprises find, use, and act on knowledge. Its Enterprise Graph and Personal Knowledge Graph map the relationships between people, content, and activity, delivering deeply personalized, context-aware responses for every employee. This foundation powers Glean’s agentic capabilities - AI agents that automate real work across teams by accessing the industry’s broadest range of data: enterprise and world, structured and unstructured, historical and real-time. The result: measurable business impact through faster onboarding, hours of productivity gained each week, and smarter, safer decisions at every level.

Recognized by Fast Company as one of the World’s Most Innovative Companies (Top 10, 2025), by CNBC’s Disruptor 50, Bloomberg’s AI Startups to Watch (2026), Forbes AI 50, and Gartner’s Tech Innovators in Agentic AI, Glean continues to accelerate its global impact. With customers across 50+ industries and 1,000+ employees in more than 25 countries, we’re helping the world’s largest organizations make every employee AI-fluent, and turning the superintelligent enterprise from concept into reality.

If you’re excited to shape how the world works, you’ll help build systems used daily across Microsoft Teams, Zoom, ServiceNow, Zendesk, GitHub, and many more. You'll be deeply embedded where people get things done. You'll ship agentic capabilities on an open, extensible stack, with the craft and care required for enterprise trust, as we bring Work AI to every employee, in every company.

About the Role:

Glean is looking for a Senior Site Reliability Engineer to strengthen the reliability, scalability, and operational excellence of our production services. In this hands-on individual-contributor role, you’ll design, build, and operate resilient cloud infrastructure; improve service reliability against meaningful SLOs; and help teams respond to production issues through effective observability, incident practices, and blameless learning. You’ll contribute technical expertise to system and architectural decisions and partner with engineers across the organization to deliver dependable systems.

Glean’s rapid growth brings complex distributed-systems challenges across a hybrid cloud environment. You’ll use your software engineering and SRE skills to automate repetitive work, build tools, and improve deployment, monitoring, and on-call workflows. From investigating incidents and reducing toil to optimizing performance, capacity, and cost, your work will help Glean scale while providing customers with a reliable experience.

You will:

• Technical Leadership and Mentorship: Play a key role in driving technical excellence and fostering a culture of reliability across engineering teams. You will lead by example, setting best practices for incident management, performance optimization, and automation. Influence best practices, drive cross-team collaborations, and contribute to the execution of key objectives in alignment with engineering leadership and cross-functional partners. Establish strong technical credibility, shaping architectural decisions and ensuring the delivery of high-quality, reliable systems.

• Ensure High Availability: Implement and maintain resilient cloud architectures, monitor system performance, and proactively identify and resolve potential bottlenecks or points of failure.

• Incident Management: Participate in primary oncall rotation; cultivate technical curiosity and growth mindset, and a blameless postmortem culture within the team. Continuously optimize the on-call process for sustainability and efficiency.

• Automation and Tooling: Develop and maintain automation scripts, tools, and processes to streamline system deployment, monitoring, and management tasks. Your contributions will be vital in efficiently scaling cloud operations.

• Performance Optimization: Optimize cloud infrastructure and applications for performance, scalability, and cost-effectiveness.

• Security and Compliance: Collaborate with security engineers to implement best practices and ensure compliance with security standards and policies.

• Monitoring and Alerting: Design and configure advanced monitoring systems to gain insights into system behavior, set up alerts, and respond proactively to potential issues. Create and maintain comprehensive dashboards and playbooks for production on-call.

• Software Development Consultation: Engage actively in the entire software development lifecycle. Participate in system design reviews and provide valuable SRE insights during launch reviews, influencing and enhancing system architecture.

About you:

• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

• 5+ years of experience in a senior-level role within Site Reliability Engineering or similar role, particularly in managing cloud-based services and infrastructure.

• 5+ years of experience with software development in one or more programming languages.

• 3+ years of experience leading projects and designing, analyzing, and troubleshooting distributed systems running in Cloud.

• Strong knowledge of cloud platforms such as Google Cloud Platform, AWS, or Azure.

• Practical experience with containerization technologies, including Docker and Kubernetes. Familiarity with infrastructure as code tools like Terraform is essential.

• Solid understanding of networking, security principles, and best SRE and security practices.

• Proficiency in using monitoring and alerting tools to detect and respond to potential issues effectively

Location:

• This role is hybrid (4 days a week in our Mountain View Office)

jobs.title: CX Knowledge Specialist
jobs.description:
WHY HARVEY

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.




ROLE OVERVIEW

Harvey ships product every week, and every release changes what our customers, our support specialists, and our AI Support agent need to know. Today that knowledge lives across fragmented surfaces, and the gap between what's shipped and what's documented shows up directly in ticket volume, resolution time, and the quality of answers customers get.

The CX Knowledge Specialist owns the source of truth: the articles, troubleshooting guides, and product knowledge that specialists and our AI Support agent answer from. You'll consolidate that knowledge into one well-structured foundation built for both people and AI, keep it accurate as the product moves, and use ticket, search, and agent data to decide what to fix next.

You'll work alongside our Enablement Specialists, who turn that knowledge into training and get the team ready for each launch. This is a hands-on role for a strong writer and systems thinker who wants to build the knowledge layer an AI-first support organization runs on.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Audit today's fragmented content surfaces: inventory and tag what exists, flag what's duplicate or stale, and migrate it into one knowledge foundation.

 - Own the knowledge base: product support articles, troubleshooting guides, how-tos, and product best practices that specialists and the AI Support agent rely on.

 - Structure knowledge for both humans and AI. Apply taxonomy, metadata, and templates consistently, and write articles that retrieve and chunk cleanly for the AI Support agent as well as for specialists.

 - Keep knowledge current through every release. Track what Product ships, and update or create the affected articles before launch so they're ready for the Enablement Specialists' training and for the AI Support agent.

 - Close knowledge gaps at the source by owning the feedback loop. Triage reports of inaccurate, missing, or buried content from downstream teams, then update the source material.

 - Mine ticket signals, search logs, and agent escalations to find missing content, stale articles, and areas with high deflection potential, then prioritize fixes.

 - Build AI-assisted workflows for drafting, refreshing, and detecting stale content (prompts, automations, review queues) so knowledge scales without adding headcount.

 - Run review cycles, ownership assignments, versioning, and archiving so content stays accurate as the product changes weekly.

 - Serve as the day-to-day contact for SMEs in Product, Engineering, AI Support, and GTM Enablement to get content reviewed, validated, and adopted.




WHAT YOU HAVE

 - 5+ years of experience in knowledge management, support operations, technical writing, or content operations.

 - Hands-on experience with knowledge base platforms (Zendesk, Notion, or similar), including structuring, migrating, and maintaining content at scale.

 - Comfortable using LLMs in your daily workflow, and able to speak concretely to how you've used them to write, maintain, or improve content.

 - A systems thinker who likes structure, and a strong writer who can turn complex technical or legal-product details into clear, retrievable content.

 - Comfortable operating at Harvey's pace, where the product changes weekly and content needs to keep up without waiting for a perfect process.

 - Uses data (ticket trends, search behavior, QA findings) to decide what to write or fix next, rather than working from a static backlog.

 - Builds strong working relationships with cross-functional SMEs quickly, and can get content reviewed and adopted without direct authority.




COMPENSATION

$88,000 - $132,000 USD

At LinkedIn, our approach to flexible work is centered on trust and optimized for culture, connection, clarity, and the evolving needs of our business. The Capacity & Efficiency Engineering team drives LinkedIn’s end-to-end infrastructure capacity planning and efficiency strategy. We build the data, models, and planning systems that connect infrastructure demand to business growth, attribute costs to the products that drive them, and forecast resource needs across dozens of infrastructure platforms. Our systems are foundational to how Product, Finance, and Infrastructure leadership make decisions on infrastructure investment, capacity allocation, budget planning, and efficiency. By providing a consistent view of demand, supply, and cost, we enable leaders to make informed trade-offs, identify efficiency opportunities, and scale LinkedIn’s infrastructure sustainably.

We are seeking a Staff Software Engineer to join LinkedIn's Capacity & Efficiency Engineering team and play a critical role in building the foundational datasets, models, and tools that power infrastructure visibility, cost attribution, and planning. • Set high standards for data quality, correctness, and reliability across the data and models underpinning critical capacity and financial decisions.

jobs.title: Engineering Manager, Provider Experience
jobs.description:
At Commure, we're building the AI Operating System for healthcare, the foundation that defines how care is delivered, documented, and financed. Our platform spans the full care journey: Ambient AI and Dictation eliminating documentation burden at the point of care, intelligent Agents automating patient and revenue workflows, and autonomous RCM processing billions in claims, all on a single AI-native platform integrated with 60+ EHRs.



Healthcare carries a $1 trillion administrative burden and we're at the center of transforming it. Today, 500,000+ clinicians across 500+ healthcare organizations nationwide trust Commure to handle $25B+ in annual claims and support over 200 million patient interactions. Our latest $70M raise at a $7B valuation reflects the confidence the market has placed in this mission. We've also been named to the Fortune Future 50 list and the 2026 AI Breakthrough Awards for “Overall NLP Company of the Year.”



Our team works directly alongside clinicians, not through layers of process, which means the gap between what you build and its impact on patient care is immediate. We move fast, deploy daily, and take full ownership from early thinking to production. If you're energized by hard problems, high stakes, and a team that holds itself to a high bar, you'll find your people here.



The future of healthcare is being built right now. Come deliver this transformation.



About the Role

At Commure, our Air AI team is building the intelligence layer that lives inside the clinical workflow — one that listens, documents, reasons, and acts so clinicians don't have to. The Provider Pod turns that intelligence into the daily clinician experience. The team works across AI-powered documentation that transcribes patient visits and structures them into clinical notes in real time, a conversational clinical assistant grounded in live patient context and medical literature, and an extensible AI Skills Library of reusable agents and workflows that automates clinical work across the platform. We also own the core provider surfaces around charting, clinical coding, treatments and flowsheets, orders, labs, prescriptions, and the signed encounter that powers downstream billing.

As the Engineering Manager for the Provider Pod, you'll lead a full-stack team responsible for building AI that clinicians trust with their most critical work. You'll own people leadership, technical direction, roadmap execution, and operational excellence across Python backend services, TypeScript/React product surfaces, and AI/LLM workflows. You'll partner closely with Product, Design, Clinical, AI/ML, Data, Platform, and RCM to turn ambitious ideas into intuitive, scalable, and reliable features that work in real clinical environments. This is a hands-on leadership role on a fast-moving team that celebrates large ambition, ships daily, and makes decisions quickly.



What You'll Do

 - Lead and grow the Provider Pod: Recruit, coach, and develop a high-performing team of full-stack engineers.

 - Own product and engineering outcomes: Drive the roadmap and execution across scribe documentation, the clinical assistant, reusable AI skills, and core provider workflows.

 - Set the technical direction: Guide architecture across Python services, TypeScript/React experiences, data systems, and AI/LLM workflows.

 - Partner cross-functionally: Work with Product, Design, clinical experts, AI/ML, Data, Platform, and Air Billing to ship intuitive solutions for real clinical environments.

 - Raise the engineering bar: Establish strong practices for planning, code quality, testing, deployment, and observability while keeping the team fast and pragmatic.

 - Drive operational excellence: Ensure provider-facing systems are reliable, secure, performant, and supported by effective on-call and incident response.

 - Build a high-ownership culture: Mentor technical leaders and foster strong judgment, customer empathy, healthy debate, and a bias toward action.
   
   

What You Have

 - Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, required

 - 6+ years of software engineering experience, including 2+ years managing or formally leading engineers

 - Proven success hiring, coaching, and developing high-performing engineering teams

 - Strong full-stack technical depth across Python, TypeScript/React, APIs, data systems, containers, and cloud infrastructure

 - Hands-on experience integrating LLM APIs or shipping AI-powered features in production

 - Track record of driving complex, user-facing products from early ideation through successful production deployment

 - Strong product judgment, communication, and cross-functional leadership in fast-moving environments

 - Bonus: experience with EHRs, clinical software, healthcare interoperability, or regulated environments such as HIPAA and SOC 2
