jobs.title: AI/ML Engineering Intern
jobs.description:
Company Overview

Amperesand is reinventing how the world powers its most critical systems.

We are facing a once-in-a-generation opportunity for infrastructure disruption. Electricity demand is skyrocketing, driven by AI factories, electric vehicles, and modern industrial growth. Energy supply is shifting to incorporate a more diverse mix of resources – including solar, gas, and batteries – at a massive scale.

And yet the power infrastructure behind our latest mega-projects hasn’t meaningfully changed in nearly 100 years. Supply chains for today’s infrastructure equipment can’t match the pace and sophistication of critical energy projects. Amperesand is building hardware and software that rewrites this broken power infrastructure playbook to support a new era of energy abundance.

We’ve built a new class of intelligent, software-defined power infrastructure products leveraging a decade of advanced medium voltage Solid State Transformer research that’s now ready for commercial deployment.

Our products and solutions go far beyond the capabilities of traditional electrical equipment. We make power systems that are faster to deploy, dramatically smaller and more efficient, and capable of supporting modern, dynamic energy needs for tomorrow’s most demanding energy consumers.

Scalable in-house advanced manufacturing capability is our foundation for meeting timeline and quality expectation to serve infrastructure customers around the world.

Amperesand is led by breakthrough energy hardware development veterans and funded by top tier investors who share our vision of building a category-defining energy technology company.

With hubs in San Francisco, Reno, and Singapore, our global team is laser focused on building foundational technology to solve the most pressing problems in power infrastructure at scale.

Join us in building the power foundation of the future!

About Amperesand

Amperesand is building next-generation power infrastructure systems for Data Centers, EV charging platforms, and future energy applications. Our systems combine advanced power electronics, embedded controls, and scalable energy architectures to rethink how power is converted, controlled, and deployed.

About the Role

This internship is an opportunity to work hands-on with a startup engineering team that builds and experiments with the latest advancements in AI and Machine Learning. You will contribute to multiple teams, architecting and implementing AI/ML solutions to help improve reliability, and accelerate the development process

You will work closely with engineers, product owners, and internal and external stakeholders who rely on our AI enabled solutions every day. This is a fast-paced, goal-oriented environment where you'll be expected to take ownership of real, production-facing work.

What You’ll Do

• Design and develop AI/ML solutions that accelerate product development and engineering workflows.

• Build AI frameworks, agentic workflows, and knowledge assistants that help teams access and utilize engineering data.

• Fine-tune, evaluate, and optimize Large Language Models (LLMs) for domain-specific engineering use cases.

• Develop Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) applications using engineering documentation, test data, and design knowledge.

• Train and deploy machine learning models to support Mechanical Design Engineering and related teams.

• Partner with Mechanical, Electrical, Manufacturing, and Software Engineers to solve high-impact business and engineering problems.

• Build data pipelines, model evaluation frameworks, and AI experimentation workflows.

• Document solutions and contribute production-quality code in a fast-paced startup environment.

• Bring a customer-oriented, team-first mindset to a fast-paced startup environment.

What You’ll Bring

• Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Data Science, or a related field.

• Strong programming skills in Python, Go, Rust, and TypeScript.

• Experience with machine learning frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, Scikit-Learn, or similar.

• Familiarity with LLMs, prompt engineering, Evals, and AI agents.

• Understanding of machine learning fundamentals, model evaluation, and data processing.

• Experience with Git and collaborative software development practices.

• Strong communication, problem-solving, and teamwork skills.

• Self-motivated, team-oriented, and comfortable working in a fast-paced, ambiguous startup environment.

• Available to work on-site.

Nice to Have

• Experience fine-tuning or evaluating open-source LLMs.

• Experience with LangChain, LlamaIndex, Hugging Face, vector databases, or agentic frameworks.

• Exposure to MLOps, cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP), or model deployment.

• Experience applying AI/ML to engineering, manufacturing, hardware, or industrial systems.

• Familiarity with CAD, PLM, simulation tools, or engineering workflows.

• Interest in energy systems, power electronics, AI infrastructure, or industrial automation.

• Research, open-source contributions, hackathons, or personal AI/ML projects.

Working Model

Employment Type:
• Full-time

Location:
Sunnyvale

Work Model:
• Onsite

Please note: This role requires working on-site 5 days a week. We do not offer hybrid or remote options.

While this role is listed for the location above, we may consider candidates in other locations on a case-by-case basis.

Onsite Collaboration Rationale:

Given the highly collaborative and cross-functional nature of hardware, embedded systems, and product development, in-person partnership across engineering and product teams is critical to enabling rapid execution, technical alignment, and successful development outcomes.

Why Join Amperesand

• Work on next-generation power infrastructure systems

• High ownership and visibility

• Cross-functional collaboration

• Opportunity to shape future products and infrastructure

• Fast-moving startup environment

Pay Disclosure & Benefits

Compensation will be determined based on experience, location, and other factors permitted by law.

The benefits outlined below apply exclusively to employees located in the United States:

• Competitive Salary + Incentive Stock Options

• Medical, vision, and dental benefits for employees and their dependents, effective from the start of hire

• Company paid Basic Life, AD&D, short-term and long-term disability insurance

• 401k retirement savings plan through Empower

• Employees receive paid time off (PTO), paid sick days, and paid company holidays

• Commuter Benefits

• 100% paid maternal leave (12 weeks) and paternal leave (6 weeks)

The benefits outlined below apply to employees located in Singapore:

• Competitive Salary + Incentive Stock Options

• Group medical, hospitalisation and surgical insurance, outpatient or GP coverage, group term life, dental and personal accident insurance

• Employer and employee Central Provident Fund contributions in accordance with the CPF Act (for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents)

• Annual leave, paid sick leave, hospitalisation leave, and all Singapore public holidays, in line with or exceeding the Employment Act

• Commuter Benefits

• Government-paid maternity, paternity, shared parental, and childcare leave in accordance with prevailing Singapore statutory entitlements

Additional benefits may be available depending on the role and employment type. Benefits are subject to the terms of applicable company policies and plans.

Candidate Confidentiality & Information Protection

As part of our commitment to protecting confidential and proprietary information, candidates should not disclose or provide Amperesand with any confidential, proprietary, or trade secret information belonging to a current or former employer or any other third party during the application or interview process.

Please do not submit or present employer-owned source code, schematics, designs, technical documentation, internal presentations, customer information, prototypes, or other confidential materials. Candidates should discuss their experience and accomplishments at an appropriate level and use only information and materials they are authorized to share.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Amperesand is an equal opportunity employer and complies with all applicable federal, state, and local fair employment practices laws. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender expression, gender identity, genetic information or characteristics, physical or mental disability, marital/domestic partner status, age, military/veteran status, medical condition, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Amperesand is also committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. Please let your recruiter know if you need an accommodation at any point during the interview process.

jobs.title: Onboarding Team Lead
jobs.description:
ABOUT NUMERAL:

At Numeral, we're building the future of tax by bringing together AI agents, human expertise, and global compliance.

We’re the largest and fastest-growing AI-native tax solution. Today, we serve more than 3,500 global businesses, including companies like Supabase, Eight Sleep, and Graza. We’ve grown quickly across our core e-commerce and software segments, more than tripled our revenue every year, and expanded into new industries, including manufacturing, distribution, and wholesale.

Numeral has raised over $157M from Insight Partners, Salesforce Ventures, Benchmark, Mayfield, Y Combinator, and many others.




ABOUT THE ROLE:

We’re looking for an Onboarding Team Lead to manage and scale our implementation engine. We’ve hit an inflection point: our customer base is surging, and we need a leader to transform our onboarding from a high-touch manual process into a scalable, tech-enabled machine.

You’ll oversee a team of 10+ Implementation Managers. This isn't just a "people management" role. You’ll be a true player-coach, owning a book of ~10 accounts yourself so you stay close to the work and can coach your team from firsthand experience. You will be the architect of our customer’s first impression. You’ll own the metrics, refine the playbooks, and ensure that as we scale, our "white-glove" reputation remains intact. This is a high-impact leadership role for someone who thrives in ambiguity, builds structure from chaos, and knows how to scale both people and processes.

 


WHAT YOU'LL DO:

 - Team Leadership & Development
   
   - Lead from the Front: Own ~10 customer implementations end-to-end. Staying hands-on keeps you sharp on our product, our customers, and the real friction points your team faces, so your coaching is grounded in reality.
   
   - Manage & Coach: Oversee a high-performing team of 10+ Implementation Managers, providing the mentorship needed to navigate complex tax logic and customer hurdles.
   
   - Build the Bench: Own hiring, onboarding, and ongoing training as we continue to expand the team, and foster an environment of extreme accountability, urgency, and customer obsession

 - Performance & Operational Design
   
   - Own the Metrics: Drive team-level outcomes including Time-to-Value (TTV), onboarding completion rates, and CSAT.
   
   - Systematize Growth: Move us from "heroics" to "systems." Build and refine scalable playbooks and internal tooling that allow us to handle 5x the volume without sacrificing quality, using AI to refine and improve processes
   
   - Data-Driven Decisions: Use data to identify bottlenecks, forecast capacity, and proactively address individual or process gaps.

 - Customer Experience & Cross-Functional Leadership
   
   - Strategic Support: Act as the primary escalation point for complex implementations and step in to support our most high-value, strategic customers.
   
   - Product Feedback Loop: Partner closely with Product and Engineering to translate frontline insights into roadmap influence, identifying where the product can "self-serve" steps currently handled manually
   
   - Define the Future: Help define how onboarding evolves as Numeral expands its product offering beyond initial compliance.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

 - Player-Coach DNA: You genuinely enjoy rolling up your sleeves. You’re energized by managing your own book of business while developing others, and you don’t see hands-on work as “beneath” a leadership role.

 - The Scaler: 5+ years of experience in implementation, onboarding, or operations, with at least 2+ years specifically managing or leading teams through high-growth phases.

 - AI Fluency: You use AI to improve team efficiency or customer workflows.

 - Technical Intuition: You don't need to be an engineer, but you are comfortable discussing APIs, data migrations, and complex logic.

 - Process-Building Mindset: Proven ability to design workflows from scratch and iterate on them as the product evolves.

 - High Ownership: A bias for action and the "figure-it-out" factor required in an early-stage startup.

 - Communication: Excellent skills across both technical and non-technical stakeholders.




NICE TO HAVES:

 - Experience managing onboarding/implementation in a high-growth SaaS or Fintech environment.

 - Experience supporting mid-market or enterprise customers.

 - Comfort with data analysis (SQL, advanced spreadsheets) to drive operational improvements.




LOCATION:

 - This role is hybrid (3 days a week in our SF or NYC office)




WHAT WE OFFER:

 - Competitive salary and equity - you'll share directly in the company's success

 - Full medical, dental, and vision coverage

 - Wellness perks like Headspace and the Peloton One App

 - 401(k) to help you build long-term financial security

 - Relocation assistance to NYC or SF (if needed)

 - Lunch and snacks when you're in the office

 - Regular team offsites and company events as we grow

 - A culture built on ownership - your work matters and people will see it!

jobs.title: Warehouse Associate/Branch Driver I
jobs.description:
We are looking for a Warehouse Associate/Branch Driver I to join our Platt team in Kent, Wa!

Summary:

The Warehouse Associate/Truck Driver I is responsible for efficiently and accurately filling customer orders, receiving, stocking, staging, and shipping material in a manner that meets company standards for safety, security, accuracy, and productivity. Responsible for all warehouse transactions, as well as the upkeep and maintenance of the branch warehouse environment and equipment. This role also has an essential driving component and may be assigned to operate a delivery vehicle for up to 50% of its time delivering products to/from customers, company branch/warehouse locations, and company suppliers in a delivery van or box truck (No CDL required). Responsible for ensuring that deliveries are prepared to meet customer requirements in the most efficient manner and materials are correct and free of damage.

What You'll Do:

• Contribute to a culture and environment focused daily on employee safety and a safe work environment
• Follow established Standard Operating Procedures, Environmental Health and Safety Rules, and immediately address safety concerns
• Receive material coming into the building by vendors, customers, or other warehouses and verify the quantity and description of materials received by checking merchandise against the packing list
• Keep incoming orders stocked on shelves orderly and in designated area and report freight damage claims
• Prepare branch orders from the warehouse and ensure that the correct number and type of product is being shipped
• Process paperwork regarding shipments including but not limited to verifying that the merchandise to be shipped is correct, applying the correct postage tape and label, following customer shipping instructions, and insuring the shipment when necessary
• Operate machinery including forklift, reach truck, and wire cutting machine when required
• Load common carrier and company vehicles
• Inspect and perform minor maintenance on equipment
• Perform inventory counts and reconcile any discrepancies
• Operate delivery vehicles to make deliveries to and from customers, company branch/warehouse locations, and company suppliers
• Inspect company vehicle for visual and operating defects; responsible for completing a daily inspection report

jobs.title: Yard Hostler
jobs.description:
Location: Long Beach, CA

Employment Type: Temp to Hire | On-Site (Monday-Friday, 6:00 AM to 3:30 PM)  | Experienced

Compensation: $29.00 per hour, depending on experience and qualifications

This is not a remote position. Relocation assistance is not offered.

Cargomatic is committed to making the lives of truckers and shippers easier. Our goal is to let truckers be truckers and shippers be shippers by simplifying the process for all our customers and vendors.

Cargomatic was named to the Built In Best Places to Work list, recognizing our people-first culture, strong benefits, and commitment to employee growth and well-being.

About the Role

The Yard Hostler Driver is responsible for safely and efficiently moving semi-trailers, shipping containers, and straight trucks around a warehouse, distribution center, or rail yard. This role is crucial to maintaining a smooth workflow, spotting trailers into active loading dock doors, staging areas, and parking stalls without driving on public highways.

Key Responsibilities:

• Shunting Trailers: Drive specialized terminal tractors to maneuver 53-foot trailers between parking stalls, staging zones, and active loading docks.

• Hydraulic Control: Use in-cab hydraulic lifts to raise and lower trailer legs, moving equipment safely without the need to manually crank landing gear.

• Yard Management: Verify trailer numbers for accuracy and log every trailer movement using onboard digital systems, inventory tracking tools, or dockyard management systems.

• Safety & Inspection: Perform thorough pre-trip and post-trip equipment inspections on yard tractors and trailers. Chock trailer wheels, manage dock locks, and report any damage or maintenance needs to supervisors.

• Coordination & Communication: Communicate effectively with warehouse, dock, and logistics staff via two-way radio or phone to ensure trailers are placed correctly for loading and unloading schedules.

• General Maintenance: Keep the yard clean, organized, and safe. Use assigned fuel stations to fuel vehicles as needed and accurately fill out driver vehicle inspection reports and logs accurately.

Requirements & Qualifications

• Driver’s License: Must have a clean driving record and be able to pass an MVR background screening.

• Experience:

• Must have previous experience as a Yard Hostler/Yard Goat, operating yard equipment or tractor-trailers, a minimum of 2+ years of experience is highly preferred.

• Experience repositioning, driving, and hauling international and/or domestic containers is required.

• Spatial Skills: Exceptional mirror-backing and maneuvering skills in tight, congested, and busy industrial spaces.

• Knowledge of Regulations: Working knowledge of DOT regulations governing safe driving, hours of service, inspection, maintenance, and vehicle safety control systems.

• Basic Skills: Ability to read, write, and perform basic mathematical calculations to handle receipts, maintain logs, and use handheld minicomputers/tablets.

Physical Requirements

• Physical Stamina: Comfort working outdoors in all weather conditions and frequently climbing in and out of the tractor cab.

• Lifting: Ability to safely lift and transport items, sometimes up to 50 pounds.

• Medical Standards: Must meet the medical standards of the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) DOT Department of Transportation, which includes passing a drug and alcohol test.

Equal Opportunity Employer

Cargomatic is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Throughout our worldwide network of experts, clients and communities, we are renowned for our leadership in fire protection engineering – a legacy of responsibility we have proudly upheld since 1939. Today, our expertise extends broadly across closely related security and risk-based fields – from accessibility consulting and risk analysis to process safety, forensic investigations, security risk consulting, emergency management, digital innovation and more.

Our engineers and consultants collaborate to solve complex safety and security challenges, ensuring our clients can protect what matters most. For over 80 years, we have helped mitigate risks that threaten lives, property and reputations. Through technology, expertise and industry-leading research, we remain dedicated to our purpose of making our world safe, secure and resilient.

At Jensen Hughes, we believe that creating and sustaining a culture of trust, integrity and professional growth starts with putting our people first. Our employees are our greatest strength, and we value the unique perspectives and talents they bring to our organization.

Our wide range of Global Employee Networks connect people from across the organization, supporting career development and providing forums for individuals to share experiences on topics they're passionate about. Together, we are cultivating a connected culture where everyone has the opportunity to learn, grow and succeed together.

Position Overview

Jensen Hughes has a new job opportunity for a Fire Protection Engineer to work on our ongoing project at a large semiconductor facility in North Phoenix.  We are looking for an experienced Engineer or Consultant to work in all aspects of fire protection engineering, including building code consulting, fire protection systems, and fire protection strategies.

The successful applicant will have a well-rounded background in fire protection and code consulting and possess strong analytical and creative thinking skills.  The role will involve many aspects of fire protection engineering with a focus on Building Code and Fire Code consulting.  The position will coordinate and conduct building plan reviews, interpret the building codes, develop alternative solutions, prepare building design reports and coordinate with fire protection engineering design teams. The candidate will be responsible for the review and implementation of fire protection strategies and will coordinate on all matters with design teams and authorities having jurisdiction.

Responsibilities:

• Perform fire and life safety code consulting tasks related to Group H-5 semiconductor facilities

• Assist with the development of alternate methods of design and/or code modification submittals

• Assist with hazardous materials consulting activities

• Perform site surveys

• Assist with fire and life safety system inspection and testing activities

• Coordinate closely with design teams and authorities having jurisdiction

• Contribute to complex, high-impact project delivery

Minimum Requirements

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Strategy & Operations (Consumer Protection Team)
jobs.description:
Flex is a growth-stage, NYC headquartered FinTech company that is building the payment layer for life's financial obligations, giving households one place to see, split, and pay their bills around how they live and get paid. By offering greater choice over how and when payments are made and allowing eligible on time payments to help build a positive credit history, Flex puts households back in control of their cash flow.

That work brings together people with different perspectives who challenge the status quo and take ownership of solving difficult problems. For you, that means doing the best work of your career next to people who make you better, and together bringing ideas to life that make a real impact for the people we serve.

About the role

The Consumer Protection Team (CPT) is Flex's internal champion for the customer, setting the standard for excellence across the customer journey, and pushing the company to create greater, tangible customer good. At Flex, we serve our customers for their most critical expenses – which means this team must set the bar exceptionally high.

As a Senior Manager, you’ll partner directly with the Senior Director of the Consumer Protection Team to drive some of our highest-impact projects. This is an exceptional opportunity for a gritty, entrepreneurial problem-solver with a genuine commitment to consumer impact, able to toggle between strategy and execution. Working closely with Strategy & Operations, Analytics, and customer-facing departments such as Product and Customer Success, this role will identify and quantify customer experience insights and pain points, collaborate on solutions, and build the customer-first system required to achieve our ambitious goals for the future. The ideal candidate must have a passion for customer impact, robust analytical toolkit, strong collaboration skills, and the tenacity to solve problems and drive prioritization through uncertainty. This role will provide frequent exposure to Flex’s Executive Team, giving hands-on experience with what it takes to lead and operate a world-class consumer fintech. The ideal candidate will be comfortable producing both rigorous data analysis and exec-ready deliverables from day one, working autonomously or together with your team.

This is a hybrid position with on-site expectations of 3 days per week in our New York Headquarters. For candidates outside of the NY/NJ area, you may be eligible for our relocation assistance program.

What you’ll do

• Build our strategy: Partner with your team leader (Senior Director of the Consumer Protection Team) to set strategy and translate it into tangible near-term goals and frameworks that ensure tight execution.

• Identify what matters: Apply your business knowledge and analytical skills to pinpoint the challenges that matter most, then partner with Analytics and Data Science to rapidly test new hypotheses and build lasting infrastructure around the insights you discover.

• Drive cross-functionally: Work with Product Managers and other functional leads to ensure we are effectively prioritizing customer experience priorities across the business.

• Influence the organization: Distill progress into executive-level reports, facilitating reviews to ensure the right strategic conversations are had. Communicate effectively with senior stakeholders, navigating complex problem sets with agility.

• Deliver with velocity: Manage a diverse portfolio of projects, adapting rapidly to shifting priorities. Operate at top-decile levels of speed and productivity, dealing constructively with pressure and debate.

Key qualifications

• 5+ years of relevant work experience, ideally in management consulting and/or S&O, Biz Ops, or Chief of Staff roles at high-growth companies

• Entrepreneurial mindset, energized by the ambiguity and pace of 0-to-1 building

• Thrive in fast-paced, dynamic environments and maintain composure amid competing priorities

• Exceptional conceptual thinker who can move fluidly from strategy to execution and make amorphous problems tractable (“fog sculpting”)

• Strong bias for action, paired with obsessive attention to detail and a high bar for work quality

• Well honed interpersonal skills; able to drive results through others without compromising relationships and rapport

• Excellent written and verbal communicator, able to distill complexity into clear, executive-ready narratives

• Exceptionally analytical, adept at identifying the right metrics and rigorously interrogating data, both independently and through others; SQL proficiency preferred, but not required

• Demonstrated AI fluency: you actively leverage AI tools to accelerate analysis, improve team workflows, and drive better decisions, and you set the standard for how your team uses them

• Genuine passion for “doing right” by our customers; we care about our mission, and you should, too!

Compensation

$184,000—$230,000 USD

$155,000—$195,000 USD

Building a successful company takes a diverse team of intelligent, curious, determined, empathetic, and self-aware people. Our headquarters is in New York City, with employees across the US, Australia, Canada, and South America. We’re growing quickly and deliberately, with a focus on building an inclusive culture. jobs.title: Associate AI Engineer
jobs.description:
About Fuel Cycle:

Fuel Cycle empowers leading organizations with agile research solutions that deliver decision-ready insights — fast, flexible, and fully integrated. As a market research disruptor, our AI-powered Insights Platform is built for speed, precision, and scale. With cutting-edge tools and seamless audience connectivity, we help brands ditch the guesswork and make smarter, customer-led decisions at lightning speed.

 

Why work at Fuel Cycle?

Join a high-growth team where curiosity is valued, ownership is encouraged, and your work drives real-world impact. Whether you’re based at our Los Angeles HQ, New York City hub, working remotely across the U.S., or part of our global team in India, you’ll help shape the future of decision intelligence for some of the world’s most iconic brands.

Overview:

Build real AI agents on a production platform, with senior engineers working alongside you. You will work in Python and FastAPI, build tool-calling agents on AWS Bedrock and AgentCore using the Strands Agents framework, and own technical decisions within the problems you take on, with your scope growing as you do. This role is fully in-office in Los Angeles because our mentorship model depends on it: pair programming, in-person code review, and a mentor a few desks away.

We hire for fundamentals, curiosity, and initiative. This is an early-career role. Engineers new to the field are welcome, and so are engineers with a year or two of experience who want to go deeper into AI and agentic systems. You do not need to know our stack on day one.

What You’ll Work On:

 - Design, build, and improve AI agents, deciding how tool-calling loops, model configuration, and multi-step workflows are structured using Strands Agents and AWS Bedrock

 - Build and integrate MCP tools and servers, and learn how tool names and descriptions shape what an LLM does

 - Deploy and run agents on Bedrock AgentCore, working with the platform team and your mentor

 - Build RAG pipelines over pgvector or FAISS, choosing chunking, embedding, and retrieval approaches based on what the results show

 - Design, test, and iterate on prompts; evaluate answer quality, latency, and token cost, and decide which tradeoffs to make; learn how guardrails are applied in production paths

 - Evaluate models, tools, and approaches, and recommend which to use, with your reasoning documented

 - Ship features and bug fixes in FastAPI services (REST and WebSocket APIs backed by PostgreSQL and Redis), deciding how to design, implement, and test them

 - Contribute to background jobs and queue consumers so agent work runs outside the API request path

 - Apply our architectural standards, use your judgment on design choices within them, help keep design documents current, and flag where the standards should change

 - Submit pull requests, respond to review feedback, and review teammates’ code as you grow

What You Bring:

 - Solid Python from coursework, internships, or work: functions, classes, type hints, error handling, testing basics

 - Data structures and algorithms, with awareness of time and space complexity

 - SQL fundamentals (joins, aggregations, indexes, schema design); PostgreSQL exposure preferred

 - REST and HTTP concepts, and how a web API is structured

 - Git and pull-request workflow

 - Clear communication, comfort asking questions, and a habit of picking up new tools and asking for help when you’re stuck

Preferred:

 - An agent project built with Strands Agents, LangChain, the OpenAI SDK, or a similar framework (coursework, personal, or professional), including how an LLM chooses and calls tools

 - Model Context Protocol (MCP): building or using MCP tools and servers

 - AWS Bedrock or Bedrock AgentCore, or AWS basics such as S3 and SQS

 - RAG: chunking, embeddings, and vector stores

 - Prompt engineering: writing, testing, and iterating on prompts

 - FastAPI or a similar framework such as Flask or Django, SQLAlchemy or another ORM, and a willingness to learn async Python

Experience:

 - Bachelor’s or Master’s in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience (bootcamp, self-taught, or on-the-job)

 - Roughly 0–2 years of software engineering experience; internships, research, and substantial projects count

 - A track record of learning quickly, shown through coursework, projects, work, open-source contributions, or community involvement

Benefits & Perks:

Fuel Cycle is committed to supporting the well-being, flexibility, and growth of our team. We offer a competitive and inclusive benefits package that includes:

 - Comprehensive Health Coverage: Medical, dental, and vision insurance plans

 - 401(k) with Company Match: Plan for your future with our retirement savings program

 - Equity Purchase Option: Participate in Fuel Cycle’s long-term success

 - Flexible Work Schedule: Empowering you to balance life and work

 - Generous Time Off:
   
   - 15 vacation days and 7 sick days per year
   
   - 12 company holidays
   
   - 4 floating holidays/recharge days to rest or celebrate what matters to you

 - Paid Parental Leave: Time to bond with your growing family

 - Monthly Internet & Phone Stipend: Support for remote work setup

 - Wellness & Lifestyle Perks: Access to tools like Rightway (healthcare navigation), Headspace (mental wellness), Peloton (fitness), and more

 - Team Connection Perks:
   
   - Weekly community lunches, refreshments, and snacks at our LA & NY headquarters

 

Compensation Overview:

The expected starting salary range for this position is $90,000 - $110,000. This range represents the typical starting compensation offered to candidates hired into this role. Final base salary will be determined based on a variety of factors, including location, work experience, skills, knowledge, education, and certifications.

In addition to base salary, this role is eligible for variable bonus, and may include an equity grant or purchase option. These components make up your total compensation package, which will be reviewed in greater detail during your initial recruiter conversation.

 

Commitment to Diversity, Equity, and Equal Opportunity:

At Fuel Cycle, we embrace the values of diversity, equity, and inclusion and are committed to fostering an inclusive company culture. We believe that everyone, regardless of their background or identity, should have equal access to opportunities for growth and advancement. Our selection processes and career pathways are designed to be fair, transparent, and free from bias. We value the unique perspectives and contributions of each team member, knowing that this diverse range of experiences strengthens our team. Fuel Cycle stands firmly against discrimination based on disability, sex, race, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, national origin, age, veteran status, or any other protected status under the law.

Fuel Cycle is an equal opportunity employer and fully comply with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). We will provide reasonable accommodations for qualified applicants and employees with disabilities, as needed, to enable them to perform the essential functions of their job and participate in the application and interview process. If you require accommodations during any part of the application process, please contact us at hr@fuelcycle.com to discuss your needs.

jobs.title: Abdominal Transplant Account Manager - PA
jobs.description:
CareDx is a leading precision medicine diagnostics company advancing care in transplant, specialty oncology, and cell therapy. Through our innovative portfolio of molecular diagnostics, digital health solutions, AI-powered data and analytics, and patient support services, we partner with healthcare providers, patients, and biopharma organizations to help inform clinical decision-making and improve patient outcomes.

At CareDx, every employee has the opportunity to contribute to innovations that help transform patient care and improve lives.

The Transplant Account Manager (TAM) is responsible for driving adoption and volume growth of the CareDx transplant diagnostics portfolio and ecosystem (www.caredx.com/products-and-services/transplant-services). Focusing primarily on abdominal programs in the transplant center and community nephrology account customers, the TAM will coordinate and collaborate with the Community Account Manager (CAM), Solutions Account Manager (SAM), Clinical Liaisons, and Medical Science Liaisons (MSL) to develop and execute account level growth strategies. Successful TAMs are collaborative, agile problem solvers with strategic account management and sales experience, possessing strong communication skills and clinical aptitude, taking a patient centric approach to delivering results. The TAM role reports directly to the Regional Director (RD).

Identify new business opportunities within existing accounts to upsell and cross-sell relevant CareDx products, solutions or services.

Strategic Planning and Executing Account Plans: Develop and execute strategic plans to drive business growth and achieve sales targets. Create and implement long-term, account-specific strategies and tactics to drive adoption, gain market share, expand the CareDx footprint and achieve commercial goals.

jobs.title: Sales Onboarding Program Manager
jobs.description:
Coder's Revenue Enablement team is building out onboarding and ramp for every customer-facing function — SDR, AE, SE, CSM, and FDE. We're looking for a Sales Onboarding Program Manager who can own that curriculum end to end: designing, running, and continuously improving how new hires ramp from day one to full productivity.

This isn't a single-audience onboarding role. You'll build ramp programs that flex across distinct functions with different skill requirements — commercial, technical, and delivery — while keeping a consistent bar for what "ready" looks like across all of them. You'll work closely with our technical enablement and sales performance functions to make sure ramp content stays current with product, methodology, and process as the company scales.



WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Design and own the onboarding curriculum and certification framework for new hires across AE, SE, CSM, and FDE roles

 - Build structured ramp timelines (30/60/90-day plans) with clear milestones, checkpoints, and certification gates for each function

 - Partner with technical enablement, sales performance, and functional leaders to keep ramp content aligned with current product, methodology (e.g., MEDDPIC, deal qualification frameworks), and sales/delivery process

 - Track and report on ramp metrics — time-to-productivity, certification completion, early performance indicators — and use that data to iterate on the program

 - Coordinate logistics and scheduling for cohort-based onboarding (live sessions, shadowing, certification exercises)

 - Build and maintain a scalable content/documentation system so onboarding materials stay current as the team grows and product evolves

 - Gather feedback from new hires and their managers to continuously refine the program

 - Serve as the primary point of contact for new hires during their ramp period




WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - 4+ years in program management, enablement, or L&D, ideally in a B2B SaaS or technical sales environment

 - Demonstrated ability to build structured, repeatable programs from scratch — not just run existing ones

 - Strong project management instincts: you default to milestones, checklists, and metrics rather than ad hoc coordination

 - Comfort designing curriculum for both commercial and technical audiences, or a fast learner's willingness to get conversant in technical sales motions

 - Excellent written communication — you'll be creating a lot of the source material new hires learn from

 - Experience partnering cross-functionally with sales, product, and marketing




ABOUT CODER

Coder is the leading platform for AI development Infrastructure, enabling enterprises to securely run human and AI-driven development workflows in consistent, governed environments. Coder provides self-hosted, agent-ready workspaces that unify developer productivity and platform governance. With Coder, enterprises can confidently evolve from human-only development to AI-assisted and autonomous workflows, without sacrificing security, compliance, or performance. Learn more at coder.com http://coder.com.




INTERVIEW PROCESS 

We believe that the interview process should be transparent, consistent, and enjoyable. We value your time and hope to complete the interview process in two to four weeks, if schedules allow.  Through your interviews, you will meet a mix of individual contributors, managers, and senior leaders. 




AI USE DURING THE INTERVIEW PROCESS

As an AI company, Coder embraces the use of AI tools, and we want to be transparent about our expectations as you navigate our interview process.  

Not permitted: Using AI assistance during conversational interviews.

Permitted: Using AI tooling for take-home assessments. Please flag where and to what extent it was used in your take-home. Your submission will not be penalized for using AI as long as it is done honestly.




OUR USE OF AI IN HIRING

We use AI tools to help manage our recruitment process efficiently and fairly. Specifically:

 - Ashby and Brainerr help us review inbound applications by surfacing candidates who best match the role requirements we've defined. This tool does not make hiring decisions; it helps our team prioritize which applications to review first.

 - Granola takes notes during our interview calls so our team can focus on the conversation with you.

All hiring decisions are made by humans. Our team reviews applications, conducts interviews, and makes final selections. AI tools assist us but never replace human judgment, and these practices are conducted in compliance with applicable data protection, AI governance, and labor laws. Your data is not used to train AI models.

In accordance with New York City Local Law 144, an independent bias audit has been conducted on "Automated Employment Decision Tools"; results are available for Ashby https://www.ashbyhq.com/downloadables/ashby-bias-audit-08-2024.pdf.

If you're applying for a role at Coder and have questions about how we use AI in our process, or if you'd like to request information about the data we collect, please contact careers@coder.com.

 


CODER IS A PROUD EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

We are committed to providing equal employment opportunities to qualified applicants and do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, pregnancy, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, national origin, age, marital status, genetic information, disability, protected veteran status or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.

Its open platform integrates with 650 software, data and consulting partners to power end-to-end investment operations across firms of all sizes and levels of complexity. Addepar supports clients worldwide with offices in New York City, Salt Lake City, São Paulo, London, Edinburgh, Geneva, Warsaw, Dubai, Pune and Singapore.

They are passionate about understanding our clients' needs, take a hands-on approach to solving problems, and work collaboratively with internal teams to take ownership of our clients' success.

• Prioritize and context-switch effectively to lead simultaneous projects, seeing each through to the finish line

• Identify and contribute to opportunities to improve our current processes and standard methodologies as the Addepar platform expands

• Connect with clients in a proactive, consultative, and professional manner

Who You Are

• Minimum 2+ years of professional experience working in finance, technology, and/or consulting

• A solution-oriented approach and a passion for problem-solving.

• Strong work ethic, proactive, and a high-contributing teammate

• Independent, adaptable, and can thrive in a fast-paced environment.

• Excellent communication, organizational, and time-management skills

• Experience programming in Python language and/or experience with project management is a plus

Addepar takes a market-based approach to pay. $74,000—$112,000 USD

Our Values

• Act Like an Owner - Think and operate with intention, purpose and care. Own outcomes.

• Build Together - Collaborate to unlock the best solutions. Deliver lasting value.

• Champion Our Clients - Exceed client expectations. Our clients’ success is our success.

• Drive Innovation - Be bold and unconstrained in problem solving. Transform the industry.

• Embrace Learning - Engage our community to broaden our perspective. Bring a growth mindset.

In addition to our core values, Addepar is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We seek to bring together diverse ideas, experiences, skill sets, perspectives, backgrounds and identities to drive innovative solutions. We commit to promoting a welcoming environment where inclusion and belonging are held as a shared responsibility.

We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation.

PHISHING SCAM WARNING: Addepar is among several companies recently made aware of a phishing scam involving con artists posing as hiring managers recruiting via email, text and social media. jobs.title: Senior Network Administrator (Palo Alto & Aruba)
jobs.description:

The company's products are powered by Coherent Distributed Networks (CDN™), empowering warfighters, commercial air operators, and border protection teams to act faster, adapt rapidly, and stay ahead of evolving threats.

CHAOS Industries was founded in 2022 and has raised a total of $1 billion in funding from leading investors, including 8VC, Accel, and Valor Equity Partners. The company is headquartered in Los Angeles, with offices in Washington, D.C., San Francisco, San Diego, Seattle, and London. For more information, please visit www.chaosinc.com.

Role Overview:

We are seeking a Senior Network Administrator to design, implement, secure, and sustain mission-critical network infrastructure supporting business operations. This role requires deep expertise in Palo Alto firewalls and Aruba networking solutions, along with the ability to operate in highly secure, performance-sensitive environments. jobs.title: Senior Field Engagment Manager
jobs.description:
SENIOR FIELD ENGAGEMENT MANAGER



You'll own Deployment's side of the rooms Firecrawl shows up in: the private dinners for the labs and companies we want to work with, the conferences where our buyers already are, and the hackathons and workshops where developers run the API for the first time. Operations runs the events. You run what they're for: you decide which accounts need to be in which room, get them there, hold your own technically once they arrive, and turn the conversations into qualified pipeline the pods can close. This is a pipeline seat that runs on events, not an events seat that reports on attendance. If you've done field marketing or developer relations, this is that job on the Deployment team, with a revenue scoreboard. You'll report to our VP of Deployment, and you're measured on the opportunities credited to you from the rooms you work, not on how many people showed up.

 

Salary Range: $174,000 to $235,000 USD/year OTE

Equity Range: Competitive equity. Details shared during the process.

Location: San Francisco, CA (SF HQ). On-site when you're not in the field. Travel up to 50 percent for events, with evenings when the room calls for it.

Job Type: Full-Time

Experience: 5+ years in roles that put you in rooms with developers (field or developer marketing, developer relations, community, solutions, or a technical seat with a pull toward the commercial side), or a body of work that makes the case. Either way, you can call an API and show someone what it did

Work Authorization: Open to candidates already authorized to work in the US. We also support H-1B transfers, F-1 OPT and STEM OPT, TN (Canada and Mexico), and E-3 (Australia). We’re not able to sponsor new H-1B visas for candidates outside the US.



About Firecrawl

Firecrawl is s a place for people who want to work at the frontier: an AI company building the infrastructure other AI companies run on, not one bolting AI onto an existing product. We move fast, go deep, and are building the tools superintelligence will rely on to gather data from the web. That library is called Alexandria, and it starts now.

In September 2026, we raised a $75M Series B led by Smash Capital, and we're spending it building the largest repository of knowledge in the world. We hit 8 figures in ARR in year one and more than doubled it in year two. We have 192k+ GitHub stars, putting us in the top 40 repositories of all time, and developers, agents, and category-defining AI companies build on us every day. Growth like this is rare, and we're just getting started.

We're a small team punching far above our weight, working out of SF HQ and our new Toronto Hub. Everyone here owns a real piece of the product and company, end to end, and runs it themselves. No hiding behind process or headcount.

 

Why This Role Exists

 

Firecrawl already has a field motion. We host curated dinners for AI researchers at model labs, run a monthly community series at SF HQ, and show up at the conferences our buyers attend. Operations owns that program as a whole: the calendar, the production, and the orchestration across teams. The pods, each owned by a Forward Deployed Engineer with a Deployment Growth Engineer building pipeline into it, close what the field produces.

 

This role is Deployment's seat in that system. It decides which accounts need to be in which rooms, curates the guest lists for the revenue rooms, holds the table technically, and owns the follow-through until the pod's FDE takes the deal. It sits outside the pods so it can serve all of them, and every deal it sources goes to the pod whose ICP the account is in.

 

The Deployment team is small and technical. Every teammate can run the product, read the code, and talk to a customer, and this seat is no exception. This is the first dedicated field seat. Start by owning Deployment's ask for one region, build the revenue side of the program, then lead it as we add pods and cities.

 

A Note On Pace

We operate at an absurd level of urgency because the window for what we're building won't stay open forever. If that excites you, keep reading. If it doesn't, no hard feelings, but this role probably isn't for you.

 


WHAT YOU'LL DO



Bring the Accounts to the Calendar

Each quarter, hand Operations the rooms Deployment needs: the ICPs and target accounts each one reaches, the format that fits them (a dinner, a workshop, a meeting block at a conference, a hackathon), and the credited-opportunity target behind it. Operations owns the calendar, the budget, and the production. You make the case for the rooms with pipeline math, and you work the ones they run.

Before an invitation goes out, every revenue room has a target list, a success metric, a teammate who owns the follow-up, and a conversion plan.

Curate the Room

Build the guest lists for the revenue rooms from the ICP map, the pods' target accounts, and the signup base, using the AI-assembled customer dossiers and the warehouse to find the right people, not just the right logos.

Run the invitation outreach in Firecrawl's voice through our outbound stack, and get replies to a yes. Hand Operations the list for registration and seating, and brief the teammates who'll be in the room on who's coming, what they're building, and why they matter.

Be Technical at the Table

Demo the API live: one request, one page, clean Markdown or structured data, in front of a researcher or a CTO. Run hands-on blocks at workshops and hackathons that take a developer from first Scrape to first Search.

Answer the first layer of technical questions yourself (JavaScript rendering, anti-bot, output formats, MCP) and know when to pull in an engineer.

Turn the Room into Pipeline

Run the pre, during, and post-event loop with the pods: account targeting before, introductions during, and follow-up within 48 hours after. Every conversation lands as a contact and an activity in the warehouse.

Hand each qualified deal to the FDE of the pod whose ICP the account is in, and stay on the thread until the FDE owns it. Operations owns the venue, the vendors, and the run of show. You own Deployment's side: who's in the room and what happens after.

Measure and Feed the Playbook

Report every revenue room on attendee quality, credited opportunities, pipeline created, and cost per credited opportunity. Run the pipeline half of the retro with Operations and change the next ask.

Write Deployment's half of the events playbook (guest curation, the pre and post loop, follow-through, measurement) into the playbook Operations keeps, and work with Product Marketing and Developer Experience on the talks and content that make a room worth attending.

How You're Measured

Credited opportunities from the rooms you work: a deal you sourced that the FDE of the account's pod took as owner. That handoff is the quality gate. Behind it: the pipeline and signings those deals produce, and what each credited opportunity cost to create. Not badge scans, not attendance.



 


WHO YOU ARE

Technically Fluent. You can read code, call the API, and show a developer what one request did to a page. You don't need to have been an engineer, but you need to be credible in a room full of them, and you need to want to learn the product to the level where you can demo it cold. Developer relations, developer marketing, a solutions seat, or a technical seat at an API-based company are all ways people get here.

You've Filled Rooms with Developers. Meetups, hackathons, dinners, workshops, a talk track at a conference: you've run them, not just attended them, and you can show what happened after.

Pipeline-Minded. You think of an event as a list of accounts with a plan, not a date on a calendar. You know what a qualified opportunity is and you're comfortable being measured on the ones the pods credit to you.

AI-Native. You use AI tools daily as core work infrastructure. Our GTM stack assembles customer dossiers, activity timelines, and usage data; you'll use them to research accounts, write invitations, and brief the room faster than anyone expects.

Taste, and Programs Others Can Run. You know the difference between a room that works and one that doesn't, and you notice which one you're in before the guests do. You've also turned a one-off that worked into a recurring program with a playbook someone else could run. That's the path from this seat to leading the function.

Urgency and Follow-Through. Same-day follow-up. The event ends when the last conversation is in the warehouse with a next step, not when the last guest leaves.

Clear Communicator. Invitations people answer, briefs teammates read, and a talk you'd sit through yourself.

Backgrounds That Often Do Well

 - Developer advocates who want a revenue scoreboard for the rooms they already fill.

 - Field or developer marketers from API-first or infrastructure companies who are done counting badge scans.

 - Community managers who built a recurring series developers kept coming back to.

 - Technical founders who ran their own dinner circuit and conference calendar to sell.

 - Solutions engineers and sales engineers who were always the one at the booth.

 

What We're NOT Looking For

Someone who wants to run the events program. Operations owns events end to end: the calendar, the production, and the orchestration across teams. You own Deployment's side of every room: who, why, and what happens after.

Badge-scan marketers. If your success metric is leads collected rather than opportunities credited, this isn't the fit.

Non-technical hosts. Rapport gets people to dinner. Relevance and technical credibility get them to a second meeting.

People who need a finished playbook. We're building the field program as we go. If you need an account list, a runbook, and a quarter already planned before you can start, you'll stall here.



Bonus Points

 - You've worked at an API-first or developer infrastructure company and marketed to engineers.

 - You've done developer relations or advocacy and have talks, workshops, or a hackathon you ran end to end to show for it.

 - You have a network in the SF AI and developer scene: labs, accelerators, meetup organizers, the people who decide who speaks where.

 - You've built or run web scraping, crawling, or RAG pipelines and can talk about JavaScript rendering, anti-bot, and Markdown for LLMs from experience.

 - You've used Firecrawl, or reached it through Claude Code, Cursor, or n8n.

 - You're comfortable with Luma, Missive, SmartLead, Slack, and reading a SQL query against a warehouse.

 - You've written a talk abstract that got accepted, or a workshop that sold out.
   
   

 
 


WHAT IS MEANS TO JOIN FIRECRAWL

Own Deployment's Side of the Field: Which accounts we put in rooms, and how we prove the rooms paid off, are yours.

High Impact: Every opportunity credited to you lands in a pod's book and moves the revenue number. No layers between you and the outcome.

Autonomy: Own your account list, your rooms, and your results. We care about outcomes, not hours.

Growth Path: Start as our first dedicated field hire, owning Deployment's ask for one region. Build the revenue side of the program, then lead it as we add pods and cities.




BENEFITS & PERKS

Available to all employees

 - Salary that makes sense: $160,000 to $220,000 USD/year OTE, based on impact, not tenure

 - Own a piece: Gain competitive equity in what you're helping build

 - Generous PTO: 15 days mandatory, anything after 24 days, just ask (holidays excluded). Take the time you need to recharge

 - Parental leave: 12 weeks fully paid, for all parents

 - Wellness stipend: $100 USD/month for the gym, therapy, massages, or whatever keeps you human

 - Learning & Development: Expense up to $1,000 USD/year toward anything that helps you grow professionally

 - Team offsites: A change of scenery, minus the trust falls

 - Sabbatical: 3 paid months off after 4 years, do something fun and new

 

Available to US-based full-time employees

 - Full coverage, no red tape: Medical, dental, and vision (100% for employees, 50% for partner and kids). No weird loopholes, just care that works

 - Life & Disability insurance: Employer-paid basic life and AD&D, short-term disability, and long-term disability. Coverage for life's curveballs

 - Virtual care and a health guide: Teladoc for the couch doctor visit, plus Rightway to answer coverage questions and fight billing errors for you

 - Mental health: Talkspace, therapy and psychiatry on your schedule

 - Fertility and family building: Carrot, covering you and your partner

 - EAP: Free confidential counseling, legal and financial consults, and online will prep through Guardian

 - 401(k) plan: Retirement might be a ways off, but future-you will thank you

 - Pre-tax benefits: HSA, FSA, and commuter benefits to help your wallet out a bit

 - Supplemental options: Extra life and AD&D, accident, critical illness, hospital indemnity, plus pet, legal, and identity protection through MetLife

 

Available to SF-based employees

 - SF HQ perks: Snacks, drinks, team lunches, intense ping pong, and peak startup energy

 - E-Bike transportation: A loaner electric bike to get you around the city, on us

 

Interview Process

 

Application Review: Send us your resume, two events you ran end to end (the goal, who was in the room, and what happened after), and a link to you speaking or demoing if you have one. We care about what you've done, not where you went to school.

 

Intro Chat (~25 min): A quick conversation to get to know each other before we go deep. We'll talk about what you've been running, what drew you to Firecrawl, and what you're looking for in your next role. Time for your questions too.

 

Field Program Interview (~55 min): We'll hand you a real quarter: the ICPs, a set of target accounts, the events calendar Operations is running, and a city. You'll make Deployment's ask into that calendar (which accounts need which rooms), curate one guest list, and walk us through the follow-through. Then you'll run one live Firecrawl request and tell us what it did. We're looking for account judgment, taste, technical credibility, and speed.

 

Founder Chat (~25 min): Culture, pace, ownership, and how you like to work. Time for your questions too.

 

Paid Work Trial (~40 Hours): Own Deployment's side of one real room with the team: curate the list, run the invitations, be at the table, and land the follow-through in the warehouse. Paid at a contractor rate. It's the truest signal for both sides. You see what the role actually feels like, and we see how you operate. We'll flex around your current commitments.

 

Decision: We move fast after the trial.

 

If you want to fill the rooms where Firecrawl's next customers meet us, and be the one they remember, this is your shot.

 

👉 Apply now.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager
jobs.description:
Rithum™ is the world’s most trusted commerce network, accelerating how brands, suppliers, and retailers work together to deliver seamless e-commerce experiences. We provide an unmatched platform for brands and retailers, enabling them to accelerate growth, optimize operations across channels, scale product offerings and enhance margins.

Today, more than 40,000 companies trust Rithum to grow their business across hundreds of channels, representing over $50 billion in annual GMV. Using our commerce, marketing, and delivery solutions, our customers create optimized consumer shopping journeys from beginning to end.

Overview

As a Senior Product Manager, you own the strategy, roadmap, and outcomes for a key product area within Rithum's commerce platform. You operate largely independently, tackle open-ended and ambiguous problems, and bring cross-functional teams together around a shared vision. You are expected to have deep expertise in your domain and leverage AI-powered capabilities to rapidly shape the next generation of commerce for the world's largest retailers and brands.

Responsibilities

• Be the owner of your product and drive the long-term vision for the world’s leading eCommerce platform, leveraging AI-first approaches to accelerate discovery, decision-making, and delivery.

• Synthesize qualitative inputs—including client interviews, support tickets, and survey feedback—using AI tools to identify themes, opportunity areas, and prioritization inputs that inform product strategy.

• Collaborate with engineering, product, and cross-functional teams to drive efficient business processes, improve team operations, and align client needs with internal objectives.

• Own and drive roadmap prioritization for your product area, making independent decisions on scope, sequencing, and trade-offs while incorporating AI-assisted insights and data exploration.

• Leverage AI tools to prototype and validate product concepts and workflows (e.g., user flows, wireframe descriptions, low-fidelity mocks) to de-risk ideas prior to engineering investment.

• Lead end-to-end product development & execution from concept to launch (e.g., PRDs, prioritization, client discussions, testing & QA, change management, client adoption/engagement, etc.), holding yourself and your cross-functional team accountable for high-quality, timely delivery.

• Use AI to accelerate product documentation workflows (PRDs, one-pagers, release notes) while exercising strong editorial judgment and maintaining product quality and clarity.

• Track development progress, report on status to stakeholders, and assist in managing product release cycles. Support product testing and validation to ensure high-quality releases and a seamless user experience.

• Be the voice and champion of our clients; triage incoming requests with urgency and follow-through and build relationships grounded in trust.

• Lead and influence stakeholders across functional teams of designers and engineers to ensure successful delivery at a fast velocity; ensuring high product validation and QA standards are met.

• Collaborate with stakeholders at all levels of the organization to gain buy-in and alignment on product strategies, goals and initiatives, balancing urgency and resource availability.

• Leverage AI-assisted data exploration and analysis (e.g., natural language querying, chart interpretation, anomaly identification) to support faster, evidence-based product decisions.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications

• 3+ years of proven product management experience within the SAAS industry with a complex enterprise level product, preferably in eCommerce or marketplace platforms

• Experience as a Product Manager working on AI‑powered products, AI workflows, or data & insights platforms

• Strong experience with the full product development lifecycle, including setting goals for your products, measuring the results, and quantifying the impact of features on the business

• Experience driving strategy and execution for complex, integrated software ecosystems, particularly with unifying multiple platforms

• Proven experience in supporting team-based projects, with a focus on ensuring alignment with project goals and contributing to technical teams.

• Experience using AI tools to synthesize qualitative research (e.g., client interviews, support tickets, survey feedback) into structured themes, opportunity areas, and/or prioritization inputs.

• Experience prototyping product concepts or workflows using AI tools (e.g., generating wireframe descriptions, user flows, or low-fidelity mockups via AI) to validate ideas before engineering investment.

• Proven use of AI to accelerate documentation workflows (PRDs, release notes, one pagers, etc.) while maintaining high quality and appropriate editorial judgment.

• Comfort using AI-assisted tools for data exploration and analysis (e.g., natural language querying of datasets, AI-generated chart interpretation, or anomaly identification) to support faster, evidence-based decisions.

• Strong ability to work with vendors and internal teams, ensuring effective communication with stakeholders for successful project delivery.

• Comfortable presenting product strategy and impact to stakeholders across all levels of the organization

• Analytically minded with proficiency in data-driven decision making and experience with product analytics tools

• Experience collaborating with large clients – our clients are some of the biggest in commerce

• Positive & growth-oriented mindset with a strong bias to action

• Strong and concise written & verbal communication skills with the ability impactfully tailor your communication to any audience

• Ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences

• Ability to work in fast-paced environments and manage multiple projects simultaneously

Preferred Qualifications

• Bachelors or Advanced degree

• 5+ years of product management experience

• PM experience at a top tech company or fast-growing startup preferably in eCommerce

• Intrapreneurial/founder mindset

• Experience working on a global product management team

Travel Required

Up to 10%

Other Duties

Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

What it’s like to work at Rithum

When you join Rithum, you can expect to work with smart risk-takers, courageous collaborators, and curious minds.

As part of the Rithum team, you are valued, supported, and included. Guided by a transparent culture and accessible, approachable leadership, we offer career opportunities aligned to your ambitions and talents. To ensure work and life balance works for you, we also offer an array of resources to support you and your families, including comprehensive benefits and wellness plans.

At Rithum you will:

• Achieve work-life balance through remote-first working conditions, generous time off, and wellness days.

• Receive industry-competitive compensation and total rewards benefits.

We believe in transparency and fairness in our compensation practices.

For this position, the expected base pay range is: $135,000-$200,000 per year.

This range represents the base pay for the role across all U.S. locations and is determined based on market data, internal equity, and experience. Final compensation may vary depending on geographic location, skills, and relevant experience.In addition to base pay, we offer a discretionary bonus for non-sales roles, a comprehensive benefits package, and, where applicable, sales incentives.

For this position, the expected discretionary bonus is 10% of the annual base salary.

Benefits

• Tuition assistance

All employment is decided on the basis of qualifications, merit, and business need.

We're committed to providing reasonable accommodations in accordance with the law for qualified applicants. If you require assistance during the interview process due to a medical condition or need support accessing our website or completing the application process, please reach out to us by completing the Accommodations Request Form. Your comfort and accessibility are important to us, and we're here to ensure a seamless experience as you explore opportunities with our team.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer - Cards
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA, New York, NY, Portland, OR, or Remote within Canada or United States
jobs.description:
As the story goes, in 1949 Frank McNamara finished dinner at a New York restaurant and found he'd left his wallet in another suit. His fix was a card that let members eat now and pay later. That card became Diners Club, widely credited as the first multipurpose charge card. It was a piece of cardboard and a promise: the restaurant trusted the card, the card trusted the member, and someone had to make sure the money actually moved.

More than seventy-five years later, the promise hasn't changed, but the machinery has. When a Mercury customer taps their card, the request goes from the merchant's terminal through an acquirer and a card network to us. In a fraction of a second, we check the balance, apply the customer's spend controls, screen for fraud and say yes or no. After that comes clearing, settlement, disputes and reporting, and every cent has to reconcile.

Cards are the way Mercury customers spend money. The Cards Integration team owns the whole Mercury card, not just the swipe: issuance, physical card shipping, spend controls, lifecycle management, authorization, money movement, settlement and reporting, and the infrastructure underneath. We're a full-stack team, and our job is to make the Mercury Debit and IO cards reliable, correct, useful, and innovative.

We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer who thinks deeply about systems architecture, cares about the customer experience, and will dive into any problem to move the team forward. We value high ownership, working in pairs and teams rather than alone, and attention to detail. Those matter when you run systems held to four nines of reliability, and everyone around you will care about them too.

In this role, you will

• Lead projects from idea to tech spec to implementation to launch, working with your PM, EM, tech lead, and teammates at each stage. When you lead a project, it's yours to see through.

• Learn how debit and credit cards actually work under the hood (authorization, clearing, settlement, disputes) and use that knowledge every day.

• Build features across the stack, from the card experiences customers use to the backend systems that move money.

• Help keep our operations excellent. Our systems are some of the most observable at Mercury, and with great observability comes great responsibility.

• Mentor other engineers and raise engineering quality through design reviews, code reviews, and collaboration.

• Work with product, design, operations, risk, compliance, sales, and many other teams.

You should

• Have strong full-stack experience, a product mindset, systems thinking, and a knack for getting things across the line.

• Have made architectural decisions on complex systems, and be able to explain your reasoning and the trade-offs.

• Be excited to put new features in customers' hands, and care just as much about keeping existing ones working like a charm.

• Care about correctness in systems where failure has real financial consequences.

• Communicate clearly, handle ambiguity well, and enjoy mentoring others.

• Be comfortable with our tech stack (Haskell and TypeScript) or be ready to learn.

• Bonus: experience in fintech, payments, or card issuing.

We encourage you to try our demo site if you're interested in applying for the role.

*Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.
