jobs.description:
At Zone 5 Technologies, we're redefining what's possible in unmanned aircraft systems. Our team of engineers and innovators is developing cutting-edge autonomous solutions that push the boundaries of UAS technology - solving complex challenges that matter.

We're building the future of UAS capabilities, and we're looking for exceptional talent to join us. If you're driven by hard problems, energized by rapid innovation, and ready to make an impact on next-generation flight systems, you belong here.

Role Summary

The UAV Avionics Assembler IV serves as the technical and process leader for avionics assembly operations, ensuring quality, efficiency, and consistency across production builds. Tasks and responsibilities expected for this role include those captured by lower role specific levels.

This role involves working closely with engineers, production technicians, and operations teams to support multiple programs and value streams.

Key Responsibilities

• Lead avionics assembly execution for a product line, program, or production cell.

• Own assembly sequencing, build standards, and workmanship consistency.

• Partner with manufacturing engineering on tooling, fixtures, and work instruction development.

• Support production readiness reviews, rate increases, and design transitions.

• Lead workmanship investigations and corrective action implementation.

• Train, coach, and support the avionics assembly team of all levels.

• Serve as a key interface between production, quality, and engineering teams.

Responsibilities (Level III)

• Build complex avionics assemblies and high-density wiring harnesses with minimal supervision.

• Execute first-article, prototype, or low-rate initial production builds.

• Interpret incomplete or ambiguous documentation and work with engineering to resolve issues.

• Perform detailed inspections and advanced continuity and isolation testing.

• Support root cause investigations related to assembly workmanship.

• Mentor and train Avionics Assembler I–II personnel.

• Provide feedback on manufacturability and assembly process improvements.

Responsibilities (Level II):

• Assemble avionics components, electromechanical assemblies, and wiring harnesses from engineering drawings and schematics.

• Perform wire terminations, connector installations, and harness routing to specification.

• Conduct continuity checks and basic functional testing.

• Identify and escalate non-conformances and workmanship issues.

• Maintain accurate as-built documentation and material traceability via MES.

• Adhere to AS9100, FAA, and internal quality requirements.

• Collaborate with quality and manufacturing engineering to resolve discrepancies.

Responsibilities (Level I):

• Assemble basic avionics components and sub-assemblies following work instructions and engineering drawings.

• Perform wire preparation tasks including cutting, stripping, crimping, and labeling.

• Assist with routing, dressing, and securing wiring in accordance with defined standards.

• Conduct visual inspections to identify obvious defects or workmanship issues.

• Use basic hand tools and test equipment such as multimeters under supervision.

• Accurately complete assembly work instructions and production documentation.

• Follow ESD, FOD, safety, and quality procedures at all times.

• Support senior assemblers and technicians as needed.

Qualifications:

• High school diploma (or equivalent) or technical degree with extensive aerospace experience.

• 7+ years of avionics or high-reliability electronics assembly experience.

• Demonstrated leadership without formal people management.

• Deep understanding of aerospace quality systems and production risk.

• Exceptionally strong attention to detail and manual dexterity.

jobs.title: HR Compensation Partner
jobs.description:

Job Summary:

The HR Compensation Partner plays a key role in supporting compensation programs, job architecture, and processes. This position combines hands-on compensation analysis with Workday administration, market benchmarking, job evaluation, and support of annual compensation programs.

Working closely with HR Business Partners, Talent Acquisition, business leaders, and other partners, this role provides practical, data-driven compensation guidance while helping maintain accurate and consistent compensation and job data within Workday. The position requires strong analytical skills, sound judgment, attention to detail, and the ability to independently manage assigned responsibilities while balancing multiple priorities.

The ideal candidate brings hands-on compensation experience, a solid understanding of compensation practices and market data, and the ability to quickly learn about the business, build effective stakeholder relationships, and deliver accurate, actionable results with limited day-to-day direction.

Compensation Analysis & Market Benchmarking

• Conduct independent market pricing of new and existing positions using external survey data, market resources, internal job architecture, and other relevant information

• Evaluate job descriptions to identify appropriate market matches, FLSA, and job level and support consistent benchmarking decisions.

• Develop data-driven recommendations for new hire offers, salary adjustments, promotions, and other compensation decisions.

• Participate in compensation surveys and assist with analyzing market trends and survey results.

Job Architecture & Workday Support

• Support job architecture and data validation initiatives by mapping employee groups to job profiles, developing validation templates and standardized job descriptions, and coordinating follow-ups with HR Partners and business leaders, while tracking outstanding items.

• Assist with testing and implementation of Workday compensation enhancements, configuration changes, and process improvements.

• Help maintain documentation and standards related to job architecture and compensation processes.

Annual Compensation Programs

• Support the annual merit and bonus review cycles from planning through completion.

• Assist with Workday compensation cycle preparation, testing, data validation, reporting, and troubleshooting.

• Develop tools, reports, job aids, guides, and other resources to support managers and HR partners during compensation cycles.

• Monitor compensation data and identify issues that require research or resolution.

• Support other compensation programs and initiatives throughout the year.

HR and Business Partnership

• Partner with HR Business Partners and business leaders to provide compensation guidance and translate compensation analysis into clear, practical recommendations that support informed business decisions.

• Respond to compensation inquiries and support the resolution of compensation matters.

• Communicate findings, recommendations, and potential risks to relevant stakeholders in a clear and professional manner.

Reporting, Data, and Process Improvement

• Support the annual merit and bonus review cycles from planning through completion.

• Assist with Workday compensation cycle preparation, testing, data validation, reporting, and troubleshooting.

• Develop tools, reports, job aids, guides, and other resources to support managers and HR partners during compensation cycles.

• Monitor compensation data and identify issues that require research or resolution.

• Support other compensation programs and initiatives throughout the year.

• Proficient in Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, and Excel, including experience with lookups, pivot tables, formulas, and data analysis

• Familiarity with Adobe Pro, SharePoint, and SmartSheet.

• Strong analytical skills and ability to translate data into practical recommendations.

• Excellent attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with HR partners, managers, and senior leaders.

• Ability to manage multiple priorities and work independently in a fast-paced, collaborative environment.

jobs.title: Housekeeping Coordinator
jobs.description:
The Housekeeping Coordinator provides administrative and communication support to the hotel’s housekeeping department. This role helps manage daily room-status information, staff assignments, guest requests, supply needs, and communication with other departments to support timely, consistent service. The Housekeeping Coordinator is responsible for overseeing daily housekeeping operations and ensuring all guest rooms and public areas meet established cleanliness and presentation standards. This role provides direct supervision, provide direction, and support to housekeeping staff, ensuring work is completed efficiently, safely, and in accordance with hotel policies. The Housekeeping Coordinator is accountable for maintaining quality standards, supporting team performance, and ensuring a consistent and positive guest experience.

• Answer and direct phone calls, emails, radio calls, and in-person inquiries.
• Communicate room-status changes and service requests between housekeeping, the front desk, maintenance, and other departments.
• Enter and update room, guest-request, and operational information in hotel systems.
• Record and follow up on guest requests, maintenance issues, room discrepancies, and lost-and-found items.
• Prepare daily work assignments, checklists, schedules, reports, and department notices.
• Assist with shift documentation, training records, and internal communications.
• Coordinate requests for housekeeping supplies, amenities, uniforms, and equipment.
• Maintain accurate, organized department files and protect confidential guest and employee information.
• Escalate urgent requests, service delays, safety concerns, and unresolved issues to the appropriate supervisor.
• Provide courteous, professional service to guests and hotel employees.
• Follow hotel policies, privacy procedures, and workplace health and safety requirements.
• Coordinate and direct housekeeping staff on a daily basis by assigning room sections, setting priorities, and monitoring progress to ensure all cleaning assignments are completed efficiently and in accordance with hotel standards.
• Provide ongoing coaching, guidance, and performance feedback to housekeeping team members to reinforce productivity standards, quality expectations, and proper cleaning procedures.
• Ensure consistent adherence to all housekeeping policies, procedures, and safety protocols, including proper handling and use of cleaning chemicals, equipment, and protective materials.
• Coordinate daily room status updates with the Front Desk to ensure accurate communication of clean, dirty, out-of-order, and inspected rooms, supporting efficient room turnover and guest check-in readiness.
• Proactively assist in planning the daily staffing levels and workload distribution based on occupancy, arrivals, departures, and operational priorities, adjusting assignments as needed throughout the shift.
• Address guest requests, service needs, and complaints related to housekeeping in a prompt, professional, and solution-oriented manner, ensuring follow-up and resolution to guest satisfaction.

• Experience in people management.

• History of developing constructive and cooperative working relationships with others and maintaining them over time.

• Proficient in MS Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and other business tools such as Microsoft Teams.

Compliance:

• Demonstrate knowledge of and carefully follow all applicable federal and state compliance requirements and regulations including those prescribed by the U.S. Department of Education, accrediting agencies, state regulations, and internal policies and procedures.

• Effectively communicate compliance requirements to other staff as appropriate and quickly escalate any compliance concerns to the Compliance department.

Work Environment/Physical Demands:

• This is a fully remote position.

• Home office set up, quiet place to work, and ability to hard wire into high-speed internet connection.

• May require setup of computer equipment, accommodation consideration available upon request.

• Flexibility to work evenings and weekends, as needed.

In addition to the compensation listed below, this position is bonus eligible.

Compensation Range

$75,400—$75,400 USD

OUR VALUES

Our institutional values are shaped and validated by our team members. They describe how we strive to operate and are the standards of behavior we look to embody.

ACT WITH INTEGRITY

We operate honestly and ethically in an industry-compliant fashion. We are fair and trustworthy in our interactions with all we serve. Our team members, at all levels, lead by example and strive to do the right thing for our students and for each other. We are disciplined professionals who strive to be straightforward and dependable.

CHAMPION STUDENT OUTCOMES

We live by a strong commitment to our students and are passionate about preparing them for meaningful careers. We are deeply dedicated to ensuring students’ educational and career success. We excel at building our students’ confidence and empowering them to reach their full potential.

COMMIT TO TEAM MEMBER SUCCESS

We are committed to our team members’ success and to each other’s success. We strive to create an environment that attracts and retains the best talent while offering continuous learning, professional development and career growth opportunities. We recognize and reward our team members for their contributions to the organization and to our students.

PURSUE RESULTS WITH PURPOSE

We pursue results with a sense of urgency and purpose. We take responsibility for achieving ambitious, measurable results and hold each other accountable. We think strategically and critically, greet new ideas and challenges openly, and look for innovative solutions to challenges.

HAVE FUN. BUILD ENERGY

Enjoying what we do is central to achieving our goals. Building energy, having fun, being optimistic and creating a positive working environment are all critical to our success and that of our students. We strive to be inspired and to inspire others. We consistently show appreciation and celebrate our successes, both large and small.

WORK AS ONE

We strive to build and maintain positive relationships with colleagues from all types of backgrounds by showing respect and humility when interacting with each other and resolving conflicts in a constructive manner. jobs.location: Boston - Massachusetts; Carmel - Indiana; Chicago - Illinois; Lambertville - New Jersey; Remote - USA; Water Street - New York
jobs.description:
At Real Chemistry, making the world a healthier place isn’t just an aspiration—it’s our everyday reality. Our drive to transform healthcare is informed by our blend of deep scientific expertise, human-centred creativity, and AI-driven insights, fostering a unique environment where innovation thrives and our people are impact-obsessed. As a global agency, we provide a full suite of services across healthcare communications and marketing to our clients, including top players in the pharmaceutical and biotech industries.

Our #LifeatRealChem culture is rooted in our people—we believe we are best together and are committed to excellence for both our clients and colleagues. Whether you're a seasoned professional or just starting your career, if you share our passion for healthcare and connection, we invite you to explore our opportunities.

Discover your purpose. Embrace innovation. Experience #LifeatRealChem.

21GRAMS, a Real Chemistry subsidiary, is an advertising agency born to make healthcare more human. Not just in our work, but in how we conduct business, approach client relationships, and treat each other. We believe in being good to each other and hard on the work, and in creating work that makes a meaningful difference for patients, caregivers, healthcare professionals, and brands.

Job Summary

The Director, Product Design is a senior design leader responsible for setting the product design vision, raising the quality of the work, and building the conditions for teams to deliver cohesive, accessible, and effective digital experiences. This role leads complex engagements across websites, platforms, products, services, and connected ecosystems, translating user needs, brand strategy, business goals, technology constraints, and healthcare requirements into clear experience direction.

This is not solely an execution role. The Director is accountable for design strategy, client leadership, team development, resourcing, design operations, and measurable experience outcomes. They remain close enough to the work to guide critical decisions, facilitate discovery, critique design, and step into high-impact moments while enabling senior designers to lead day to day.

What You Will Do

Design Vision and Product Strategy

• Own the product design vision and experience strategy across a portfolio of complex client engagements, connecting user needs, brand intent, business objectives, and technical feasibility.

• Partner with Experience Strategy, UX, Product Management, Creative, Technology, Data, Medical, Strategy, and Account leadership to frame opportunities, define roadmaps, and establish measurable outcomes.

• Lead discovery and definition activities, including stakeholder alignment, experience principles, journey framing, service blueprints, value propositions, prioritization, and product or platform planning.

• Identify opportunities that extend beyond the immediate brief and turn them into clear, decision-ready recommendations for clients and agency leadership.

Design Excellence and Delivery

• Set and uphold a high bar for interaction design, visual design, responsive behavior, content hierarchy, prototyping, motion, and end-to-end experience coherence.

• Guide teams from early concepts through detailed design, validation, launch, and optimization, ensuring that strategic intent is maintained through implementation.

• Oversee scalable design systems, component libraries, pattern governance, and documentation in Figma, working with engineering partners to improve quality and delivery efficiency.

• Build accessibility into the work from the start, applying WCAG 2.2 AA principles and inclusive design practices rather than treating compliance as a final review step.

• Use qualitative research, analytics, usability findings, and business measures to evaluate design decisions and recommend iteration.

Client and Cross-Functional Leadership

• Act as a trusted senior design partner to clients, clearly articulating experience strategy, design rationale, trade-offs, risks, and recommendations to executive and working teams.

• Lead high-stakes presentations, workshops, critiques, and decision-making sessions, creating alignment across internal and external stakeholders.

• Partner with project and account leadership on scope, staffing, schedules, assumptions, and change management; surface delivery risks early and propose practical solutions.

• Represent Product Design in new-business opportunities, estimates, proposals, capability presentations, and pitch work.

People Leadership and Practice Development

• Manage, coach, and develop product designers across levels through clear expectations, actionable feedback, growth plans, and regular career conversations.

• Create an environment where designers can do their best work, with strong critique, psychological safety, accountability, and thoughtful delegation.

• Partner with Experience leadership on hiring, staffing, performance management, succession planning, and capability development.

• Improve the Product Design practice through reusable methods, templates, standards, training, and responsible adoption of emerging tools, including AI-enabled workflows.

• Contribute to a culture of collaboration across Product Design, UX, Creative, Technology, and Strategy, reducing silos and improving continuity from concept through launch.

What Success Looks Like

• Clients see Product Design as a strategic partner, not only a production capability.

• Teams have clear experience direction, decision criteria, and an appropriate level of design leadership from discovery through delivery.

• Creates a more consistent, accessible, and high-quality experience across the portfolio.

• Designers receive strong coaching, understand what is expected of them, and demonstrate measurable growth.

• The practice becomes more scalable through better systems, methods, staffing decisions, and cross-functional ways of working.

• Experience recommendations connect to defined user, client, and business outcomes.

What You Should Have

• 10+ years of experience in product design, experience design, interaction design, or a related discipline, including 3+ years managing and developing designers.

• A portfolio demonstrating leadership across complex, multi-channel digital products or platforms, from strategy and concept through detailed design and launch.

• Experience leading multiple workstreams or a portfolio of client engagements in an agency, consultancy, product organization, or similarly complex environment.

• Deep fluency in human-centered design, interaction design, visual systems, prototyping, responsive design, information architecture, and design systems.

• Strong working knowledge of Figma and modern collaborative design workflows; familiarity with Adobe Creative Cloud and prototyping or motion tools is helpful.

• Practical knowledge of accessibility standards, including WCAG 2.2 AA, and the ability to guide teams in designing inclusive experiences.

• Demonstrated ability to partner with engineering, product, research, content, analytics, strategy, creative, and account teams.

• Excellent executive communication, facilitation, storytelling, critique, negotiation, and stakeholder-management skills.

• Experience defining design outcomes and using research, usability testing, analytics, and performance data to improve experiences.

• Comfort operating in ambiguity, making informed trade-offs, and balancing strategic leadership with hands-on guidance when the work requires it.

This Position Is a Strong Fit If

• You can move between the 30,000-foot view and the detail that determines whether an experience actually works.

• You are direct, low-ego, generous with feedback, and able to challenge the work while supporting the people doing it.

• You bring structure to ambiguity, anticipate needs, and help teams make better decisions faster.

• You care about craft, but judge success by the quality, usefulness, accessibility, and impact of the experience.

• Our Company values – Best Together, Impact-Obsessed, Excellence Expected, Evolve Always and Accountability with an “I” – really speak to you.

• You are adaptable, resilient, and OK with adjusting your scope, responsibilities, and focus as we grow. When things change, so do we. We’re always evolving.

• You are proactive, driven, and resourceful with strong prioritization skills and a desire to dive into the data.

• You are highly organized self-starter, able to work independently and under tight deadlines.

Preferred Experience

• Healthcare, pharmaceutical, patient support, medical technology, or other regulated-industry experience.

• Experience with privacy, consent, regulated content, and design considerations for patients, caregivers, and healthcare professionals.

• Experience supporting business development, scoping, estimating, and presenting capabilities or pitch work.

• Experience leading enterprise websites, authenticated platforms, service ecosystems, omnichannel programs, or AI-enabled experiences.

Pay Range: $140,000 - $155,000
This is the pay range the Company believes it will pay for this position at the time of this posting.  Consistent with applicable law, compensation will be determined based on job-related, non-discriminatory factors including but not limited to work experience, skills, certifications, and geographical location. The Company reserves the right to modify this pay range at any time.

jobs.title: Product Startup Founder
jobs.description:
About Formlabs:

To reinvent an industry, you have to build the best team. Join Formlabs if you want to help us build the tools that make it possible for anyone to bring their ideas to life.

Starting a company is the ultimate test of product-market fit, execution, and resilient leadership. If you're an ex-co-founder, seasoned tinkerer, or Product Leader at an early-stage startup looking for the ultimate platform to apply your experiences, Formlabs offers the infrastructure to build high-impact products without the bureaucratic drag of a large enterprise.

Your Impact:

New products usually fail because they cost too much to build or can't ship on time, not because the prototype didn't work. We're looking for operations leaders who think like founders. This posting isn't tied to one opening. If your background fits, we'll talk about where your experience can have the most impact across our operations teams and match you to a role.

Wherever you land, you'll run the work you own like a mini-CEO and build the manufacturing, supply chain, and fulfillment that let Formlabs products scale globally. We value bias for action, comfort with ambiguity, and deep ownership over outcomes.

We are seeking results-focused leaders/entrepreneurs who can quickly pivot and take charge.

What You’ll Do:

• Define Product Strategy & Vision: Act as the ultimate Product Owner, creating products and services that define the future of digital manufacturing by identifying unmet user needs and high-potential market gaps.

• Own Business Outcomes: Don't just manage projects—drive P&L results by identifying new market opportunities and scaling existing business units.

• Build & Lead: Create and lead multi-disciplinary teams of talented engineers, operators, and designers. Hire and mentor the next generation of Formlabs leaders.

• Take Decisive Action: Make crucial, high-stakes decisions that directly impact our core technology and business trajectory.

• Embrace the Ambiguity: Work at the intersection of complex disciplines (engineering, sales, manufacturing, marketing) and take full ownership to get the job done.

About You:

You are a tinkerer and/or an ex-co-founder who thrives on complexity and doesn't wait for permission. You get results.

• Proven Entrepreneurial Experience: You have previously built a business or significant venture (technology startup experience is ideal), demonstrating a high tolerance for risk and a bias for action.

• Comfort with Breadth: You have direct experience creating multi-disciplinary technology products and understand the full lifecycle from ideation to scale.

• Ownership & Hustle: You possess the "get it done" mindset—the hustle to do whatever it takes, whether it’s pitching a customer, setting up a supply chain, or debugging a prototype.

• Adaptive Leadership: You excel at both hiring and leading teams and are energized by a constantly changing, high-standard environment.

The standard is high, and the work is hard. Success here means you will be fundamentally changing digital manufacturing for designers, engineers, researchers, and artists everywhere.

Bonus Skills:

• Entrepreneurial experience like founding your own business.

• MBA or experience in a consulting role

• Familiarity with manufacturing, regulatory, or product standards and compliance in industries like healthcare, pharma, or life sciences.

• Experience with 3D printing technologies and materials.

• Familiarity with Tableau or SQL.

Our Benefits & Perks:

• Robust equity program to build future wealth through RSUs

• Comprehensive healthcare coverage (Medical, Dental, Vision)

• Low-cost fund options in our 401K and access to advisors

• Generous paid Parental Leave (up to 16 weeks)

• Tenure-based paid Sabbatical Leave (up to 6 weeks)

• Flexible Out of Office Plan – Take time when you need it

• Ample on-site parking & pre-tax commuter benefits

• Healthy on-site lunches, snacks, beverages, & treats

• Regularly sponsored professional development opportunities

• Many opt-in culture events across our diverse community

• And of course… unlimited 3D prints

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company.  We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

Even if you don't check every box, but see yourself contributing, please apply. Help us build an inclusive community that will change the face of 3D printing.

Compensation

Every Formlabs employee receives equity because everyone contributes to building the company. You’ll have the opportunity to share financially in the value we create together, with a shared incentive to build a business that succeeds over the long term. Equity will be a significant portion of your total compensation, and will increase over time in proportion to your impact. The base pay will be determined by your skills, qualifications, experience, location, and expected impact on the organization.

The annual base pay range for this role is:

$120,000—$250,000 USD

jobs.title: Embedded Software Engineer Intern - Winter 2027
jobs.description:
Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors https://www.skydio.com/solutions/energy-and-utilities to first responders https://www.skydio.com/solutions/public-safety, soldiers in battlefield scenarios https://www.skydio.com/solutions/national-security/tactical-isr, and beyond https://www.skydio.com/solutions.

About the role:

We are looking for interns for the Winter 2027 Season. Reliable embedded firmware acts as the brain stem of our autonomous drones and accessory products -- bridging the gap between the algorithms and the sensors/mechanical hardware. As an Embedded Software Engineering Intern, you will have the opportunity to help define and develop functionality for internal teams and/or current & future products in a collaborative, fast-paced environment.

An ideal intern candidate is a junior, senior, or MS-level college student with industry experience developing device-level embedded software or firmware.

About the team:
 Our team is responsible for large portions of the software engineering stack, working on a wide variety of subsystems. We write bare metal and RTOS microcontroller code (generally STM32 product line), integrate and write code for embedded linux and android platforms (Qualcomm and Nvidia SOCs), maintain the associated linux kernels, and help design and bring up all new electronics.

 - We work closely with both the hardware team and the rest of the software organization, creating the foundation for the rest of the Skydio software team to build upon.

How you'll make an impact:

 - Develop and implement the embedded software that runs on the drone and our growing accessory product lines e.g. Skydio Dock https://youtu.be/k8RRykNVL6E

 - Characterize, integrate, and validate key subsystems (e.g. cameras, radios, flight controllers)

 - Bring up and debug new hardware

 - Write interfaces and drivers for sensors, cameras, and other devices

What makes you a good fit:

 - Practical experience writing firmware/embedded code for a physical device

 - Proficiency with C++ within the context of embedded systems

 - Proficiency with Python for testing, experimentation, and tools development

 - Ability to write clean code with appropriate abstraction boundaries

 - Ability to read schematics and use standard debugging equipment: oscilloscope, logic analyzer, multimeter

 - Ownership in digging into complex problems

 - Bonus points for embedded linux userspace and kernel development

 - Bonus points for knowledge of debugging systems at ARM assembly code level
   
   Compensation Range: The hourly rate for this position is $47/hr for Undergrad, $53/hr for Graduate students, and $58 for PhD students*. Compensation will vary based on factors, including skill level, proficiencies, transferable knowledge, and experience.

Headquartered in Singapore, with more than 15,000 employees operating from offices around the world, SHEIN is committed to making the beauty of fashion accessible to all, promoting its industry-leading, on-demand production methodology, for a smarter, future-ready industry.

Position Summary

We’re seeking a full-time Senior Studio Producer (official title: Senior Studio Producer I) for our Los Angeles-based studio. The Producer is responsible for the day to day execution of casting and talent booking for high volume ecommerce photo productions. This role partners closely with the Production Manager, Studio Manager, Design Teams, modeling agencies, talent, HMU, and Studio teams to ensure casting, booking, and shoot-related details are confirmed, communicated, and production ready. The ideal candidate is highly organized, proactive, resourceful, and confident managing multiple bookings and shifting priorities. They bring strong industry relationships, excellent negotiation skills, and a deep understanding of commercial casting and talent trends

Major responsibilities:

• Serve as the primary APEX point of contact for assigned Eye Care brands, proactively identifying solutions to key business questions, and communicating insights to brand teams to influence decisions.
• Proactively identify and automate repetitive analyses and reporting, using AI and other tools to free capacity for higher-value insight work.
• Deliver the analytics and market research inputs to the annual brand planning process, including coordinating insights across the patient journey, market structure and standard of care from claims, awareness and usage tracking, and appropriate competitive intelligence, payer insights, etc.
• Lead custom market research projects, qualitative and quantitative, from design through reporting, managing suppliers, timelines, and budgets, and ensuring all research and vendor work aligns to company policy and data-access requirements.
• Identify sub-national drivers of brand performance across accounts, physicians, and distribution channels.
• Partner with the above-brand analytics team on promotional and marketing-mix evaluations, supplying brand and market context, interpreting results, and presenting implications and recommended actions to brand teams.

Required

• Bachelor's degree in a quantitative or business field (e.g., statistics, economics, engineering, business, public health).
• 5+ years of commercial insights and analytics experience, including prior pharmaceutical experience, translating data into business recommendations.
• Experience with primary market research (qualitative and quantitative), from design through reporting, including managing suppliers.
• Strong analytical reasoning, intellectual curiosity, business acumen, and creativity in problem-solving.
• Strong communication skills, with the ability to present insights and influence decisions in a matrixed organization.
• Strong project management and prioritization skills.

Preferred

jobs.description:
About Stitch Fix, Inc.

Stitch Fix (NASDAQ: SFIX) Stitch Fix is redefining retail by combining human creativity with advanced data science and Generative AI. As we build the future of personalized shopping, we’re equally committed to building yours.  We believe in investing in our team as much as our technology. Join us to be a trendsetter in the industry and help us redefine what’s possible for our clients, while we help you reach your full potential.

About the Role

The Women’s Private Brands team creates differentiated, brand-right products that deliver against the needs of our clients and the business. The Private Brands Design and Brand Lead brings this product vision to life from initial concept through physical execution, combining strong product instinct, trend and market expertise, and commercial acumen to create a compelling and successful product.

This highly hands-on role owns product decisions across the creation process, translating brand strategy, client insights, trends, and performance data into specific product opportunities. The Lead partners closely with Brand Management, Buying, Technical Design, Sourcing, Planning, and vendors to develop products that balances newness, commercial opportunity, quality, value, and client relevance. Using next-generation AI product creation tools alongside core product development systems, this role helps accelerate concept development, improve decision-making, and evolve how products are created across Women’s Private Brands.

Responsibilities:

• Own product creation from concept through final execution, translating seasonal strategy, client needs, trend insights, competitive intelligence, and business performance into differentiated products across silhouette, fabric, print, color, proportion, construction, and product details.

• Create and iterate product concepts using AI-enabled design tools, applying next-generation Ai Tools to product creation platforms to accelerate ideation, visualization, refinement, and communication while continuously learning and applying new technologies to improve the product creation process.

• Drive product development and make critical execution decisions, partnering with Technical Design, Sourcing, and vendors to translate 2D concepts into high-quality physical products and making informed trade-offs across fabric, trims, construction, fit, quality, cost, functionality, and scalability.

• Use commercial performance to inform future product decisions, regularly analyzing sales, client feedback, historical hindsight, and market trends to determine where to repeat, evolve, expand, improve, or exit product and to identify new opportunities for the assortment.

• Lead cross-functional product partnership and decision-making, working closely with Brand Management, Buying, Technical Design, Sourcing, Planning, and vendor partners to pitch product opportunities, incorporate feedback, solve problems, and move product forward with a high degree of ownership and autonomy.

About You

This is what you’ll need to succeed in this role from day 1:

Requirements:

• Deep women’s apparel product acumen with an exceptional eye for silhouette, proportion, fabric, construction, color, print, trend, quality, and product details.

• 5-7 years of experience spanning design, product development, merchandising, or a combination of these disciplines, with the ability to think both creatively and commercially.

• Strong understanding of the end-to-end apparel product creation process, from trend and concept through tech pack, sampling, fit, costing, development, and production.

• Ability to translate broad trends and brand direction into specific, commercially viable product ideas.

• Strong understanding of fabrics, trims, garment construction, fit, wash, finish, and manufacturing, with the ability to evaluate and improve physical products.

• Demonstrated ability to use sales data, client insights, and hindsight to inform future product decisions while continuing to push the assortment forward.

• Strong market awareness and curiosity, with an instinct for identifying emerging trends and determining what is relevant for a specific client and brand.

• Comfortable adopting emerging technology and AI-enabled workflows as an integral part of the creative and product development process.

• Excellent visual and verbal communication skills with the ability to present product ideas, influence cross-functional partners, and build alignment around a product vision.

• Highly collaborative, curious, hands-on, and comfortable operating in an environment where strategy and execution are deeply connected.

• Ability to manage multiple products and priorities simultaneously while maintaining exceptional attention to detail and product quality.

You’ll love working at Stitch Fix  because you will…

• Fuse human creativity and styling expertise to redefine personalized retail.

• Set a high bar for our craft and drive measurable impact across fashion, tech, and data science.

• Actively leverage AI and modern tech to evolve how work gets done.

• Lead with innovation, think boldly, and aren't afraid to challenge conventional retail norms.

• Win together in a collaborative, low-ego environment where diverse perspectives are celebrated.

• Be client obsessed by putting our customers at the heart of every decision to deliver unmatched personalization and trust.

• Support our team with competitive compensation packages, comprehensive benefits, and meaningful career growth.

Compensation and Benefits

This role will receive a competitive salary and benefits. The salary for US-based employees hired into this role will be aligned with the range below, which includes our three geographic areas. A variety of factors are considered when determining someone’s compensation–including a candidate’s professional background, experience, location, and performance. In addition, the position is eligible for medical, dental, vision, and other benefits. Applicants should apply via our internal or external careers site.

jobs.description:

Position Summary:
Analytic Services, Inc. (ANSER) is seeking a Budget & Finance Analyst to work in support of the Office of the Assistant Secretary of War for Nuclear Deterrence, Chemical, and Biological Defense, Policy and Programs OASW(NDCBD). In this key role, you will provide budgetary, programmatic, financial and resource management support to the OASW(NDCBD) in the oversight and integration of resources.

This position can support a hybrid work schedule with 3-4 days per week onsite at the Mark Center in Alexandria, VA and 1-2 days remotely.

Day to Day Responsibilities:

• Support the Planning, Programming, Budgeting and Execution (PPBE) process and integration across phases through Program Objective Memorandum (POM) development, budget exhibit reviews, and oversight of financial execution.

• Support OASW(NDCBD) oversight of Capability Portfolio Management into the development, prioritization and alignment of strategy to funding requirements.

• Assist in writing, editing, and justifying language in Research Development Test and Evaluation (RDT&E), Procurement, and Operations & Management (O&M) budget exhibits.

• Analyze financial and programmatic data related to operations business performance opportunities and investments.

• Provide programmatic, business, financial, and policy assessments to the OASW(NDCBD) for all resourcing requests.

• Provide support in planning for and managing the execution of budgetary resources.

• Perform program analysis and integration across the OASW(NDCBD) portfolio for resource requests and justification for RDT&E, Procurement, and O&M appropriations. Develop analytical products leveraging various tools such as the War Data Platform (WDP) and the Defense Agencies Initiative (DAI).

• Support input of OASW(NDCBD) resource information into Washington Headquarters Service (WHS), Cost Assessment & Program Evaluation (CAPE), and Comptroller databases.

• Support development of Congressional budget briefing products and support to engagements and requests for information from Office of Management and Budget (OMB), Congressional, CAPE, Comptroller, WHS, and Under Secretary of War for Acquisition and Sustainment (A&S) Business Operations staff.

• Maintain detailed knowledge of all statutory, Department of War (DoW), and Office of Management and Budget (OMB) financial management related regulations.

Required Qualifications:

• Possess an active Secret security clearance.

• Bachelor's degree in business, finance, accounting, economics, or other related field. Master’s degree may substitute for 3 years of experience.

• 8+ years of budget and financial analysis experience.

• Familiar with current DoW budgetary principles and their associated operational impact.

• Experience working with military components or other DoW agencies’ chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear (CBRN) or countering weapons of mass destruction (CWMD) activities budget.

• Experience in addressing RDT&E/Procurement/O&M budget issues.

• Experience with DoW appropriations and budget documents.

• Experience working with briefing and engaging General Officer/Flag Officer/Senior Executive Service (GO/FO/SES) level personnel.

• Experience working as an action officer at a headquarters staff/component command level.

• Knowledge of DoW programming, budgeting, financial processes and the DoW Financial Management Regulation (FMR).

• Experience developing budgetary and financial management policy and guidance.

• Experience with and knowledge of DoW financial management systems (e.g. WDP and DAI).

• Experience using the Microsoft Office suite particularly pivot tables within Excel, developing briefing material with PowerPoint, and creating guidance documents/action memos/info memos for GO/FO/SES level.

jobs.description:

Oura is seeking a Voice AI Lead to shape our Voice vision and turn it into experiences members can hear, trust, and use.Working within Audio Design, you’ll partner with Content Design, Engineering, and Product to define, implement, and scale Voice AI experiences across Oura. You will identify opportunities, prototype features, guide implementation, and build initial design, production, and evaluation practices that teams can reuse. You will also evaluate vendor voice models and recommend the right fit for Oura, balancing voice quality, technical constraints, product needs, and responsible AI.As a member of the Design team, you will collaborate with Audio Design, Interaction Design, Content Design, Product Design, Product Management, AI/ML, Engineering, Research, Brand, Legal, Partnerships, Privacy, Procurement, Localization, and Software and Hardware teams.

• Audition vendor voice models and design voice performance through scripts, pronunciation rules, and model settings; listen to and refine results across contexts and devices

• Partner with Content Design and Engineering to refine conversational behavior, including turn-taking, interruptions, mishearing, repair, and knowing when not to speak

• Establish voice quality criteria and review methods covering delivery, pronunciation, accessibility, safety, and intelligibility

• Partner with Legal, Privacy, and AI/ML on responsible AI voice guidelines

• Work with product teams across Oura to identify and prioritize Voice AI opportunities

• Translate voice design needs into requirements and acceptance criteria with AI/ML and Engineering, informing implementation without owning platform architecture

• Evaluate text-to-speech (TTS) and speech-to-speech (STS) providers and tools; recommend choices based on voice quality, technical constraints, product needs, and responsible AI requirements

• Drive vendor and voice talent workflows, assets, and approvals; partner with Localization on quality across languages and with Legal, Partnerships, Privacy, and Procurement on consent, usage rights, AI-cloning permissions, and data retention

This is a hybrid role out of our San Francisco office.

What you'll bring

• 8+ years of experience in relevant technologies.

• Working proficiency with audio editing tools (Pro Tools, Logic Pro, iZotope RX)

• Hands-on fluency with AI voice platforms, LLM tools, and prototyping and evaluation environments, including configuring models, iterating prompts, and comparing outputs

• Demonstrated experience independently leading complex voice or audio design initiatives from ambiguous problems through production and testing, resolving competing priorities and maintaining quality across teams, dependencies, vendors, and approvals

• Experience translating voice identity into practical design standards and production assets that other teams can use

• Familiarity with AI voice consent, likeness, cloning, training, data retention, and responsible AI practices

• Experience evaluating voice models and conducting quality and regression testing

• Technical fluency and the ability to translate creative and product needs into requirements, evaluate tradeoffs, and work effectively with AI/ML and Engineering

• Experience managing production or vendor budgets

At Ōura, we care about you and your well-being. Everyone here at Ōura has a ring of their own and we are continually looking to improve employee health.

jobs.title: Executive Director, Clinical Operations
jobs.description:
Spyre Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company committed to developing next-generation therapies that elevate the standard in immunology by delivering more complete disease control, greater durability, and a simpler treatment experience for patients. Spyre's pipeline includes investigational extended half-life antibodies targeting α4β7, TL1A, IL-23, and IL-17A/F as well as rational combination programs.

Role Summary:

The Executive Director, Clinical Operations, will provide strategic leadership and hands-on oversight of global clinical trials, ensuring trials are delivered within agreed timelines and budgets and meet quality standards and applicable regulatory requirements.

This individual will translate clinical development objectives into operational plans and lead trial execution from start-up through close-out. Responsibilities include trial planning, enrollment, site engagement, CRO and vendor oversight, budget management, risk mitigation, and operational readiness for key trial milestones.

The Executive Director will partner closely with Clinical Development and other functions, serve as a key point of contact for CROs and clinical investigators, and develop and mentor Clinical Operations personnel. Success requires sound judgment, accountability, and the ability to balance strategic leadership with hands-on execution in a growing biotechnology company.

Key Responsibilities:

• Lead the development and execution of clinical operational strategies and study plans aligned with clinical development priorities and corporate objectives. Oversee global clinical trial activities from feasibility and start-up through enrollment, trial conduct, database lock, and closeout.

• Establish and manage trial timelines, budgets, resource plans, and performance metrics; identify risks early, establish mitigation plans, and drive timely resolution of issues.

• Partner with Clinical Development and cross-functional colleagues to assess protocol feasibility and contribute operational input to protocols, informed consent forms, study plans, and other trial-related documents.

• Implementation and management of the clinical operational plans and programs in order to meet corporate goals and objectives.

• Lead CRO and vendor selection, contracting, governance, and performance oversight, ensuring clear responsibilities, effective communication, and accountability for deliverables.

• Oversee country and site feasibility, site selection, activation, monitoring, and closeout activities.

• Build effective relationships with clinical investigators and site teams to support trial execution, participant recruitment and retention, and timely issue resolution.

• Develop and oversee enrollment strategies along with Medical Affairs, monitor recruitment performance, and implement actions to address enrollment challenges.

• Partner with Data Management, Biometrics, Clinical Development, and other functions to support data quality, timely query resolution, database lock, and clinical trial reporting.

• Develop and manage study budgets, oversee contract and budget negotiations, and monitor forecasts, invoices, and payments in partnership with Finance and Legal.

• Partner with Quality to maintain inspection readiness, support audits and regulatory inspections, and ensure timely resolution of findings and implementation of corrective actions.

• Develop and maintain Clinical Operations SOPs, processes, and tools; provide training and drive improvements that support quality and efficient execution.

• Provide clear, actionable updates to senior leadership and Development Teams on study progress, budget performance, risks, and decisions requiring escalation.

• Lead, mentor, and develop Clinical Operations personnel, establishing clear expectations and fostering collaboration, ownership, and high-quality execution.

• Maintain current knowledge of relevant therapeutic areas, clinical trial practices, and applicable regulatory requirements.

• Regularly make presentations to senior staff members and participate in relevant Development Team meetings.

• Ensure familiarity with new developments in disease indications being studied as well as relevant guidelines and regulations pertaining to the conduct of clinical trials.

• Attend scientific and external training meetings as needed.

• Other clinical operations activities as required.

Ideal Candidate:

• Bachelor’s degree in a scientific, healthcare, or related discipline required; advanced degree preferred. A minimum of 10 years of global clinical research experience within the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry.

• Late-stage dermatology clinical trial experience is strongly preferred.

• Demonstrated success overseeing clinical trial planning, start-up, enrollment, monitoring, data cleaning, database lock, closeout, and clinical trial reporting.

• Experience leading CROs and other clinical service providers, including vendor selection, contract negotiation, governance, and performance management.

• Strong financial and operational management skills, including study budgeting, forecasting, resource planning, and risk management.

• Thorough understanding of Good Clinical Practice and applicable local and global clinical trial requirements, with experience supporting audits, regulatory inspections, and inspection readiness.

• Experience contributing to protocols, SOPs, clinical study reports, and regulatory submissions preferred.

• Demonstrated ability to lead and develop Clinical Operations personnel and guide cross-functional teams through influence.

• Excellent communication, interpersonal, and decision-making skills, including the ability to communicate complex issues and recommendations clearly to senior leadership.

• Ability to manage competing priorities, adapt to changing needs, and combine strategic thinking with hands-on execution in a growing organization.

What We Offer:

• Opportunity to work in a fast-paced, dynamic environment where you help shape the culture of our young company, contribute broadly to advance meaningful medicines, and learn quickly.

• Market competitive compensation and benefits package, including base salary, performance bonus, equity grant opportunities, health, welfare & retirement benefits.

• Unlimited PTO

• Two, one-week company-wide shutdowns each

• Commitment to provide professional development opportunities.

• Remote working environment with frequent in-person meetings to address complex problems and build relationships.

The expected salary range offer for this role is $285,000 to $310,000. Actual pay offered may vary depending on job related knowledge, experience, education, and geographic location.

As an equal opportunity employer, Spyre is committed to a diverse workforce. Employment decisions regarding recruitment and selection will be made without discrimination based on race, color, religion, national origin, gender, age, sexual orientation, physical or mental disability, genetic information or characteristic, gender identity and expression, veteran status, or other non-job-related characteristics or other prohibited grounds specified in applicable federal, state and local laws. We also embrace differences in experience and background, and welcome diversity of opinions and thought with active recruitment designed to create a stronger and better Spyre that is focused on developing life-changing products for patients.

Please also be aware that all job postings will be listed on our website at spyre.com/careers/.

jobs.title: Manager, IT Operations
jobs.description:
DO YOU LOVE KEEPING PEOPLE, OFFICES, AND GEAR RUNNING SMOOTHLY?

Then Jobber might be the place for you! We're looking for a Manager, IT Operations to be part of our Operations department.

Jobber exists to help people in small businesses be successful. We work with small home service businesses, like your local plumbers, painters, and landscapers, to transform the way service is delivered through technology. With Jobber they can quote, schedule, invoice, and collect payments from their customers while providing an easy and professional customer experience. Running a small business today isn't like it used to be—the way we consume and deliver service is changing rapidly, technology is evolving, and customers expect more. That's why we put the power and flexibility in their hands to run their businesses how, where, and when they want!

Our culture of transparency, inclusivity, collaboration, and innovation has been recognized by Great Place to Work, Canada's Most Admired Corporate Cultures, and more. Jobber has also been named on the Globe and Mail's Canada's Top Growing Companies list, and Deloitte Canada's Technology Fast 50™, Enterprise Fast 15, and Technology Fast 500™ lists. With an Executive team that has over thirty years of industry experience of leading the way, we've come a long way from our first customer in 2011—but we've just scratched the surface of what we want to accomplish for our customers https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EkfZmHrRLx4&list=PLoktA_D-2UEnxMLfCe93bANKXVXd2bdN8&index=24.

The Team:

The IT team is one of the most cross-functional teams at Jobber. We build the systems, offices, and processes that scale as we transform our industry.

Our mission is to support our entire team through technology and first-class customer service. We keep our systems ahead of the curve and are always finding better ways for Jobberinos to do their best work. That includes you: through dedicated feedback, regular 1:1s, and endless learning opportunities, we want to accelerate your career too!

The Role:

Reporting to the Director, IT & Operations, the Manager, IT Operations will lead the IT Coordinator team, the people every Jobberino turns to when a laptop won't boot, a meeting room won't connect, or a new hire needs to be ready on day one. You're a player/coach: close enough to the work to spot what's slow or broken, and experienced enough to fix the process instead of just the ticket.

We're growing fast, and we don't want our support team to grow at the same rate. Your mandate is to deliver a better experience to more Jobberinos without a matching increase in headcount. That means fixing root causes, making self-serve genuinely good, and putting automation and AI to work on repeatable tasks, so your team spends its time where a human matters most.

This role is based in our Edmonton or Vancouver office, 4 days a week, with about 10% travel to our other offices. Our offices are where much of this work happens: meeting rooms, new-hire setups, company-wide standup, and a steady flow of hardware coming in and going out. You'll be the person on the ground who makes sure it all just works, for Jobberinos in Edmonton, Toronto, Vancouver, and everywhere in between.

Your team owns three things: office and workplace experience, the help desk, and the hardware lifecycle. You make sure all three run well at the same time.

The Manager, IT Operations will:

 - Partner with the Employee Experience team to keep our offices running well, from meeting rooms and AV to new-hire onboarding days.

 - Own the technical side of company-wide standup and all-hands, so they run smoothly no matter which office is hosting or where people are joining from.

 - Coordinate with facilities, vendors, and building management on the IT side of office moves, expansions, and changes.

 - Lead the IT Coordinators who work the queue, as their point of escalation, coach, and the person who removes what's slowing them down.

 - Own the health of the help desk, including response and resolution times, ticket volume and trends, and the quality of the support experience.

 - Turn repeat tickets into fixes by finding the root cause and choosing the right remedy: a process change, a knowledge article, a self-serve flow, or an AI automation built with IT Engineering. Then measure whether it worked.

 - Treat the knowledge base as a product, since it's what both people and AI answer from.

 - Own the performance of our AI-assisted support channels: what they handle, how well, and when they hand off to a human.

 - Set and report on the service levels that matter, and use the data to decide where the team spends its time.

 - Make sure every Jobberino has the right tools, whether they're a new hire, returning from leave, a boomerang, a contractor, in office, hybrid, or remote.

 - Build a proactive hardware plan, working ahead of the hiring pipeline and using hiring data and automation to trigger provisioning, shipping, returns, and asset reconciliation.

 - Own inventory and asset tracking end to end, from purchase through deployment, repair, reassignment, and decommission.

 - Manage hardware vendors, shipping partners, and budget, and find the cost and time savings hiding in the current process.

 - Mentor and manage the IT Coordinator team by setting clear expectations, giving regular feedback, and growing people into the next step of their careers.

 - Partner with the Director, IT & Operations and the Manager, IT Engineering on IT strategy, priorities, and where the work should live.

 - Redesign how the team works as automation takes on more of the queue, growing coordinators into builders, analysts, and experienced owners, not just ticket-closers.

 - Share system administration responsibilities with IT Engineering across tools like Okta, Jira, Google Workspace, Jamf, Slack, and Zoom.

To be successful, you should have:

 - Experience running a help desk, including ITSM and ITIL best practices, Jira, queue management, SLAs, and turning ticket data into decisions.

 - Experience leading a support team, including coaching people and holding them accountable through difficult conversations. You're a player/coach who sets direction and can still get your hands dirty when needed.

 - Hands-on experience with hardware procurement, inventory, and lifecycle management, including shipping to remote and hybrid employees.

 - Experience with office-based IT and AV support, including meeting rooms and large-audience live events like all-hands.

 - Comfort with our tech stack, such as Okta, Jira/Confluence, Google Workspace, Jamf, and Slack, plus automation tools like Zapier, n8n, or Okta Workflows.

 - Excellent communication skills, and experience partnering with People, Finance, and Security.

 - Openness and enthusiasm to play a major role in our shift to an AI-enabled service desk. You don't need to have done it before.

 - The ability to be a visible, approachable presence in our Edmonton or Vancouver office 4 days a week, and to travel about 10% of the time to our offices in Vancouver, Edmonton, Toronto, and Kitchener-Waterloo.

It would be really great (but not a deal-breaker!) if you had:

 - Experience in a growing SaaS company.

 - Experience with macOS and Apple hardware at scale, Google Workspace, and cloud-based MDMs like Jamf.

 - Experience with vendor negotiation and IT budgeting.

 - Experience supporting a company through an office move, expansion, or major growth phase.

Compensation:

At Jobber, we believe that compensation should be transparent, fair, and reflective of your experience and growth. This role has a minimum annual salary of $120,870, a midpoint of $142,200, and a maximum salary of $163,530, designed to show the progression from learning the ropes to truly excelling.

We design our compensation to reflect each new hire's skills, experience against the complexity of the role, ensuring a fair and competitive salary. Our range is intentionally broad to support growth and long-term impact, with fully established hires typically starting around the midpoint. The higher end of the range is reserved for those who have demonstrated deep expertise and lasting contributions, while offers below the midpoint reflect strong potential with room to develop. This approach ensures that compensation aligns with both an individual's current capabilities and their opportunity for future growth.

Base salary is just one part of a total compensation package that will include equity rewards, annual stipends for health and wellness, retirement savings matching, and an extended health package with fully paid premiums for body and mind. Your professional growth matters to us too! You'll have access to a dedicated talent development program that includes career coaching and opportunities for career development.

We believe in transparency and open conversations about compensation. If you have any questions about our approach, we're happy to discuss them throughout the hiring process!

Location:

We believe great collaboration is intentional, and sometimes that means coming together in person to build, brainstorm, and connect. To support this, the role is open to candidates based in one of our hub cities: Edmonton or Vancouver. This role includes about 10% travel to our offices in Vancouver, Edmonton, Toronto, and Kitchener-Waterloo.



What you can expect from Jobber:

 - A total compensation package that includes an extended health benefits package with fully paid premiums for both body and mind, matching in RRSP, TFSA or FHSA, and stock options.

 - A dedicated Talent Development team and access to coaching, learning, and leadership programs to help you grow your career, reach your goals, and unlock your full potential.

 - A unique opportunity to build, grow, and leave your impact on a $400-billion industry that has no dominant player...yet.

 - To work with a group of people who are humble, supportive, and give a sh*t about our customers.

We believe that diverse teams perform better and that fostering an inclusive work environment is a key part of growing a successful team. We welcome people of diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we are committed to working with applicants requesting accommodation at any stage of the hiring process.



A bit more about us:

Job by job, we’re transforming the way service is delivered. Your lawn care provider, home cleaning service, plumber or painter could use Jobber to better connect with their customers, save time in the office, invoice faster, and get paid! We’re bringing tens of thousands of people together with technology to deliver billions of dollars a year in services to happy customers. Jobber exists to help make these small businesses successful, and when they’re successful we all win!

The Director of Finance partners closely with the Senior Director of Finance and the Hotel General Manager to ensure sound financial management, operational excellence, regulatory compliance, and the achievement of the hotels' financial objectives. This position reports to the Senior Director of Finance.

The salary range for this position is $170,000 to $200,000. Actual pay will be dependent on budget and experience; all our salaried roles are eligible for bonus.

jobs.title: Partnerships - Private Equity
jobs.description:
ABOUT ELEVENLABS

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

 - ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

 - ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

 - ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.




HOW WE WORK

 - High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

 - Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

 - AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

 - Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

 - Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.




WHAT WE OFFER

 - Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

 - Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

 - Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

 - Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

 - Annual company offsite: Each year, we bring the entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia and Italy.

 - Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.


ABOUT THE ROLE

As the PE & Growth Investor Partnerships at ElevenLabs, you will build and scale one of our most strategic growth channels. You will own relationships with leading PE & Growth Investor firms, embed ElevenLabs into their Enterprise Value Creation programs, and drive AI adoption across portfolio companies.

Operating at the intersection of PE, Growth Investors, enterprise AI, & GTM, you will  partner with Operating Partners, Value Creation teams, portfolio executives, and our Sales organization to source, accelerate, and close opportunities. You’ll work closely with the Global Head of BD & Partnerships & all regional GTM leads to define the strategy while owning execution across multiple PE & Growth Investor relationships.

Your success will be measured by your ability to build a scalable investor partner ecosystem that consistently generates enterprise pipeline and ARR.




WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

In your first 6 - 9 months, you will:

 - Launch the ElevenLabs Private Equity & Growth Investor Partner Program.

 - Recruit and activate 8–10 leading PE and growth investor partners, securing ElevenLabs’ inclusion in their Value Creation and portfolio engagement programs.

 - Build a repeatable GTM engagement model between investor operating teams and ElevenLabs to accelerate portfolio company adoption, pipeline generation, and deal velocity.

 - Establish a foundation for a scalable, partner-sourced ARR business.





RESPONSIBILITIES




PRIVATE EQUITY & GROWTH INVESTOR PARTNERSHIPS

 - Build and manage executive relationships with Operating Partners, Value Creation leaders, and investment professionals across leading PE & Growth investor firms.

 - Structure and negotiate partnership agreements, joint GTM plans, referral models, and enterprise value programs.

 - Become the trusted AI partner for PE firms looking to accelerate value creation across their portfolio.


PORTFOLIO COMPANY ACTIVATION

 - Identify high-priority portfolio companies and develop joint account plans with PE operating teams.

 - Coordinate with Enterprise AEs, FDEs, Customer Success, and Product to drive AI deployments from initial introduction through production.

 - Help portfolio companies identify high-value AI use cases and accelerate adoption.


PIPELINE & REVENUE

 - Own pipeline generation and ARR sourced through PE partnerships.

 - Build and maintain a rolling portfolio company pipeline across assigned sponsors.

 - Drive executive introductions, accelerate deal velocity, and expand successful deployments across additional portfolio companies.


CROSS-FUNCTIONAL LEADERSHIP

 - Partner closely with Sales, Solutions Engineering, Product, Marketing, Legal, and Customer Success to execute PE opportunities.

 - Develop repeatable GTM playbooks, executive engagement models, and portfolio-wide AI adoption frameworks.

 - Represent ElevenLabs at PE conferences, operating partner forums, and executive events.




YOU MAY BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU

 - Have 8–12+ years of experience in Enterprise AI, Cloud, or enterprise software, with a focus on strategic partnerships involving Private Equity and Growth Investors.

 - Have experience working with PE firms, Growth Investors, Operating Partners, Value Creation teams, or PE-backed portfolio companies.

 - Have a track record of building strategic partnerships that generate measurable pipeline and revenue.

 - Have strong executive presence and can engage credibly with Managing Partners, Operating Partners, CEOs, CIOs, CTOs, and investment professionals.

 - Have successfully navigated complex enterprise sales cycles involving multiple internal and external stakeholders.

 - Are comfortable discussing AI platforms and enterprise technology with both business and technical audiences.

 - Thrive in fast-paced, ambiguous environments and enjoy building new partnership motions from the ground up.

 - Are highly commercial, operate with urgency, and consistently create opportunities where none previously existed.




LOCATION

This role is remote-first but NYC or London is preferred.

We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability or other legally protected statuses.
