jobs.title: Social Media Senior Associate
jobs.description:
THE POSITION
Our roster has an opening with your name on it

The Social Media Senior Associate will play an important role in executing and advancing FanDuel’s organic social strategy and helping shape how the brand shows up across key social platforms. This role will support the development and execution of social-first, video-forward content that strengthens brand relevance, grows and engages our audiences, and supports key business priorities.

The Senior Associate will help manage social channels, develop and publish content, identify real-time opportunities, support talent and creator integrations, and use performance insights to continuously improve our approach. This role will work closely with Brand, Creative, Partnerships, Talent, Editorial, Go-to-Market, and other cross-functional teams to bring FanDuel’s social strategy to life.

We’re seeking a creative, culturally connected, and highly engaged social marketer who understands what makes audiences stop, watch, engage, and share. The ideal candidate has strong knowledge of social platforms, sports and internet culture, an audience-first mindset, and the ability to turn trends and conversations into relevant opportunities for FanDuel.

They should be comfortable independently managing day-to-day social responsibilities, contributing ideas and recommendations, using data to inform decisions, and jumping into fast-moving sports and cultural moments.

In addition to the specific responsibilities outlined above, employees may be required to perform other such duties as assigned by the Company. This ensures operational flexibility and allows the Company to meet evolving business needs.

THE GAME PLAN
Everyone on our team has a part to play

• Execute FanDuel’s organic social strategy across key platforms, helping bring channel strategies, content priorities, campaigns, and audience goals to life.

• Manage day-to-day publishing and content execution across multiple social channels, with an emphasis on video-first storytelling, platform-native content, and emerging formats that drive reach and engagement.

• Develop and pitch timely, culturally relevant and distinctive social content that strengthens FanDuel’s connection with sports fans and customers.

• Identify and react to real-time sports, entertainment, cultural, and platform moments where FanDuel can authentically participate in the conversation.

• Help manage editorial calendars and publishing operations, ensuring content, assets, approvals, scheduling, and execution are accurate and timely.

• Write and edit engaging, platform-native social copy across brand storytelling, product marketing, promotional campaigns, partnerships, talent, video, and real-time sports coverage.

• Partner with Go-to-Market, Brand, Creative, Editorial, Partnerships, Talent, Product, and other stakeholders to translate business priorities into compelling social-first content.

• Support organic social plans for major launches, campaigns, and tentpole moments, helping develop and execute content before, during, and after key events.

• Work with FanDuel talent, creators, athletes, influencers, and partners to develop engaging content that extends FanDuel’s storytelling and creates authentic connections with audiences.

• Stay closely connected to social platforms and emerging trends, identifying new features, formats, behaviors, and content opportunities that FanDuel can test.

• Monitor social and content performance, using data and audience insights to identify learnings and recommend ways to improve future content.

• Regularly test new creative formats, platform features, posting strategies, and audience engagement tactics to identify opportunities for growth.

• Monitor competitors, sports media brands, creators, and broader internet culture to identify trends and opportunities relevant to FanDuel.

• Bring forward social platform expertise, audience insights, competitive learnings, and creative recommendations to help continuously evolve FanDuel’s organic social presence.

• Collaborate closely with other members of the social team, contributing ideas, sharing learnings, and helping maintain a high standard of execution across FanDuel’s channels.

THE STATS
What we're looking for in our next teammate

• 3+ years of professional social media, editorial, sports media, digital content, or related experience preferred.

• Experience managing or posting for a league, team, brand, publisher, media outlet, or similar organization across platforms including X, Instagram, TikTok, and Facebook.

• Strong understanding of social-first content and what works across different platforms, particularly short-form video.

• Strong knowledge of sports, sports betting, internet culture, social trends, and the conversations that matter to sports fans.

• Ability to identify and act on real-time social opportunities with strong creative judgment and minimal guidance.

• Strong social copywriting skills with the ability to adapt voice and tone across platforms, audiences, and content types.

• Experience with basic social video clipping and editing; familiarity with Photoshop or other creative tools is preferred.

• Ability to interpret basic social performance metrics and use insights to inform content decisions.

• Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities, deadlines, and stakeholders in a fast-paced environment.

• Strong grammar skills and meticulous attention to detail.

• Collaborative mindset and ability to work effectively with creative, editorial, marketing, talent, partnerships, and other cross-functional teams.

• Must be willing to work nights, weekends, and holidays as dictated by the sports and FanDuel calendar.

ABOUT FANDUEL

FanDuel Group is the premier mobile gaming company in the United States and Canada. FanDuel Group consists of a portfolio of leading brands across mobile wagering including: America’s #1 Sportsbook, FanDuel Sportsbook; its leading iGaming platform, FanDuel Casino; the industry’s unquestioned leader in horse racing and advance-deposit wagering, FanDuel Racing; and its daily fantasy sports product.

In addition, FanDuel Group operates FanDuel TV, its broadly distributed linear cable television network and FanDuel TV+, its leading direct-to-consumer OTT platform. FanDuel Group has a presence across all 50 states, Canada, and Puerto Rico.

The company is based in New York with US offices in Los Angeles, Atlanta, and Jersey City, as well as global offices in Canada and Scotland. The company’s affiliates have offices worldwide, including in Ireland, Portugal, Romania, and Australia.

FanDuel Group is a subsidiary of Flutter Entertainment, the world's largest sports betting and gaming operator with a portfolio of globally recognized brands and traded on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE: FLUT).

PLAYER BENEFITS
We treat our team right

We offer amazing benefits above and beyond the basics. We have an array of health plans to choose from (some as low as $0 per paycheck) that include programs for fertility and family planning, mental health support, and fitness benefits. We offer generous paid time off (PTO & sick leave), annual bonus and long-term incentive opportunities (based on performance), 401k with up to a 5% match, commuter benefits, pet insurance, and more - check out all our benefits here: FanDuel Total Rewards. *Benefits differ across location, role, and level.

jobs.description:

jobs.description:
Datavant is the data collaboration platform trusted for healthcare. Guided by our mission to make the world’s health data secure, accessible and actionable, we provide critical data solutions for organizations across the healthcare ecosystem - including providers, health plans, researchers, and life sciences companies. From fulfilling a single patient’s request for their medical records to powering the AI revolution in healthcare, Datavanters are building the future of how data is connected and used to improve health.

The ideal candidate for this role possesses high attention to detail and a depth of knowledge in medical terminology. • Assign the appropriate discharge disposition.

• Proficiency with most or all of these coding specialties (Ancillary, Emergency Department, Injections/Infusions, E/M leveling)

jobs.title: Channel Account Manager, DIB/MSSP
jobs.description:
Hypori, Inc. is a high-growth cybersecurity SaaS company transforming how organizations think about secure mobility. Our virtual workspace platform enables users to access enterprise apps and data from any mobile device—with zero data on the endpoint and total personal privacy. Backed by $55M in funding from investors including UBS, AE Industrial Partners, Hale Capital Partners, and GreatPoint Ventures, Hypori is expanding into new commercial and regulated markets. Learn more at hypori.com.

Hypori is looking for a builder-minded Channel Account Manager to join our growing commercial sales team. You will recruit, enable, and drive revenue through the MSSPs, MSPs, RPOs, and C3PAOs that serve small and mid-size defense contractors, building partners who sell, deploy, and support Hypori on their own. You will report to the VP of Commercial Sales.

More than 100,000 companies sit in the Defense Industrial Base, and most buy security from the partner that runs their IT. Hypori gives those partners a proven answer: more than 95,000 Department of War users are on the platform today, and we hold IL5, FedRAMP High, NIAP Common Criteria, NSA CSfC, CMMC 2.0 Level 2, and SOC 2 Type II, so it clears review with defense clients. The DIB partner program is being built from scratch, and the person in this seat builds it.

Responsibilities

• Own an annual target for new MSSP, MSP, RPO, and C3PAO partners serving defense contractors

• Source partners through outbound, the CMMC practitioner community, and events including CMMC CON, AFCEA small business forums, and Hypori CMMC Accelerate

• Understand the partner’s why first: why add Hypori, why now for their clients, what it does for their practice and margin, and why not stick with the status quo

• Qualify partners on DIB client base, CUI exposure, GCC High or enclave practice, and willingness to sell, then negotiate and sign agreements across referral, co-sell, and resell tiers

• Take every new partner to first transaction on a defined timeline, and move partners from referral to selling on their own as an extension of Hypori

• Build and run the partner certification path with the channel sales engineer

• Get partner sellers ready to position isolation and defend the scope reduction argument to their clients

• Own partner content, deal registration, the partner portal, and the enablement calendar

• Carry a partner-sourced and partner-influenced revenue number and forecast it accurately in Salesforce

• Run joint business plans and quarterly business reviews with top partners, and co-sell into partner client bases with Hypori account executives and sales engineers

• Work with Carahsoft, our distributor, on distribution and procurement paths, including opportunities under 100 licenses, and with Marketing on campaigns, co-branded content, and events

• Report monthly on recruitment, time to first transaction, pipeline, and revenue by tier

• Over time, help stand up the foundation for a broader security reseller and solution provider channel

Qualifications

• 5+ years in channel sales or partner management at a cybersecurity, infrastructure, or SaaS vendor

• Experience building a DIB-focused MSP or MSSP partner program, not just managing an existing one

• A track record of recruiting and activating MSP or MSSP partners from signature to first transaction and beyond

• Working relationships across the MSP, MSSP, or CMMC practitioner ecosystem serving the DIB

• Working knowledge of CMMC 2.0 and NIST SP 800-171: CUI vs. FCI, the 5 asset categories, SPRS scoring, and DFARS 7012 obligations

• Experience carrying and hitting a partner-sourced or partner-influenced revenue number

• Experience building your own enablement material, and familiarity with deal registration, partner portals, and margin structures

• Strong Salesforce and pipeline hygiene

• Location: Remote, United States, with travel up to 40 percent to partner sites and industry events

Who You Are

• Speed: You move with urgency and get things done today, not next week

• Focus: You spend your time on the partners who will actually sell

• Extreme ownership: Your program, your partners, your number. No excuses

• Accountability: You do what you say, when you say. You flag slips early

• Coachability: You ask for feedback, act on it, and get better

• Humility: You know what you don’t know, and you say so

• Creativity: You find new ways to recruit partners and get them selling

Preferred Attributes

• Technical credibility: Partners only carry products their engineers and compliance leads believe in. You will have a dedicated channel sales engineer, but this is still a technical role, and you should be able to have these conversations whether your SE is in the room or not

• CMMC and 800-171: Walk a partner through how an unmanaged device moves from CUI Asset to out of scope. Speak to the External Service Provider question, FedRAMP Moderate equivalency under DFARS 7012, and shared responsibility

• Microsoft 365 GCC High: Commercial vs. GCC vs. GCC High, enclave vs. full-tenant migration, and where Hypori shrinks the GCC High footprint

• Endpoint and mobile: MDM, UEM, MAM, mobile threat defense, enterprise browser, VDI, and DaaS. You know where the data rests in each

• Hypori platform: Run a partner enablement session covering architecture, deployment scoping, licensing, and what each accreditation means to a client

• MSP operations: RMM and PSA platforms, per-seat packaging, margin expectations, and multi-tenant administration

• Prior time at an MSP, MSSP, RPO, or C3PAO serving defense contractors

• CMMC CCP or CCA certification

• Military service or Department of War civilian experience

About Us

Compensation: $215,000 – $235,000 on-target earnings (commensurate with experience). Variable compensation is uncapped, with accelerators above 100 percent attainment, and the role includes equity. Targets are based on partner-sourced and partner-influenced revenue, plus partner recruitment and activation.

jobs.title: TreePeople - Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
CHIEF FINANCIAL OFFICER

ABOUT TREEPEOPLE

Born in 1973 from the hopes and dreams of a teenager, TreePeople is now one of the largest environmental organizations headquartered in Southern California. They have inspired, engaged, and supported more than 3 million people to take action for our environment by planting and caring for trees in forests, mountains, parks, and our neighborhoods. Their unique, engaging, and proven model empowers communities to plant a more resilient future and take personal responsibility for greening their neighborhoods. Through their on-the-ground research and educational programs, TreePeople shares knowledge with policymakers, students and educators, and communities around the world. As the world faces increasing threats from a changing climate, TreePeople helps create actionable solutions.

POSITION OVERVIEW

The Chief Financial Officer (CFO) leads TreePeople’s finance and accounting functions and partners with the Chief Executive Officer, Chief Grants and Contracts Officer (CGCO), leadership team, and board to advance financial stability, sustainability, and responsible growth. The CFO combines strategic financial leadership with practical oversight of accounting, budgeting, forecasting, cash flow, grants and contracts, and financial systems.

TreePeople’s project-based work and complex government grants and reimbursable contracts require a seasoned nonprofit leader who anticipates funding needs, strengthens infrastructure, and connects financial decisions to program impact. The CFO will improve cash flow visibility, project budget reporting, billing and collections, and long-term financial planning. This leader will manage and develop the finance team, address audits, and establish clear processes and accountability while building trust across departments through a collaborative, approachable leadership style grounded in TreePeople’s environmental mission.

ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Financial Strategy and Organizational Planning

• Lead short-term and multi-year financial planning aligned with TreePeople’s mission, strategic priorities, and operational needs.

• Partner with the CEO and leadership team to assess financial risks, reserves, funding gaps, and scenarios; recommend practical options that support financial resilience and sustainable growth.

• Evaluate the financial impact and full costs of new programs, partnerships, and expansion opportunities, including administrative costs not fully covered by grants or contracts.

Budgeting, Project Finance and Cash Flow

• Lead annual operating and project budget development with department leaders; establish clear timelines, assumptions, responsibilities, and budget accountability.

• Establish regular monthly budget-to-actual reviews, reconciliations, and updated forecasts with program leaders. Explain variances in operational context and coach staff on financial planning based on completed work and estimates to completion.

• Oversee cash flow forecasting and liquidity management, incorporating project obligations, billing schedules, receivables, reimbursement timing, and operating expenses.

• Obtain timely project information across departments to identify cash needs and funding gaps early; recommend actions and monitor progress.

• Coordinate with development to align fundraising priorities and restricted funding with program needs and the organization’s broader financial outlook.

Grants, Contracts and Funding Compliance

• Oversee financial management of a substantial portfolio of government contracts and federal, foundation, and other grants, including restricted and unrestricted funds.

• Partner with grants and program leaders to strengthen award budgeting, allowable cost allocation, financial reporting, documentation, and compliance with funding requirements.

• Improve timely and accurate billing and reimbursement submissions; coordinate collections and funder communication to support receivables management and cash flow.

• Track funding sources and restrictions, monitor contract and grant financial performance, and communicate financial obligations and risks to leadership.

Accounting, Audit and Financial Controls

• Oversee daily finance operations, accurate general ledger records, timely monthly closes, fixed assets, depreciation, and reliable monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reports.

• Ensure financial operations comply with GAAP and applicable local, state, and federal requirements; stay current on changes affecting the organization.

• Maintain effective internal controls, documented accounting policies, and standard operating procedures; conduct periodic internal reviews.

• Coordinate annual audits and timely audited financial statements; present results to the finance committee and board, and lead corrective actions to address findings and prevent recurrence.

• Oversee preparation and timely filing of IRS Form 990 and other required financial filings.

Financial Systems, Reporting and Data Access

• Assess and improve the use of Sage Intacct and related tools to strengthen reporting, forecasting, and access to dependable financial data.

• Partner across departments to improve data coordination and appropriate integration among Sage Intacct, ADP, and Salesforce, reducing duplicate entry and manual reconciliation.

• Develop accessible project dashboards and timely budget-to-actual reporting so program leaders can obtain useful financial information with less manual support.

• Establish clear data ownership, reporting standards, and review practices; provide training and support for effective system use.

• Establish meaningful key financial and performance metrics to support management decision-making.

Finance Team, Leadership and Cross-Department Collaboration

• Lead, develop, and support the finance team through clear expectations, coaching, professional development, knowledge sharing, and effective onboarding.

• Assess staffing capacity and workloads, including billing support, and recommend resources and practices that promote continuity and staff retention.

• Build trust across finance, programs, development, grants and contracts, and other departments; clarify responsibilities, resolve misunderstandings constructively, and promote respectful communication and shared accountability.

• Introduce processes and accountability with staff input, clear explanations, and a manageable implementation pace that respects TreePeople’s participatory culture.

• Create consistent service and communication standards so the finance team provides approachable, direct support across the organization, including in remote or hybrid working environments.

CEO & Board Partnership

• Serve as a trusted financial advisor to the CEO and represent finance at Board and finance committee meetings.

• Present financial results as a clear narrative linking variances, program performance, cash needs, risks, and recommended actions for audiences with varied financial knowledge.

• Provide candid, timely financial communication to leadership and appropriate visibility for staff; translate board priorities into practical next steps.

• Support clear boundaries between Board governance and daily operations while navigating differing perspectives with sound judgment and professionalism.

• Other duties as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS

• A minimum of ten years of accounting or finance experience in the nonprofit sector with organizations generating at least $10 million in revenue, including at least five years of senior leadership.

• Demonstrated CFO-level leadership of a complex nonprofit finance function, including strategic planning, executive advising, board reporting, and finance team development.

• Deep experience with government grants and reimbursable contracts, nonprofit fund accounting, restricted and unrestricted funds, and a high volume of concurrent awards and reporting obligations.

• Strong command of GAAP, audit oversight, internal controls, regulatory compliance, tax filing oversight, and corrective action implementation.

• Demonstrated success in annual and multi-year budgeting, project-level analysis, cash flow forecasting, liquidity management, and scenario planning.

• Experience strengthening financial infrastructure during organizational growth, documenting processes, improving systems, and guiding collaborative change.

• Advanced proficiency with financial systems and analytical tools, including Sage Intacct and Excel; ability to improve reporting and coordinate data across systems.

• An approachable and empathetic leadership style, strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to remain calm and exercise sound judgment under pressure.

• Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills, including the ability to explain complex financial information clearly to staff, executives, and board members.

• A strong commitment to TreePeople’s environmental mission and a willingness to understand its programs and field-based work.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

The CFO salary range is $180,000 - $200,000. TreePeople offers medical coverage with fully paid employee premiums for select plans; optional dental, vision, and supplemental insurance; employer-paid life insurance and employee assistance; flexible spending accounts; and a retirement plan. Paid time off includes two to four weeks of vacation based on tenure, 96 hours of annual sick leave for full-time employees, 12 holidays, a floating holiday, and winter closure from December 26–31.

TreePeople is an Equal Opportunity Employer, committed to fostering diversity and inclusion. TreePeople promotes equal opportunity for all employees and applicants. In doing so, we comply with local, state, and federal laws and regulations to ensure an equal employment opportunity for everyone. We don’t discriminate in employment opportunities or practices on the basis of race, ancestry, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, national origin, age, disability, citizenship, military service obligation, veteran status or any other basis protected by federal, state or local laws. Our policies and personnel practices are intended to ensure that all of us are treated equally with regard to recruiting, hiring, and advancement, and our decisions on employment are made to further the principle of equal employment opportunities for employees.

jobs.title: Vice President, Engineering
jobs.description:
At Submittable, we are transforming how organizations create social impact. Our platform empowers thousands of mission-driven organizations, from nonprofits to government entities, to make a difference in their communities and beyond. In 2024, our innovative software helped organizations worldwide run 30,000 programs, welcomed 1.2 million applicants, and facilitated the distribution of more than $10 billion in funding through our products on behalf of our clients.

We are on a mission to help organizations accelerate their impact, so we are proud to partner with organizations focused on Equity & Social Justice, Children & Education, Creative & Arts, Health & Wellness, Economic Justice & Opportunity, and Environment & Climate. At Submittable, technology and purpose converge, offering a unique opportunity to contribute to meaningful change.

About the Role

Submittable is hiring a Vice President of Engineering who is deeply technical, works hands-on, and builds with AI every day. You will report to the CTO and run engineering day to day: delivery, quality, reliability, cost, and the people who make them happen.

We want a different VP than the old SaaS playbook produced. That playbook grew output by growing headcount and adding layers of management. We believe AI coding tools now let a small team of strong engineers ship what once took a team several times its size. We intend to run engineering that way. You will keep the organization lean, keep layers few, and raise output per engineer rather than the number of engineers.

You cannot lead that change from a slide deck. You need to know firsthand what it is like to ship production software with AI agents, including where they fail. We expect you to have done this yourself in the last 12 months and to keep doing it here. Plan on roughly a fifth of your week going to hands-on technical work: reading and writing code, reviewing pull requests, working incidents, and building the tools your teams use.

We are choosing depth over span. This is a hands-on leadership role for a small, senior team, not a role leading a large organization through layers of managers. If you want to make architecture calls, contribute and ship code, and help a lean team deliver well beyond its size, we want to talk.

What You'll Do

• Run engineering day to day. Turn the CTO's technical strategy and the product roadmap into plans, priorities, and shipped software.

• Stay hands-on. Review pull requests, prototype, debug production issues, and write tools. You should be able to pick up a ticket and ship it. Teams should trust your calls because of your technical judgment, not your title.

• Make AI the default way we build. Expect every engineer to work with AI coding agents (tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot) for design, coding, testing, and review. Show people how by doing it yourself, and remove whatever stops them.

• Measure what AI changes. Track the four DORA metrics (how often we deploy, how long a change takes to reach production, how often changes fail, and how fast we recover), plus defects that reach customers and engineering cost per release. Report plainly on where AI helps and where it creates new problems, such as oversized pull requests, thinner review, or code no one on the team understands.

• Keep the organization lean. Grow output faster than headcount. Keep management layers thin, expect managers to stay technical, and favor small teams with clear ownership over large teams that need heavy coordination. Before adding a person, ask whether better tooling or automation solves the problem.

• Automate the toil. Use AI and automation for test generation, CI/CD checks, code review assistance, release notes, incident triage, and alerting, so engineers spend their time on the product.

• Raise the technical bar. Set standards for architecture, code review, testing, CI/CD, release management, and incident response. Shipping more code, faster, raises the stakes for review, testing, and observability. Make sure speed does not cost us quality.

• Own platform reliability, security, and cost. Our products are multi-tenant SaaS running on AWS and Azure, with Kubernetes. Work with infrastructure and security partners to meet uptime targets, pass SOC 2 audits, and keep cloud spend growing slower than revenue. Simplify our architecture where consolidation pays for itself.

• Build AI into the product. Work with the CTO and Product to add AI to Submittable so customers can set up programs, review applications, and make funding decisions in less time. Help decide what to build and how to test it for accuracy and fairness, because real applicants' outcomes depend on it.

• Hire and grow a small, strong team. Recruit engineers and leaders who already build with AI. Coach managers to stay close to the work. Build career paths that reward impact and technical depth, not team size.

• Partner across the company. Work with Product and Design on scope and trade-offs among new features, technical debt, and platform health. Work with Customer Experience and Support to resolve escalations and reduce customer-facing defects.

What We're Looking For

• You have shipped software with AI in the last 12 months. You personally built and shipped production code using AI coding tools within the past year. You can tell us what you built, which tools you used, what broke, and how it changed the way you work. This is a requirement, not a preference.

• Deep technical skill. 15+ years in software engineering, with real depth in distributed systems, API design, data modeling, cloud infrastructure (AWS and Azure, Kubernetes), and DevOps. You can hold your own in an architecture review with our strongest engineers and spot the flaw in a design or a pull request.

• You have run lean, high-output teams. 7+ years in engineering leadership, including at least 3 years leading other managers. You have raised a team's output without matching growth in headcount, and you can show the numbers: delivery metrics, team size, and cost, before and after.

• B2B SaaS at scale. Experience building and running multi-tenant, cloud-based B2B SaaS products. Experience consolidating platforms or integrating acquired products is a plus.

• Predictable delivery. A record of shipping complex software on predictable timelines without trading away quality, security, or reliability.

• Distributed teams. You have led teams across multiple countries and time zones, including offshore or nearshore partners. You write clearly, because much of this work happens in writing.

• Comfort with fast change. The norms for building software now shift every few months. You form a view, test it, and change your mind when the evidence says so.

• A clear storyteller. You can explain technical trade-offs to executives and non-technical colleagues in plain language. You tell people where engineering is going and why, often enough that they repeat it.

• A builder of strong teams. A track record of hiring, developing, and keeping strong engineers and building inclusive teams.

• Nice to Have: Experience in a private equity-backed or high-growth SaaS company; familiarity with SOC 2 and GDPR; experience shipping LLM-based features to customers, including how to evaluate them.

• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

Location: This is a remote, U.S.-based role — you must live and reside in the U.S. full-time.

Salary Details: The annual salary range for this position is $220,000 - $260,000. Actual compensation is based on factors such as the candidate's skills, qualifications, and experience. We also have a location-based compensation structure; there may be a different range for candidates in other locations.

We are interested in every qualified candidate eligible to work in the United States; however, we cannot accommodate scholastic or employment visas at this time. In addition, we are not able to consider applicants who reside in the following states: Alaska, Delaware, Hawaii, Louisiana, Maine, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oklahoma, Rhode Island, Vermont, Washington, West Virginia, and Wyoming.

Fraudulent Recruitment Advisory: Submittable will NEVER request bank details, payment, or personal information during the hiring process, nor extend offers without an interview. All legitimate communications come from official submittable.com email addresses. If you receive suspicious outreach, please report it to people@submittable.com. (Please do not submit applications, resumes, cover letters, or other candidacy materials to this email address. Emails of this nature will not be reviewed or considered.)

Why Submittable?

Joining Submittable means becoming part of a forward-thinking, mission-driven company that values innovation, collaboration, and growth. We empower organizations working for social good with technology that accelerates their work, amplifies their impact, and drives meaningful change.

At Submittable, you’ll find a supportive, dynamic work environment where your contributions directly influence our success. If you thrive in a fast-paced, evolving environment and are excited to be part of a company dedicated to social impact, we invite you to apply!

Benefits: We are proud to offer highly competitive benefits to our full-time employees, including:

• Comprehensive health and life insurance with optional HSA, FSA, and DCA accounts

• 401(k) plan with employer match starting day one

• Equity stock options to share in our success

• Flexible hours, remote work options, and generous vacation and sick leave

• Paid parental leave for mothers, fathers, and adoptive parents

• Professional development stipends to support your career growth

• Opportunities to participate in community outreach and volunteer programs

• Monthly company-sponsored happy hours and gatherings to connect and unwind

Our Commitment to Inclusion & Belonging

At Submittable, we believe technology is a force for good, driving social impact and enabling corporate social responsibility on a global scale. To achieve this, we are committed to fostering a workplace that values inclusion and belonging as central pillars of our culture.

We embrace the strength of our diverse community by creating a safe space where employees feel empowered to share ideas, celebrate unique experiences, and learn from one another. By prioritizing inclusion, we aim to build an environment where everyone can bring their authentic selves to work and make innovative contributions that enable our customers to tackle complex challenges and spread more good.

As a globally used platform, we are dedicated to hiring and supporting employees who represent a range of backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. This includes diversity in ethnicity, sexual orientation, gender, religion, ability, culture, and socioeconomic background.

About Our Process

Our goal is a fair, efficient, and thorough evaluation process that benefits you and our team and respects your time. As you can imagine, we have received a high volume of applications. Your willingness to participate in I.D. Verification and answer a few questions early allows us to move through the process more quickly.

Let's Talk About AI:

Guidelines for using AI in our Hiring Process: At Submittable, we believe that Artificial Intelligence (AI) can be a powerful tool for good. We are committed to leveraging AI technologies responsibly, ensuring their use is equitable, fair and safe. To ensure fairness and accurate skill assessment, we do not allow the use of AI tools (including note takers, transcription tools, or recordings) during take home tests or interviews. If you have questions or need accommodations, please let us know.

For additional information and guidance on using AI to prepare an interview at Submittable, please click here.

We believe our approach streamlines the hiring process and respects your time by ensuring that every conversation is substantive and focused on your unique qualifications. We appreciate your cooperation and look forward to learning more about you.

About Engine

Engine is the AI-native platform for intelligent travel. For a decade, Engine has built the proprietary technology and supply behind modern business travel, serving over 40,000 customers and nearly 2 million travelers, along with leading travel and AI companies that build on Engine's infrastructure. One system powers business travel, group travel, human agents, and AI agents.

That work has earned Engine recognition as TravelTech's Reservation Platform of the Year (2026), a spot on Inc.'s Power Partners list (2026), and one of Built In's Best Places to Work (2020–2026).

We're looking for bold, ambitious people to help redefine how businesses manage and experience travel. Working here, you can expect exponential growth, an ambitious pace, full ownership, and high-caliber colleagues who push you to do the best work of your career. Every hire raises the bar.

Come outpace the ordinary and build the future of travel with us.

Your Mission

As part of the Engine team, you'll play a vital role in an environment where innovation meets collaboration. Here's what you'll take charge of:

• Implementation Strategy for New Customer Rollouts: Craft and execute the implementation strategy for Engine's most important new customer opportunities (deals ranging from $200K to $1M), setting the foundation for lasting partnerships and driving adoption across Engine's full product suite in a customer's first months on the platform.

• Cross-Functional Partnership: Collaborate with Sales and Account Management to deliver a seamless experience from signed contract to first booking, and feed implementation blockers and patterns from the field back to Product and Engineering to sharpen the motion.

• Team Leadership and Scalable Process: Lead a team of Implementation Managers through live deployments, run workload and milestone reviews, coach to the motion, and build processes that scale efficiently as new customer volume grows.

• Senior Implementation Voice: Serve as the senior implementation voice on Engine's most important new customer opportunities, leading key customer meetings, delivering training, and ensuring every interaction with Engine exceeds expectations through a clean handoff to the dedicated Account Manager.

What You'll Bring to Engine

We're looking for someone who's ready to make an impact and grow alongside us:

• Experience: 4+ years of hands-on experience in implementation, customer success, account management, or technical program management at a B2B SaaS, travel, or fintech platform, including 1+ year leading a team or formally mentoring ICs.

• Skills: You've owned customer onboarding and implementation end to end, translating customer requirements into tailored rollout plans that drive adoption across a full product suite, and you're comfortable being the senior customer-facing voice on a deal.

• Tech-Savvy: Fluent in the mechanics of customer onboarding at scale: configuration and rollout planning, mutual success plans, adoption benchmarks, and GTM handoffs across Sales, AM, and support. Comfortable holding a team to a high customer-engagement cadence (roughly 15 customer meetings per week per IC). Bonus points for experience with corporate travel, expense, or spend management platforms.

• Mindset: You're a problem-solver who anticipates customer needs, removes friction, and builds conviction through consultative conversations, and you thrive in fast-paced environments where the playbook is still being refined. You lead from inside live deployments and deliver results that matter.

Applications for this role will be accepted through February 20, 2027 or until the role is filled. We encourage you to apply early, as we may begin reviewing applications before the deadline.

Compensation
Our compensation packages are based on several factors, including your experience, expertise, and location. In addition to a competitive base salary, all roles receive equity. Depending on the role, total compensation may also include an annual bonus. Your recruiter will share your complete compensation package as you move through the process.

Base Pay Range

$102,000—$140,000 USD

The Engine Edge: Perks & Compensation
We believe in rewarding great work with great benefits:

• Compensation: Competitive base pay tied to role and experience, with equity for all employees. Some roles are also eligible for bonuses or commissions.

• Benefits: Check out our full list at engine.com/culture

• Environments for Success: Different roles have different needs in terms of the environments that drive success which is why we have a hybrid-hub model. Whether you are in one of our amazing offices or fully remote, we'll make sure you have what you need to succeed.

jobs.title: Senior Auditor – Business & IT Operations
jobs.description:
Role and team:

We are looking for an experienced Senior Auditor to support planning and lead execution of global and/or regional operational and integrated audits spanning business operational controls, IT general controls and application controls. This remote position will be reporting to Director, Internal Audit Management. You’ll also help build the next version of Internal Audit by designing AI-enabled tools and automations that change how audits get done, not just using the tools others hand you.

We have a tight team environment where support, loyalty, and honest feedback are the currency. ServiceNow employees are expected to be self-starting, proactive, and thrive in a fast-paced environment.

What you get to do in this role:

• Support planning and scoping of operational and integrated audits across business and IT operations. Complete assignments efficiently and timely.
• Conduct walkthroughs, evaluate process design, and perform controls testing across both business processes and IT systems, consistently delivering quality audit work papers that support and substantiate audit observations.
• Identify manual or repetitive steps in the audit lifecycle and build AI-enabled solutions to automate them, such as prompt workflows, AI agents, scripts, or data pipelines for evidence gathering, testing, and workpaper drafting.
• Use data analytics and AI to test full populations when possible, identify control gaps, quantify risk exposure, and deliver data-driven insights to management.
• Document and share what you build so the team can reuse it, and help shape Internal Audit’s AI playbook.
• Assist in producing high-quality Internal Audit reports by clearly drafting audit issues and developing valid conclusions resulting in process and internal control improvements, while considering implementation requirements, cost, and stakeholder feedback.
• Timely and effective communication with audit leads on audit status, escalations, issues, and reporting.
• Perform action tracking follow-up with management for Audit Committee reporting purposes.
• Participate in major business initiatives and proactively advise and assist the business on key risks, control environment, and change initiatives.
• Contribute to the evolution of Internal Audit methodology, automation, and reporting, including ServiceNow IRM to scale audit coverage and quality.
• Responsible for internal stakeholder engagement, including the development of working relationships with key stakeholders and proudly representing the Internal Audit function.

To be successful in this role, you have:

• A passion for Internal Audit and strong desire to be part of a stellar IA team!
• Minimum 4-year degree (or US equivalent) from an accredited university; degree in Management Information Systems, Finance and Accounting strongly preferred.
• Minimum of 5 years’ work experience, with 3 years at a public accounting firm (Big 4 or national consulting firm preferred), including experience in internal auditing, external auditing, SOX, operations and process improvement.
• Demonstrated experience auditing both IT general controls and application controls, and business operational processes. Comfort moving fluidly between technology and business-process audits, including within the same integrated engagement.
• Understanding of data governance and privacy compliance, and the ability to apply system architecture knowledge to the processes being reviewed.
• Understanding of risks and controls in modern technology environments. Awareness of AI/GenAI governance and model risk considerations.
• Builder track record: you’ve built something, such as a tool, automation, script, or AI workflow, that solved a real problem in your work. Be ready to walk us through it.
• Hands-on experience with generative AI tools (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot) beyond basic chat, such as building custom prompts, agents, or automated workflows.
• Good understanding of business and operations, strong analytical and project management skills.
• Proficiency in Excel and process mapping tools. Hands-on experience with data analytics tools such as Power BI. Experience with SAP preferred.
• Strong critical thinking and analytical skills; ability to identify and conduct root cause analysis.
• Excellent verbal, written, oral communication and presentation skills.
• Ability to work both independently and as a team member.
• Ability to manage multiple tasks concurrently, efficiently and effectively with minimal oversight.
• Familiarity with the ServiceNow platform, including IRM modules, a strong plus
• (Preferred) At least one of the following certifications: CISA, CISM, CIA, CPA
• Prefer candidates with exposure to a high growth and/or rapidly changing technology enterprise.

jobs.title: Software Engineer III
jobs.description:
Who we are

We're on a mission to bring joy to the business of events. Weddings, galas, festivals... the moments that people remember the most are put on by dozens of small businesses working together behind the scenes to bring that experience to life. These businesses have historically run off of software that doesn't meet their needs, spreadsheets, or even memory.

Goodshuffle Pro runs the end-to-end operations of event rental companies — invoicing, payment processing, inventory management, and the logistics of getting a warehouse worth of equipment to a venue and back at precisely the right time. Rental companies are one piece of everything that goes into an event, and we're changing how the whole industry operates together.

Some of us are event nerds, some of us are tech nerds, and some of us are both — but all of us are passionate problem-solvers who care about helping our users succeed. Our values describe how we work:

Sincerely Care — about yourself, about your team, about your work.

Speak Up — liberally share knowledge, seek to solve, recognize and appreciate.

Learn from Everything — listen intently, stay curious. Don't fear failure; fear not learning.

Show Up — come prepared, execute diligently, honor accountability.

What you'll do

You’ll be focused on building technology that powers the events industry, and you’ll own the full lifecycle of your work. Your primary focuses will be to:

Build products that people love using. You will get to know the people you're building for. This involves running discovery calls every week, visiting warehouses to see how our customers run their day-to-day, and uncovering the pain that we can solve. You will take problems and own the right way to solve them, instrument and measure the outcome of your work, and propose iterations for the product roadmap.

Own the end-to-end build. You will work directly with our founders, Design, Customer Experience, and GTM to shape requirements and navigate ambiguity on your projects. The events industry is fast-paced, detailed, and has little tolerance for mistakes; precision and architecting for scale are key. You’ll manage complex data modeling, migrations, distributed system design, and intuitive UX.

Build systems our customers rely on. You will support production systems with the rest of the Engineering team, ensuring that reliability is always our #1 priority. This requires a deep understanding of how our systems, infrastructure, and integrations work. You’ll find ways to automate routine tasks, freeing up more time for the team to focus on innovative work. When something breaks, you trace down the root cause and fix it at the core, ensuring it doesn’t continue happening.

Operate with an AI-first mentality. You will work alongside a company of builders who are passionate about technology and delivering value. AI is changing daily, and we are changing just as fast. You should be someone who keeps up with the latest and greatest in tech, and brings new opportunities back to your team. AI is not just accelerating development, but every aspect of what we do – everything from product discovery to evaluating success.

Who you are

You care about the details. You write requirements carefully, think through edge cases, and mitigate risk for everything you do. Our customers rely on our products to run their businesses, and getting it right is important to you.

You approach your work with curiosity. Your first instinct is to ask questions to learn more. You understand different perspectives, the importance of context, and nuance. Your friends describe you as empathetic and someone who seeks to solve problems.

You balance organizational rigor and adaptability. You track your commitments, close open threads, keep documentation current, and flag when things start to slip. When your priorities shift, you adjust plans and keep moving forward, ensuring all relevant parties are aware of the shift. You explain your work clearly to non-engineers, and your manager doesn’t have to consistently follow up with you.

You think in systems. You approach problems, both product and process, by understanding how systems interact and influence one another, rather than looking at a single piece of the puzzle.

Qualifications

Must-Haves

• 4+ years experience as a Software Engineer

• A Computer Science degree

• Experience shipping products that people use in their daily lives

• Experience building distributed systems

• Excitement and energy from how fast the field is moving with AI

Strong Preference for Experience with:

• Building SaaS products, especially for small businesses

• Building FinTech products

• Grails or Java/Spring

• Angular or React

• RDBMS

Benefits

• Base salary: $150,000 – $190,000

• Full Health Care (including Dental, Vision, HSA, FSA, LTD, AD&D)

• Unlimited PTO

• 401k (with matching)

• Commuter Benefits ($100/mo)

• WFH Flexibility (hybrid, 3 days in-office)

• Passionate, caring, and enthusiastic coworkers (We've been called one of DC's best places to work!)

To Apply

If you'd like to join us, we recommend reviewing our website and our company values, then applying on our website. We encourage applicants of every race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status and are committed to an environment of equity and inclusion.

jobs.title: Solution Architect, Legal Billing
jobs.description:
About Us

At Litify, we're powering a new era for the legal industry. Since its founding in 2016, Litify has helped law firms and corporate legal departments turn operations into impact through its leading AI-native Platform of Action.

Over 55K legal professionals and 450+ enterprise clients across plaintiff, insurance defense, immigration, and the Fortune 500 trust Litify to combine cloud-based technology, configurable AI-native workflows, agentic AI, and powerful business analytics into one open ecosystem that moves legal teams from systems of record to systems of action.

Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and recognized as an Inc. 5000 and Deloitte Technology Fast 500 fastest-growing private company, Litify is at the center of legal innovation. Headquartered in New York, we're building the last legal platform our customers will ever need.

About the Role

The Solution Architect, Legal Billing is a member of Litify Professional Services who leads the time, billing, and financial side of client implementations. You bring a formal accounting background and software implementation skills to design and deliver time entry, expense tracking, billing, and collections workflows for law firms on the Litify platform. You work directly with firm billing teams, finance staff, and partners. You learn how they capture time and costs and turn them into paid invoices today, then translate that into a sound Litify design and own it through go-live.

You will:

• Lead discovery with firm billing and finance teams to map how they capture time and expenses, review pre-bills, issue invoices, and collect payment.

• Design billing setups on Litify and Salesforce: timekeeper and client-matter rates, rate hierarchies and overrides, fee arrangements (hourly, flat fee, contingency, and hybrid), and invoice templates.

• Configure time and expense capture, including activity and task codes, hard and soft costs, cost recovery, and markups.

• Build pre-bill review and approval workflows, including write-ups, write-downs, and billing adjustments.

• Set up e-billing for clients that require it, including LEDES file formats, UTBMS codes, and outside counsel billing guidelines.

• Design AR and collections processes, including payments, retainers, applying trust funds to invoices, and client statements.

• Deliver billing and financial reporting: WIP, realization, timekeeper utilization, aged AR, and collections.

• Plan and support migration of open WIP, unbilled costs, and AR balances from legacy billing systems, with reconciliation to the source.

• Configure and test the solution, working with Litify developers and other Solution Architects where custom build is needed.

• Run workshops, UAT, training, and go-live support with client billing, finance, and operations staff.

• Keep project status, risks, and documentation current.

• Feed field learnings back to Product and Professional Services to improve the billing offering.

You have (required):

Listed in priority order.

• Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field; CPA license or CPA-eligible status preferred

• Legal billing experience: 3+ years of hands-on work in law firm billing or finance, or at a legal time and billing software company, with working knowledge of all of the following: time and expense entry, rate management, fee arrangements, pre-bill review and adjustments, invoicing, LEDES and UTBMS e-billing, client billing guidelines, AR and collections, WIP and realization reporting, and trust accounting basics.

• Software implementation and technical experience: 3+ years implementing or consulting on time, billing, or financial software. Covers discovery, requirements, configuration, data migration of WIP, unbilled time and costs, and AR, UAT, and go-live. Comfortable with SQL or ETL tools for loading and validating financial data, and with how systems integrate.

• Client delivery: runs workshops with firm billing teams, finance staff, and partners, presents clearly to executives, and manages several projects at once.

You have (nice-to-have):

• Salesforce experience: implementation or admin work on Salesforce; Salesforce Administrator certification.

• Accounting Seed or Certinia (formerly FinancialForce): a major plus. Hands-on implementation of a Salesforce-native accounting or billing product.

• Experience implementing or supporting legal time and billing systems such as Elite 3E, Aderant, Centerbase, or Juris.

• Experience with e-billing platforms such as Legal Tracker, TyMetrix 360, or BillBlast.

• Experience with Litify or another legal practice management platform.

Disclosure:

This job is fully remote, with the exception of employees living in New York City and New Jersey. Our NYC/NJ employees adhere to our hybrid schedule, which involves working in our Manhattan office 6 days a month.

The estimated base salary for this role is $130-145k. You may also be offered a bonus and benefits.

Our salary ranges are based on paying competitively for our size and industry, and are one part of many compensation, benefits and other reward opportunities we provide.

Individual pay rate decisions are based on a number of factors, including qualifications for the role, experience level, skill set, and balancing internal equity relative to peers at the company.

Key Responsibilities Include:

Creative Project Management

• Collaborate with the Managing Director, Brand and Creative to build and maintain clear project briefs, leveraging AI and other tools to make creative workflows more efficient.

• Support project management across communications and creative projects, including developing timelines, tracking deliverables, and keeping projects moving toward completion.

• Coordinate logistics and schedules for photo and video shoots.

• Develop clear briefing materials for creative vendors, including photographers, videographers, designers, and other production partners.

• Maintain Elemental’s photo asset management system in Canto, ensuring assets are organized, searchable, and accessible to the team.

• Build and maintain a centralized video asset management system.

• Help improve the systems, tools, and processes the team uses to manage creative projects and assets.

• Maintain and update Elemental’s website, including publishing blog posts, updating page copy and images using our content management system, and liaising with Elemental’s technical website team as needed.

Visual Communications

• Independently create polished visuals leveraging Elemental’s existing brand system and creative templates, including presentation decks, social graphics, simple videos, and other digital assets.

• Partner with Elemental’s Senior Designer and Communications team to translate ideas and information into clear, compelling visual content.

Owned events

• Support Elemental’s Events Director in developing and maintaining event project briefs, production timelines, and planning materials.

• Curate, organize, and maintain audience and invitation lists for Elemental events.

• Track event registration and guest logistics, including RSVPs, waitlists, rooming lists, and other attendee information.

• Support event production and coordination leading up to Elemental’s owned events.

About you

You are equal parts organizer and creative thinker. You like making complex projects feel manageable and take pride in the details that make creative work excellent. You can keep a project tracker organized one moment and jump into a presentation or social graphic the next.

You’re naturally curious about visual storytelling and emerging creative tools. You don’t need to be a specialist designer, photographer, or videographer, but you have a strong visual eye and a desire to learn about what makes creative work clear, engaging, and on-brand.

You thrive in collaborative, fast-moving environments and are comfortable juggling multiple projects, deadlines, and stakeholders without losing sight of the details.

Qualifications

Foundational skills & experience:

• Mission alignment – energized by Elemental’s mission and values and want to apply your creative and operational skills to the work

• Creative production experience – professional experience in creative project management, production, digital media or marketing, brand development, or a related field

• Project management – ability to manage timelines, deliverables, details, and stakeholders across multiple concurrent projects

• Detail orientation – a track record of producing accurate, polished work and keeping complex information organized

• Visual fluency – experience creating or producing visual communications, with a strong eye for design and storytelling

• Digital savvy – comfort working across websites, digital asset management systems, presentation and design tools, and other digital platforms

What Will Set You Apart

• Creative curiosity – generate ideas, explore possibilities, and look for ways to make the work better rather than simply executing what already exists.

• AI fluency – excited to experiment with AI and emerging tools to improve creative development, project management, and production workflows.

• Design instincts – hands-on experience with tools such as Canva, Adobe Creative Suite, Figma, or similar platforms.

Compensation & Benefits

This is a full-time "at-will" position working at least 40 hours per week. You may be asked to travel for work periodically. The salary for this role is $86,900 - $117,500 which is based on market data and the organization's compensation philosophy. Our offer will be within the range as required by certain state laws and individual salary offers will vary within the range depending on relevant education, knowledge, skills, and experience. We also offer comprehensive employee benefits, including a professional development stipend and three weeks paid time off.

Location

We strongly prefer candidates located near one of our headquarters: Honolulu, San Francisco, and New York. Elemental has a hybrid working model and if you are within a reasonable distance to one of our offices in New York, Bay Area, or Honolulu, we ask employees to come into the office at least once a week. Currently, most people come in two times a week to build community with team members.

Other Application Details

Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment Visa.

We will accept and review applications on a rolling basis. Although all applications will be considered, we may be unable to respond to all inquiries. Please note that we do read cover letters, so we advise spending time on them to share your relevant stories and experiences with us. We ask that you keep the cover letter to 1-2 pages long.

Elemental is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. Elemental is also committed to providing access and reasonable accommodation in its services, activities, programs, and employment opportunities in accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act and other applicable laws.

jobs.title: Senior Research Infrastructure Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT HUD

HUD https://www.hud.ai/'s mission is to build reliable, fair and open infrastructure for AI data. We want data to be valuable for the people who create it and trustworthy for the labs that train on it. Our team is a quickly growing group of researchers, engineers and operators building the economy that shapes what AI will become. Backed by $16M from top VCs and YC (W25), our marketplace and platform are used by startups, Fortune 500 companies and frontier labs.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a Senior Research Infrastructure Engineer to accelerate research on training and evaluating frontier AI agents. You’ll build the software and infrastructure that enable HUD’s researchers to iterate on environments, collect trajectories, and evaluate model behavior.

You’ll work closely with research engineers to understand the questions they’re investigating, identify bottlenecks in experimentation, and turn research code into reliable, reusable systems. You’ll own the tools, pipelines, and execution infrastructure that help researchers explore ideas, reproduce results, and scale promising approaches.


RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Build infrastructure that supports research on agent behavior through reliable environment execution, trajectory collection, and evaluation at scale

 - Develop reusable tools, APIs, and pipelines that let researchers launch experiments, manage datasets and configurations, and inspect trajectories and evaluation results

 - Turn research prototypes and experimental workflows into tested, documented software that researchers can reuse and extend

 - Design experiments to understand model behavior, agent failure modes, and data quality issues

 - Make experimentation faster, more reproducible, and more cost-efficient by improving orchestration, observability, and recovery from failed runs

 - Partner with research and engineering to translate evolving research needs into infrastructure priorities and architecture decisions, owning systems from implementation through ongoing operation


EXPERIENCE

You may be a good fit if you have:

 - Strong software engineering fundamentals and proficiency in Python, with a record of building maintainable systems used by others

 - Ownership of backend services, data pipelines, developer tools, or infrastructure from design through deployment and operation

 - Sound judgment about APIs, data models, asynchronous workloads, and the tradeoffs involved in building reliable systems

 - Comfort with Docker, Linux, cloud infrastructure, and debugging failures across application code and the systems it runs on

 - The ability to work closely with researchers, understand experimental workflows, and translate open-ended research needs into useful software

 - Independent technical judgment to set priorities, make pragmatic architecture decisions, and improve systems as their users and workloads grow

Strong candidates may also have:

 - Working knowledge of reinforcement learning, including environments, rollouts, reward signals, and evaluation workflows

 - Experience building research infrastructure, ML pipelines, or tools that made a research team faster

 - Familiarity with distributed job execution, containerized environments, or high-concurrency workloads

 - A track record of improving experiment reproducibility, data lineage, or visibility into complex pipeline failures

We prioritize technical aptitude and learning potential over years of experience. Motivated candidates are encouraged to apply even if they don't meet all criteria.


TEAM & COMPANY DETAILS

 - Team Size: ~25 people currently, mostly full-time in-person, but some remote.

 - Our team: Our team includes 4 International Olympiad medalists (IOI, ILO, IPhO), the former #1 ranked Catan player in the world, serial AI startup founders, and researchers with publications at ICLR, NeurIPS, etc.

 - Company stage: We have 8 figures in funding and are scaling profitably and quickly to meet very strong demand.


LOGISTICS

 - Employment: Full-time.

 - Location: We have offices in San Francisco or Singapore but are open to remote candidates who can work hours that 70-80% overlap with either San Francisco or Singapore time zones.

 - Visa Sponsorship: We provide support for relocation and visas for strong full-time candidates to the US or Singapore.

 - Timeline: Applications are rolling. The process is 2 technical interviews and a 2-3 day work trial.


WHAT WE OFFER

 - Competitive compensation

 - 100% covered top-of-the-line medical, dental, and vision (US and Singapore employees)

 - Lunch and dinner for in-office employees

 - Company-wide holiday break (Christmas Eve to New Year’s Day) on top of PTO and paid holidays

 - 401k with a 4% match

 - Other perks including an Equinox membership and commuter benefits (US employees) and a health/wellness stipend (Singapore employees)

 - Unlimited* access to tokens for ChatGPT, Claude Code, Cursor, etc. *By unlimited, we mean no one on our token usage leaderboard has ever hit a limit. So we have no idea what the limit is.

 - Two top-floor offices in San Francisco’s Union Square and Singapore’s Raffles Place

 - Annual travel budget to visit either office


COMPENSATION

Actual offers are adjusted for experience and location, but our base salary bands are

 - San Francisco (and other major US cities): $175,000 - $260,000

 - Singapore: $130,000 - $195,000

 - Rest of world: $105,000 - $195,000

Due to high volume, we may not actively respond to every application, but feel free to contact us at recruiting@hud.so or elsewhere if we missed your application!

jobs.title: Program Manager
jobs.description:
AST SpaceMobile is building the first and only global cellular broadband network in space to operate directly with standard, unmodified mobile devices based on our extensive IP and patent portfolio and designed for both commercial and government applications. Our engineers and space scientists are on a mission to eliminate the connectivity gaps faced by today’s five billion mobile subscribers and finally bring broadband to the billions who remain unconnected.

Position Overview

We are seeking a Program Manager to join our Telecommunications Program Management Office (PMO) and lead end-to-end service readiness and delivery programs for strategic telecommunications partners. This role is responsible for managing integrated program plans, coordinating cross-functional teams, tracking readiness milestones, and ensuring successful progression through delivery and service launch phases.

The Program Manager will work closely with commercial, technical, engineering, operations, and partner teams to align execution against a single delivery plan, manage dependencies, and drive successful deployment outcomes. The ideal candidate combines strong program management expertise with telecommunications knowledge and a collaborative leadership style.

Key Responsibilities

• Develop and maintain integrated end-to-end program plans supporting service delivery and operational readiness initiatives.

• Track project milestones, dependencies, risks, assumptions, issues, and action items across multiple workstreams.

• Establish and manage program governance, including status reporting, change control, and executive-level communications.

• Coordinate readiness activities, validation efforts, and milestone reviews to support successful service launches.

• Facilitate stage-gate reviews and ensure completion of entry and exit criteria for program progression.

• Monitor readiness metrics, acceptance criteria, and key performance indicators (KPIs), providing visibility to stakeholders.

• Partner with commercial, technical, and operational teams to align delivery activities and strategic objectives.

• Manage cross-functional dependencies and proactively resolve obstacles impacting project timelines.

• Leverage automation and project management platforms to improve delivery efficiency and visibility.

Qualifications

Education
